findings.statement: Cooperative cancellation reaches trampolines through two unrelated channels, and the trampolines in this slice disagree on which one they read. solve_elastic_static_trampoline takes `_cancellation: &CancellationHandle` and ignores it. It reads the thread-local `solver_progress::current_solve_dispatch_context()` instead, which `engine_compute.rs` fills from `Engine::active_solve_cancel`; that is the handle the GUI sets via `set_active_solve_cancel` (gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs). modal_ops (run_modal_analysis, run_mechanism_modal, run_transient_response) polls only the `cancellation` parameter. In production that parameter is a fresh `CancellationHandle::new()` created per dispatch in engine_eval.rs and stored on `ComputeNodeData.running`. The only code that calls `.cancel()` on it is a branch the source itself labels dead ('Until then the branch is dead', engine_eval.rs). So the modal checkpoints poll a handle that production never cancels, and the elastic-static trampoline's signature advertises a parameter it does not honour.
findings.proposal: Pick one channel. Either have the engine pass the active solve cancel handle (or a handle linked to it) as the ComputeFn `cancellation` argument and delete the ambient read in elastic_static, or remove the parameter. Then add one e2e test that cancels through Engine::set_active_solve_cancel and asserts Cancelled from every registered long-running target.

findings.statement: Every compute target decodes the same stdlib structures from `Value` with its own hand-rolled readers, and the failure policy changes from file to file. ElasticMaterial's youngs_modulus/poisson_ratio are read by elastic_static::isotropic_from_data (Result, with Failed naming the argument, but dimension-blind `scalar_si_field`), buckling::extract_material (panic!), modal_ops::extract_isotropic_material (a missing field silently becomes 0.0) and as_printed_material::read_base_elastic (Option). modal_ops::read_scalar_si takes `si_value` from a Scalar of any dimension and maps every non-numeric value to 0.0. It feeds the beam geometry, E and ν, the forcing magnitudes, the time grid, the Rayleigh α/β and the reference direction. The canonical dimension-checked reader, reify_ir::arg_acceptance::accept_arg/accept_field (PRD dimension-checked-readers.md), is used in this slice only at elastic_static's Point3/Vector3 component positions. extract_loss_factor is the one modal reader that fences read_scalar_si off by hand. Fix history shows the closure being done one position at a time: task 7019's dimension gates touched only elastic_static, and d10bad1deb gated only loss_factor in modal.
findings.proposal: Give the shared stdlib input structs (ElasticMaterial, ModalOptions, BucklingOptions, ElasticOptions, load kinds) one typed decoder each, built on arg_acceptance::accept_field and returning a single error type. Have every trampoline map that error to ComputeOutcome::Failed in one place, then delete the per-file readers.

findings.statement: solve_elastic_static_trampoline is one function spanning lines 409-1578 that branches inline on five independent axes. (a) Calling overload (dims / body / field): it is inferred by sniffing positional Value variants ('[1] is GeometryHandle OR Undef AND [2] is a List'), and the body call is then normalised to placeholder 1 m dims, so every dims reader needs its own `!body_path` guard. (b) Shell vs tet route. (c) Material model (iso / aniso / heterogeneous). (d) Adaptive lane (none / uniform / gmsh-localized, with runtime fallback). (e) Realized mesh present or absent. It returns at 11 points and builds the ElasticResult field list twice, once for the shell arm and once for the tet arm. More than half of its lines are comments, including several PERF NOTE blocks addressed to reviewers.
findings.proposal: Make the overload explicit: register the body overload with its own entry point, or pass an overload tag, instead of sniffing Values. Split the trampoline into a decode stage that produces a typed request, a route selection that returns an enum over (shell / tet × adaptive lane), and per-route solvers, each returning a typed result that one ElasticResult builder turns into a Value.

findings.statement: ElasticResult's field schema is hand-spelled at three writer sites (the shell arm and the tet arm of solve_elastic_static_trampoline, and value_from_elastic_result) and one reader site (elastic_result_from_value), on top of persistent_cache::ElasticResult. The Rust writers emit a field the declaration does not have: `warm_started` is written at all three sites, but `structure def ElasticResult` in solver_elastic.ri declares 15 params and no warm_started. docs/legibility/design-invariants.md INV-PD-2 says 'a written-but-undeclared field is itself a finding' and names `reify-audit --pattern PVAC` as its enforcement. No PVAC detector exists anywhere in the repo; it appears only in PRD prose. The hash-identity round-trip tests catch writer-vs-bridge drift, but nothing checks the writers against the .ri declaration.
findings.proposal: Build ElasticResult in one function that takes a typed record, used by both arms and by the cache bridge, and add a test that compares the produced key set against the registry's field_layout for `ElasticResult`. That same test is the missing PVAC check for this type.

findings.statement: The ModalResult field list is hand-spelled in three builders (degenerate_modal_result, inline in run_modal_analysis, mechanism_modal_result_value), and the Mode field list in two (inline in run_modal_analysis, mechanism_mode_value). All three ModalResult builders write `topology`, which `structure def ModalResult` (modal_analysis.ri) does not declare: it has 6 params. The docstrings of degenerate_modal_result and run_modal_analysis still say '6 fields'. mechanism_modal_result_value's doc calls topology 'an undeclared write owned by #7097', so the INV-PD-2 violation is known but enforced by nothing (see the PVAC measurement in finding .4). The module docstring describes the file as the free_vibration trampoline only.
findings.proposal: One `modal_result_value(ModalResultParts)` and one `mode_value(ModeParts)` builder, used by all producers, plus the same field_layout comparison test proposed in .4.

findings.statement: The synthetic Freudenthal cantilever mesher exists twice in production: modal_ops::build_beam_mesh and the `None =>` arm of elastic_static::solve_cantilever_fea. Both have the same node_idx/node_coord closures and the same six-tet table, and the two copies have already drifted. elastic_static clamps nx to NX_MAX = 120 (task #4877, so thin bodies stay below PARALLEL_DOF_THRESHOLD and terminate on the serial path). build_beam_mesh uses `.max(1)` with no upper bound, yet its doc says it 'mirrors solve_cantilever_fea's meshing so the modal mesh matches the validated elastic-static pattern'. The same table is copied again in 5 test or solver-test sites.
findings.proposal: One `synthetic_beam_mesh(length, width, height, grid_override)` in a shared module (or in reify-solver-elastic next to its mesher), called by both. NX_MAX policy then lives in one place.

findings.statement: solve_cantilever_fea is pub(crate) and takes 14 positional parameters, five of them Option or bool knobs (provided_mesh, prior_cg, deterministic, threads, progress, bc_override, grid_override). Its `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` justification still says '10 args'. Three production sites call it, and the in-file test module calls it directly 20 more times, spelling out runs of positional `None`. The output struct CantileverFeaSolve has `#[allow(dead_code)]` because its fields 'are read in #[cfg(test)] code'. Across the two files, 7 dead_code allowances (modal 4, elastic_static 3) plus one #[cfg(test)] function in the production section (extract_pressure_loads) exist only so tests can reach in. multi_case.rs's tests re-copy make_box_tet_volume_mesh because 'those live in that file's private #[cfg(test)] module'.
findings.proposal: A `CantileverSolveRequest` struct with named fields and defaults for the execution and override knobs. Tests drive the trampoline, or a narrow typed solve API, instead of the 14-argument internal.

findings.statement: modal_ops.rs is 12,835 lines: four compute targets (modal::free_vibration, modal::mechanism_modal, modal::transient_response, modal::displacement_at), a face-name Dirichlet realization subsystem (build_dirichlet_bcs, FaceCompany, FaceRealization, DeclaredSupport, face_bound, 'x_min'…'z_max' strings), damping classification, and options readers. Its module doc says 'Compute trampoline for modal::free_vibration'. The in-file test module imports 47 names via `use super::{…}`, 30 of them fully private: policy units such as face_company, face_realization, classify_damping, plan_modal_damping and solve_generalized_eigen are tested by private path, not through a seam. A clean partition exists (see h14_measurements); its one cycle hazard is where the ModalResult builders go.
findings.proposal: Split along the partition in h14_measurements. Give the BC realization a narrow seam (`realize_supports(options, nodes, dims) -> DirichletRealization`) and the damping planner a seam (`plan_modal_damping`), and move their tests onto those seams.

findings.statement: Diagnostic identity in modal_ops is mostly a message-string prefix. 24 distinct mnemonics (E_ModalNoMassMatrix, W_ModalRigidBodyMode, E_MechanismModalNoMass, …) are emitted as the leading text of the message, and only 3 carry a DiagnosticCode. Comments call the prefixes 'consumer grouping keys', and tests match on substrings. In one case the mnemonic contradicts the severity: run_mechanism_modal emits 'I_MechanismModalNModesTruncated' through Diagnostic::warning, so an Info-named diagnostic arrives as a Warning, while I_ModalPinnedFaceRealization correctly uses Diagnostic::info.
findings.proposal: Mint DiagnosticCode variants for the modal family, as was done for ShiftAtEigenvalue/ShiftSkippedModes/ModalOptionUnsupported, and assert on codes. As an immediate mechanical fix, emit I_MechanismModalNModesTruncated via Diagnostic::info, or rename it W_.

findings.statement: Production P2 promotion depends on a module named and documented as test-only. modal_ops::promote_beam_mesh_to_p2 and buckling.rs's solve path call `reify_solver_elastic::assembly::test_support::promote_tets_to_p2`. That module is `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod test_support`, its doc says 'all of these items are only reachable from #[cfg(test)] contexts', and it carries a module-wide `#![allow(dead_code)]`. The name lies about the module's role, and the blanket allowance would hide the item if its production callers changed.
findings.proposal: Move promote_tets_to_p2 to a production module of reify-solver-elastic (e.g. p2_tet or mesher), re-export it, and leave test_support with only fixtures.

findings.statement: PressureLoad.direction (declared `param direction : String = "normal"` in fea_multi_case.ri) is parsed into PressureSpec.direction: String and never read. assemble_box_face_pressures always applies the inward face normal, so an author-supplied non-'normal' direction is dropped silently, with no diagnostic. PressureSpec.face is likewise a String that box_face_plane routes on, and only a tracing::warn (not a Diagnostic) reports unresolvable faces.
findings.proposal: Until directions are honoured, emit a Warning Diagnostic for direction != "normal" and drop the field from PressureSpec, or parse it into an enum and reject unknown values. Surface the unresolvable-face case as a Diagnostic rather than tracing only.

findings.statement: About 46-47% of the production lines in both files are comments. Much of it answers reviewers (tagged 'review #N', 'suggestion N', 'amendment', 'esc-NNNN', 'reviewer_comprehensive', PERF NOTE blocks), and some of it has already drifted from the code. elastic_static's module doc says the solve 'Builds a P1-tet FEA mesh (1×1×6 hex blocks, 6 tets per hex = 36 tets, 28 nodes)', but synthetic_grid_counts gives nx = 60 for the documented L = 1 m, h = 0.1 m smoke case, i.e. 2,160 tets. element_stress_anisotropic is documented as 'Mirrors element_von_mises_anisotropic', a function deleted in 8de74b4c3b that is still named 9 times. solve_cantilever_fea's allow says '10 args' over 14. The module doc also carries a TODO escaped with '// ptodo:allow — permanent design note, no live owner', which bypasses the TODO-citation convention rather than citing a task.
findings.proposal: Move the rationale blocks (determinism and cache contract, PERF NOTEs, field-population contract) into the PRDs they cite, leave one-line pointers, and drop the review-answering prose (it belongs in commit messages). Fix the four measured drifts.

findings.statement: The force-density form-finding input contract has no single home. Each entry point re-implements it inline: form_find_anchored, form_find_anchored_surfaces and form_find_anchored_surfaces_aniso in form_find.rs, plus form_find_free/form_find_free_surfaces in form_find_free.rs. The cable q>0 / strut q<0 sign rule is spelled out as a `match kind { MemberKind::Cable => qi > 0.0, .. }` loop in 6 production places, and MemberKind has no impl. The anchor partition is copied 3 times, the member-force loop 3 times, the cotangent fixed-point loop 2 times (isotropic and aniso, line-identical except the assembler), the surface-stencil scatter 3 times and the line rank-1 scatter 2 times (scatter_line_members vs form_find_free::assemble_force_density_matrix). Three error enums (FormFindError, AnisoFormFindError, FreeFormError) share 5 variant names, and map_ff_error translates between them. Enforcement is not uniform. The anchored kernels range-check surface corners but not member endpoints or anchors, so `is_anchor[a] = true` and `d[(j, j)]` panic on a bad index. Only the reify-eval trampoline's crack_anchors/check_index protects them, while form_find_free::validate_explicit does check member indices. form_find_anchored and the aniso entry have no production caller.
findings.proposal: Validate once into a typed problem value (members, kinds, q, anchors, surfaces, each range-checked at construction) with `MemberKind::admits(q)` as the sign rule's only home. Use one shared input-error enum nested in the per-solver errors. Drive the isotropic and anisotropic loops from one fixed-point driver parameterised by a per-triangle stencil. form_find_anchored becomes the empty-surfaces case.
findings.change_note: weakened: Partly fixed by #7553 (be3dfeb590, 9c06044e10, 31157ed423). It added validate_members and partition_anchors to form_find.rs, so all three anchored entries now range-check member endpoints and anchors (no more panic). The unguarded `is_anchor[a] = true` is down from 3 production sites to 1 (guarded, in partition_anchors). Production copies of the sign rule (`MemberKind::Cable =>`) are down from 6 to 4: form_find.rs:364 plus form_find_free.rs:327, :665 and :1507. Unchanged: the three error enums, map_ff_error (form_find.rs:697), the duplicated iso/aniso fixed-point loops and scatter_line_members vs assemble_force_density_matrix. #8628 is stale in two places: its ratchet baselines (6→1, 3→1) and its BT1 'no panic' premise. The out-of-range case now already returns DimensionMismatch.

findings.statement: Element-level shell primitives (ShellFrame, build_shell_frame, plane_stress_d, KAPPA, membrane_node_pair_block, rotate_blockdiag) live in the assembly-level module shell_assembly.rs. Lower and sibling layers import upward into it, and shell_assembly imports them back, which closes module cycles. elements/degenerate_shell.rs:81 does `use crate::shell_assembly::build_shell_frame` while shell_assembly::degenerate_stiffness_core does a fn-local `use crate::elements::degenerate_shell::{..}`. shell_kinematics.rs:11 does `use crate::shell_assembly::ShellFrame` while shell_assembly calls `crate::shell_kinematics::shell_kinematics`. elements/membrane_cst.rs:22 and geometric_stiffness/membrane.rs:27 also reach into shell_assembly for frame and rotation helpers. The #[cfg(test)] fixture tilted_q_for_shell_tests is likewise hosted in shell_assembly and reached from 6 other modules' tests.
findings.proposal: Move ShellFrame, build_shell_frame, plane_stress_d, KAPPA, mat3_mul, membrane_node_pair_block and rotate_blockdiag into a lower module (e.g. elements/shell_frame.rs) that shell_assembly, elements/* and shell_kinematics all import downward. Move tilted_q_for_shell_tests into a test_support module.

findings.statement: The bubble-condensation numerics are copied between shell_element_stiffness_mitc3_plus and degenerate_stiffness_core, and the copies have diverged. The 2x2 K_BB inverse plus Schur correction block appears twice. Only the degenerate copy has the release-time near-singular guard (`det_bb > 1e-14 * k00*k11`, else zero correction). The MITC3+ copy divides by det_bb unguarded, behind a debug_assert. The flat-kinematics bubble-bending K_BB loop is duplicated verbatim, and the t*D / t^3/12*D scaling block is written 5 times. kappa_g = KAPPA*G and ElementStiffness packing are each written 3 times. The shear-correction factor KAPPA = 5/6 is defined independently in shell_result.rs (stress recovery), and G = E/(2(1+nu)) is inlined 16 times across solver-elastic. degenerate_stiffness_core selects its formulation with two bool flags (use_ans_membrane, use_rotation_bubble) behind three public wrappers.
findings.proposal: Extract the condensation (with its guard), the bubble K_BB integral, and a `scaled(d, s)` helper into shared functions. Put KAPPA and the shear modulus on the constitutive/section type. Replace the two bools with an enum or struct for the membrane and bubble variants.

findings.statement: A compute target is identified by a bare &'static str, and every per-target capability is a separate string-keyed table in a different module. Persistence: PERSISTABLE_TARGETS plus two `match target` codec blocks in compute_persist.rs. Significance: is_opted_in plus a `target == "solver::buckling"` branch in significance_filter.rs. Post-dispatch fold: `target == "shell-extract::extract"` written twice in run_compute_dispatch, once in the persistent-HIT arm and once in the Completed arm. Upstream insertion: `target == "solver::elastic_static"` twice in engine_eval.rs. engine_admin.rs adds a `match node.target.as_str()` classifier. The HIT arm must mirror the Completed arm's per-target hooks by convention only, and a prose NOTE in run_compute_dispatch says so. Commit a148207c93 was exactly that mirror missing: the HIT arm did not replay solver diagnostics.
findings.proposal: Register a per-target descriptor (codec, significance comparator, completion hook, demands) alongside the ComputeFn in ComputeDispatchRegistry. Then run_compute_dispatch and compute_persist consult one typed record, and both completion arms call the same hook.

findings.statement: The reify-solver-elastic integration tests carry the FEA harness as private copies in each file instead of a shared module. kuhn_split_hex_to_six_tets, box_p1_mesh, dirichlet_fix_face, end_face_nodes, distributed_tip_load and dedup_bcs each have 5 copies (analytical_validation, aposteriori_validation, determinism, dwr_boundary_tests, solver_gate_smoke), and gather_u_p1 has 4. aposteriori_validation.rs labels its block 'ported FEA harness helpers (tests/analytical_validation.rs, task 2928)'. The copies have drifted in behaviour: dedup_bcs asserts on conflicting duplicate-DOF values in 3 copies and silently keeps the first in 2 (determinism.rs, solver_gate_smoke.rs). Shared homes already exist and are underused. tests/common/mod.rs (92 lines, tensegrity only) and src/assembly/test_support.rs, whose own header states its purpose as preventing drift between inlined integration-test copies, do not host these helpers. canonical_prism and triplex_topology are redefined, with drift, in 3 tensegrity test files despite living in common/mod.rs.
findings.proposal: Move the FEA harness into tests/common/fea_harness.rs (or into assembly::test_support where the src-side tests also need it), with one dedup_bcs that always checks conflicts. Delete the per-file copies.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: The per-element DOF-layout invariant has no single home and is not enforced uniformly. ElementStiffness exposes `pub n_dofs` and `pub data`, so `data.len() == n_dofs^2` is never checked. Its doc still says 'the DOF index is 3 * node_idx + axis', while shells emit 6 DOFs/node and the global assembly derives the stride per element. AssemblyElement's stride `d_e = k_e.n_dofs / connectivity.len()` is recomputed inline at 3 code sites in global.rs. Only assemble_global_stiffness asserts non-empty connectivity, divisibility and node range. detect_orphan_dofs checks only empty connectivity and node range, behind debug_assert, and has no divisibility check, so a non-divisible element silently truncates d_e there. The validated path panics on the same element.
findings.proposal: Give AssemblyElement a validating constructor and a `dofs_per_node()` accessor that both entry points call. Make ElementStiffness's fields private behind zeros/get/add/from_row_major, and fix its doc to state the stride as n_dofs / n_nodes.
findings.change_note: weakened: Partly fixed by #8373: one private dofs_per_node() at global.rs:63. Still true: AssemblyElement and ElementStiffness have pub fields. detect_orphan_dofs checks only under debug_assert! (global.rs:217-228) and has no divisibility check, while assemble_stiffness asserts all three in release. The ElementStiffness doc at assembly/mod.rs:118 still says '3 · node_idx + axis'. There are 72 `.data[` sites across 14 src files. Owned by #8619/#8621.

findings.statement: Rationale pointers in this slice point at places a reader cannot reach. 14 comments in 9 reify-solver-elastic src files send the reader to `plan.json` design_decisions, but the repo tracks no plan.json at all. Examples: eigensolve's 'See plan.json design_decisions entries', shell_assembly's KAPPA 'See design decision in plan.json', form_find's 'ε plan.json D1'. 34 comments in reify-solver-elastic carry file:line pointers, and the ones checked are stale. form_find.rs AnisoFormFindError cites compute_targets/form_find.rs:308 (the match is now at 328). shell_benchmarks.rs cites shell_assembly.rs:1104 (the fn is now at 1254). engine_compute.rs says 'per the NOTE at line 407' (the NOTE is now ~537). Production prose is the majority of the code in engine_compute.rs (65%), assembly/global.rs (64%), eigensolve.rs (60%) and degenerate_shell.rs (54%). Some of it is reviewer-answering history that the Comments stance homes in commit or task records: 'a claim this comment made until task 5311, and which was false', 'An earlier draft of this list also named concurrent.rs', eigensolve's measured tables, debug-perf before/after (task 4055) and '478 tests pass'.
findings.proposal: Rehome the plan.json rationale that must persist into the cited PRD sections or docs/ with path-only pointers, and move measurement or history prose to commit and task records. Replace file:line pointers with symbol pointers (path::fn).
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: The task-5079 panic-containment guard (catch_unwind over a ComputeFn call) is reproduced in OptimizedComputeDispatcher::dispatch instead of shared with Engine::invoke_compute_trampoline. Its rustdoc says 'the two must be kept in step'. The reason given is that invoke_compute_trampoline needs &Engine, but the guard itself needs only the ComputeFn and its arguments. invoke_compute_trampoline's own comment says 'Any new dispatch path must do the same rather than calling ... f(..) directly', so this INV-FEA-2 rule is enforced by prose at each call site.
findings.proposal: Extract `fn call_compute_fn_guarded(f: ComputeFn, target: &str, ..args) -> ComputeOutcome` (panic -> Failed with the existing message) and call it from both sites. The dispatcher then maps a non-Completed outcome to None.

findings.statement: dynamics_ops.rs holds two unrelated units. The first is body_mass_props evaluation (lines 44-717). The second is the inverse_dynamics ComputeNode trampoline (InverseDynamicsCache, InverseDynamicsRun, run_inverse_dynamics, solve_inverse_dynamics_trampoline, lines 1940-2232), placed after a 1200-line test module. The module doc describes only body_mass_props. The trampoline half references none of the mass-props helpers. Its core also returns a production struct carrying a test-only field: InverseDynamicsRun.reused is `#[allow(dead_code)]` and 'observable only in-crate (the cache-HIT tests)'. modal_ops::ModalTrampolineRun repeats the pattern.
findings.proposal: Move the inverse-dynamics half and its tests to inverse_dynamics_ops.rs (no shared private symbols, measured). Assert the cache-hit through the public ComputeOutcome (the donated warm state, or a cancellation-before-first-sample probe) and drop `reused`.

findings.statement: The spatial hash is correct only under the completeness keystone r_a + r_b >= threshold(a,b). That keystone is restated as a literal 0.75 at two code sites (max_r and r_i in compute_adjacency_with_stats) and is not derived from the thresholds' own coefficients (0.5 touching + 0.25 slack in adjacency_threshold and inter_layer_threshold). Raising the slack in either threshold silently breaks completeness, so the hash drops true adjacencies. The differential test shares the threshold functions and has no pair near the boundary, so it would not catch this. The same function carries a stale comment ('degenerate ... beads floor cell_size to 1e-9' against a 1e-3 floor two paragraphs up) and a same_layer branch in the inter-layer loop that cannot fire by construction. parse_prusaslicer_gcode also carries a stale comment (';LAYER_CHANGE / ;Z: are handled in step-8', though both are handled just above it).
findings.proposal: Define one SLACK (or inflation) constant and derive both the thresholds and r_i from it, with a debug_assert of r_a + r_b >= threshold at probe time. Delete the dead branch and the stale comments.

findings.statement: engine_compute.rs still carries pieces of the contract crate that task #4934 split out. The first is a re-export shim (`pub use reify_compute_contract::{ComputeFn, ComputeOutcome, DispatchError, RealizationReadHandle, RealizedContent, StructuredComputeDetail}`), kept, per its comment, so `crate::engine_compute::X` paths resolve. That makes three import paths for each contract type (contract crate, reify_eval root via lib.rs, engine_compute). The second is the RealizationReadHandle accessor tests (handle_new_*, typed_accessor_*, boundary_accessor_*, clone_shares_arc_*), which live in this module's 3878-line test block. crates/reify-compute-contract/src/realization.rs, which defines those accessors, has 0 tests.
findings.proposal: Move the accessor tests to reify-compute-contract. Rewrite the 31 shim-path imports to reify_compute_contract:: (or crate root) and delete the shim.

findings.statement: closed_chain_inverse_dynamics repeats snapshot_inverse_dynamics's mechanism/snapshot marshalling instead of sharing it. The repeated steps are: the per-body at/id extraction, parent_idx from joint_parents, topo_order plus its inverse permutation, the motion subspaces, slicing q̇/q̈, the snapshot world_transform index, and the RneaLink build loop. The copies have already diverged. The open chain computes `compliance` through joint_compliance (spring and damping), while the closed chain hard-codes `compliance: None`. The closed chain's comment justifies this as 'mirrors the open-chain snapshot literal above (`snapshot_inverse_dynamics`), which also passes `None`', which is false. As a result, a flexure joint inside a loop-closed mechanism silently loses its spring and damping torque, and no diagnostic reports it. Both functions are around 225 lines with deep Option-early-return chains.
findings.proposal: Extract one `MechanismTree` parse: from (mechanism, snapshot, n_tree, q̇, q̈, positions) to a typed struct holding links, ordering, dof_counts, at_joints and ids. Both paths build from it. The closed chain then gets compliance either through that parse or through an explicit, named refusal. Delete the false parity comment.

findings.statement: stdlib builtins return a bare Value::Undef with no reason attached. Diagnostics are produced afterwards by classifier hooks that re-run the builtin's validation to infer why it failed. fea::diagnose says its 'Check ordering faithfully mirrors linear_combine's own per-entry Undef order'. It re-implements the arity, cases-map, weights-map, empty, String-key, numeric/finite-weight, known-case, container, displacement/stress resolution and metadata_matches checks in the same order, citing linear_combine by stale line numbers (fea.rs:140-173, 180-196, 209-250). dynamics::eval::diagnose openly documents 'Best-effort attribution… the diagnostic will attribute the failure to mass' even when Undef came from something else. reify-expr's emit_undef_builtin_diagnostics runs six such hooks in a row. This is the doc's 're-derives state in order to check it' smell: the invariant that says why a builtin returns Undef has two homes per builtin.
findings.proposal: Have each builtin's validator return a typed failure (for example Result<Value, BuiltinFailure> with an optional DiagnosticCode). eval_builtin then maps a failure to Undef plus a diagnostic at a single point, and the six re-deriving classifiers go away. This is a cross-area contract change in reify-expr's builtin dispatch.

findings.statement: The MassProperties Value shape (mass Scalar{MASS}, com Point of lengths, inertia Matrix of MOMENT_OF_INERTIA scalars, origin Frame3) is built by two producers and read by two inertia parsers in two crates. The producers are reify-stdlib's dynamics::eval::make_mass_properties and reify-eval's dynamics_ops::assemble_mass_properties plus inertia_value. The parsers are stdlib's inertia_3x3_from_value and reify-eval's dynamics_psd::inertia_3x3_from_value. Only `origin` was consolidated, through the shared default_frame3. The stated reason for the copy is 'Re-spelled locally from reify_eval::dynamics_psd::inertia_3x3_from_value (that one lives in another crate)'. That reasoning points the wrong way: reify-eval already depends on reify-stdlib as a normal dependency (reify-eval/Cargo.toml `reify-stdlib.workspace = true`) and already imports resolve_body_mass and mass_properties_from_value from it.
findings.proposal: Make reify-stdlib's dynamics module the single owner: a typed `MassProps { mass, com, inertia }` with `to_value`/`from_value`. reify-eval's assemble_mass_properties and dynamics_psd call it, and the reify-eval copies are deleted.

findings.statement: result.rs keeps private copies of the persistent-cache wire primitives: bincode_options, check_len, MAX_*_ELEMENTS, write/read slab codecs for f64, u32, [u32;3], [f64;3] and [i32;3], and severity and diagnostic codecs. Each slab reader carries its own unsafe spare-capacity block with SAFETY reasoning. The same primitives exist as `pub` in reify-compute-contract/src/elastic_result.rs, and the severity codec exists again in reify-eval/src/persistent_cache/diagnostics_wire.rs. The module doc claims 'every cacheable type in the engine shares one wire-format contract', but the sharing is done by copying. The copies have already diverged: read_f64_slab's big-endian path and its SAFETY text differ between the two crates.
findings.proposal: Move the slab and length-cap primitives next to the PersistentlyCacheable trait (reify-core::persistent_cache, or a small wire crate that both reify-compute-contract and reify-shell-extract can depend on). Delete the copies so that result.rs holds only its DTOs and tag tables.

findings.statement: mesh-morph has two process-global observability registries for the same morph events. diagnostics.rs (AtomicU64 COUNTERS) is fed by compose_morph's record_morphed, record_ineligible, record_panicked and record_quality_remesh calls. stats.rs (a Mutex-wrapped MorphStats) has recorders with zero production callers; its own G-allow markers say task #4744 'landed its diagnostics via diagnostics.rs … not these stats.rs counters'. Even so, stats::snapshot is re-exported as the crate-root `reify_mesh_morph::snapshot`, while the live one has to be reached as diagnostics::snapshot to avoid the name collision. stats::snapshot is also served by the GUI debug RPC `morph_stats` (gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs::handle_morph_stats), which therefore always reports morph_count=0, remesh_count=0. Global counters also force a shared TEST_LOCK and reset_for_test, and fix 8bf7a53070 was needed to serialise those tests.
findings.proposal: Retire stats.rs. Point `morph_stats` at diagnostics::snapshot, or delete it in favour of `mesh_morph_stats`. Remove the crate-root `snapshot` re-export so the only observability path is the one compose_morph writes.

findings.statement: `pub fn morph` is a skeleton that never morphs. It ignores old_mesh and options, and for every eligible edit it returns SolverError('engine not yet implemented (PRD … tasks #5-#9)'), even though those tasks have landed as compose_morph. Its doc table still says 'until PRD tasks #5–#9 land the engine'. Four unit tests pin the stub behaviour, for example asserting 'eligible path should return SolverError (unimplemented)'. options.rs comments still say the quality floors will be re-evaluated 'once PRD task #10 (engine wiring, `lib.rs::morph()`) lands'. The engine wiring actually landed in compose_morph and register_morph_producer.
findings.proposal: Delete `morph` and its four stub tests. Point the options.rs comments at compose_morph.

findings.statement: No type or accessor in reify-ir encodes the axis order of Regular3D SampledField data. reify-ir's doc says only 'Flat row-major data'. Readers each spell out the index themselves: shell-extract medial::sample_at_index uses `data[i*nj*nk + j*nk + k]`, and reify-expr interp::index_3d and sampled_fd do the same. Producers flatten with hand-written loops. One production producer, reify-eval compute_targets/shell_solve.rs::build_slab_sdf (wired by engine_eval to feed shell-extract's extract node), flattens z-outermost over axis_grids [x(16), y(16), z(7)]. That transposes it relative to the reader, so shell-extract sees a scrambled field rather than a slab. Only a non-empty-mask check guards it. Inside shell-extract, the grid-sampling primitives live in medial.rs. walk_direction imports medial::{normalize3, sample_at_index} while medial imports walk_direction::medial_walk_direction, which forms a 2-cycle. Six private slab_sdf_3d fixture copies re-spell the layout, and tests/common/mod.rs has to warn 'do not copy' the transposed eval fixtures.
findings.proposal: Give SampledField in reify-ir a `flat_index_3d([i,j,k])` / `at_3d` accessor and a `from_fn_3d` constructor that state the axis-0-outermost order. Move shell-extract's sampling primitives into a `grid` module beside grid_validation, which breaks the medial↔walk_direction cycle. Rebuild build_slab_sdf and the fixtures on the constructor.

findings.statement: grid_validation.rs was 'Extracted from the duplicated validation prelude in medial.rs and mid_surface.rs', but only the kind, axis-length and empty-axis checks moved. The data-length check (validate_flat_data_length, giving DataLengthMismatch or AxisExtentsOverflow) and the finite/positive-spacing and non-inverted-bounds check (InvalidAxisGeometry) stayed in compute_medial_mask. extract_mid_surface is public and calls medial::sample_at_index (`sdf.data[...]`) without either check, and MidSurfaceError has no variant for them. A malformed SampledField is therefore rejected with a typed error by compute_medial_mask but panics with an index-out-of-bounds in extract_mid_surface. The NaN-spacing case also slips through the mask-alignment check, because `(NaN - x).abs() > tol` is false. The comment there calls the lookup 'infallible by construction'.
findings.proposal: Move the axis-geometry and flat-data-length checks into grid_validation::validate_regular3d (with GridValidationError variants), so every entry point enforces the same invariant through one definition.

findings.statement: Joint kind is carried as a string ("revolute", "prismatic", …) in the joint Value::Map, and every consumer re-dispatches on the literal. joint_force_value matches six kind strings with a `_ => None` wildcard. joints::motion_subspace_columns, snapshot.rs and loop_closure.rs each do the same. A typed `JointKind` enum already exists in loop_closure_value.rs, documented as 'mirroring `joints::JOINT_KINDS` 1:1', next to `JOINT_KINDS: &[&str]` in joints.rs. So the kind set has two definitions, and the per-kind behaviour axis has one string match per consumer. Because of the wildcard arms, adding a kind compiles cleanly and silently turns every unhandled consumer into Undef.
findings.proposal: Parse the kind once at the joint boundary into the existing JointKind enum (made the single definition, with JOINT_KINDS derived from it), and give each consumer an exhaustive match on the enum.

findings.statement: fea.rs defines its own 'same sampling grid' predicate, grids_equal: kind, interpolation, data length and bit-equal bounds, spacing and axis_grids, listed field by field. reify-ir already has SampledField::grid_metadata_eq for the same concept. That method destructures `Self` so that a new field causes a compile error. The two predicates also disagree on what they include: grid_metadata_eq compares `name` and ignores data length, while grids_equal ignores name and compares data length. grids_equal's doc cites 'crates/reify-types/src/value.rs:149-189', a crate path that no longer exists. Separately, the 'clone grid metadata, swap data' SampledField literal is written out 6 times in fea.rs production.
findings.proposal: Add a name-agnostic, exhaustive `SampledField::same_grid(&other)` and a `with_data(name, data)` constructor to reify-ir. Route grids_equal, metadata_matches and the six literals through them.

findings.statement: Production prose in the slice's large files is 40-57% of non-blank lines. Much of it is prose aimed at a reviewer, defending choices in place. Examples: min_max_stress's 50-line 'deliberate two-call trade-off', envelope_tensor_projection's two-pass defence, compliance_cell_f64's roughly 65-line dimension-erasure declaration, and MedialOptions field docs that restate derivations owned by the PRD. The pointers inside that prose are file:line citations, and every one I checked is stale. In dynamics/eval.rs, 'eval.rs:862' and 'eval.rs:403-416' point at unrelated code, and value_for is cited at snapshot.rs:961 but sits at 1403. In fea.rs, the 'fea.rs:517-524', '140-173', '1604' and '1647' citations miss, and a crate path that no longer exists is cited. In medial.rs, precompute_gradient_grid cites 'line 470 … line 475' and MedialOptions cites '~:617' for code now around 700. Recent amend commits (7992f56f3e 'correct four stale comments', c2fa9972fa 'replace task-process archaeology') show this drift is recurring maintenance work.
findings.proposal: Replace file:line citations with symbol paths, and add a cheap lint (ptodo-style ratchet) that rejects `\.rs:[0-9]+` in comments. Move the decision defences (the two-call/two-pass trade-offs, the window derivation) to the PRD or commit messages, leaving a one-line pointer.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: The ShellExtractionResult <-> Value::StructureInstance projection has one hand-written string-keyed encoder (shell_extraction_result_to_value) and three independent decoders with different strictness: value_to_shell_extraction_result (persistent-cache rehydration; returns None on any mismatch, does not check inner type_name), fold_mid_surface_attributes_into_table in the same file (re-decodes naming.face_records/edges with a warn-and-skip policy), and reify_eval::engine_admin::parse_shell_extraction_result (GUI populator; checks inner type_name "MidSurfaceMesh"/"SegmentationResult" and accepts vertex rows of any length, where decode_real3_list demands exactly 3). The encoder is lossy (regions -> voxel_count only, diagnostics -> Debug strings, region_pair dropped) and the decoder defaults regions/diagnostics to vec![], so a persistent-cache warm serve returns a Value whose segmentation.regions is [] where the cold dispatch had N>0 entries. The only guard that no consumer reads those fields is a prose census in value_to_shell_extraction_result's doc ("Verified: the only two consumers..."), and tests/harness_topology_selector/shell_extract_persistent_cache_round_trip.rs pins the divergence (cold regions > 0, warm regions == []) rather than preventing it.
findings.proposal: One typed codec for the projection (named field constants, encode(&ShellExtractionResult) -> Value and decode(&Value) -> Result<view, DecodeError>) used by the persistence bridge, the fold hook and the GUI populator; make the round trip lossless by construction, either by projecting only what decode rebuilds (so cold == warm) or by persisting the projected Value itself.

findings.statement: membrane_load.rs re-implements tensegrity_load.rs instead of extending it. GROUNDING_DIAGONAL, member_force_delta and bar_axial_force_delta are copied (its doc says "Ported verbatim from T3b"). The validation preamble, the tension-only active-set loop, the post-loop member-force report and solve_active_pass's assemble -> Dirichlet -> solve_cg -> scatter tail are line-for-line copies, and MembraneLoadError/MembraneLoadOptions mirror TensegrityLoadError/TensegrityLoadOptions. With an empty patch slice, membrane_load_analysis computes exactly what tensegrity_load_analysis computes. The copies have already diverged: tensegrity_load's orphan-grounding loop guards `node < n_nodes &&`, membrane_load's does not.
findings.proposal: Make tensegrity_load_analysis a thin call of membrane_load_analysis with no patches (mapping result and error types), or extract the shared bar / active-set / solve core into one module both kernels call.

findings.statement: The persistable-target set is a string allowlist (PERSISTABLE_TARGETS). Each target's typed cache container and Value bridge are chosen by `match target { "solver::elastic_static" => .., "solver::buckling" => .., "shell-extract::extract" => .., _ => None }` in both persistent_lookup and persistent_write; all six arms share one ~35-line read_entry/write_entry + tracing::warn shape and differ only in the cache type, the bridge fn and the message text. The same strings sit in engine_hash_tests.rs (PERSISTED_TARGET_SOURCES) and in the test-only persistable_target_fixtures, and significance_filter::is_opted_in holds an overlapping matches! list. Drift between the lists is caught today, but only by test cross-checks (persisted_target_sources_cover_exactly_the_persistable_targets; the assert_eq in persistable_target_fixtures plus per-target round trips). In release builds the `_ => None` / `_ => {}` arms mean an allowlisted target with no arm is silently never cached. Cross-cutting envelope changes (diagnostics replay 2026-09-09, structured_detail 2026-10-05) each had to be threaded through and pinned per arm.
findings.proposal: A trait per persistable target (cache type, to_cache(&Value) -> Option<Cache>, from_cache(&Cache) -> Value) with one registry keyed by a typed target id, so lookup and write are each one generic body and the allowlist, the fixtures and the engine-hash table derive from the registry.

findings.statement: MpcRow's invariant (dofs.len() == coeffs.len(), non-empty, coeffs[0] finite and non-zero, rhs finite) is enforced only in MpcRow::new, but all three fields are pub and neither consumer checks it again. apply_mpc_row_elimination divides by coeffs[0] and zips dofs[1..] with coeffs[1..], so a length mismatch silently truncates the constraint and a zero pivot writes +/-inf into K and f. buckling_kernel's MPC reduction reads row.dofs[0] and row.coeffs[0] in the same unchecked way. The unvalidated path is actively pinned: tests::mpc_row_type_compiles_with_documented_field_shape and the lib.rs crate-root doctest both build MpcRow from a struct literal. The struct doc still says "Constructors that enforce this invariant are deferred to T10 (Task 3020); for now consumers build via struct-literal initialization", and the module doc calls T10 "pending", although new, shell_tet_tying and apply_mpc_row_elimination all ship in the file.
findings.proposal: Make the fields private with read accessors so new / shell_tet_tying are the only constructors; delete the struct-literal smoke test and doctest line; rewrite the module and struct docs to describe the shipped surface.

findings.statement: The stress builtins (von_mises, principal_stresses, max_shear, safety_factor, stress_invariants, dispatched from registry_dispatch) accept any 3x3 matrix Value from user .ri code. The kernels read only the upper triangle and check symmetry with debug_assert!, so an asymmetric user matrix panics the evaluator in debug builds (the profile the test suite and agents run) and returns the upper-triangle answer in release. compute_stress_invariants_3x3's own doc states this: "A user passing a genuinely asymmetric 3x3 .ri matrix will panic in debug builds". The symmetry predicate is a closure copied verbatim into compute_von_mises_3x3, compute_eigenvalues_3x3 and compute_stress_invariants_3x3. Nothing checks symmetry at the Value seam, and no test uses an asymmetric input.
findings.proposal: Validate (or symmetrize) once at the Value boundary, in one helper every builtin uses, returning Undef or a diagnostic for an asymmetric 3x3. The f64 kernels keep the documented precondition and share one is_symmetric_3x3 for their debug asserts.

findings.statement: "Registry-free StructureInstance" has two incompatible type_id conventions. analysis.rs defines REGISTRY_FREE_TYPE_ID = StructureTypeId(u32::MAX) as a private const; its doc admits it is one of several copies and that the dedup is "deferred beyond task 2884's scope". There are now five production const copies. Meanwhile shell_extract_compute.rs (8 sites) and reify-stdlib tensegrity.rs (10 sites) mint registry-free instances with StructureTypeId(0), and 0 is not a sentinel: StructureRegistry::intern assigns ids from by_id.len(), so 0 is the first real interned structure. reify_eval::value_type_kind_matches resolves a TraitObject cell type through registry.meta(data.type_id). A 0-tagged instance is therefore checked against the trait bounds of whichever structure was interned first, while a u32::MAX instance resolves to None.
findings.proposal: One pub constructor in reify-ir (e.g. StructureInstanceData::registry_free(type_name, fields), or a single pub const) used at every minting site, with the StructureTypeId(0) placeholders migrated to it.

findings.statement: The fact that libgmsh is absent from this build travels as a substring of GeometryError::OperationFailed(String). The two kernel-gmsh stubs format STUB_UNAVAILABLE_MARKER into their message, and two consumer-side copies of map_geometry_error (volume_refine.rs and mesher.rs) recover the fact with msg.contains(STUB_UNAVAILABLE_MARKER) to produce RefineError::GmshUnavailable / Mesh2dError::GmshUnavailable. Sharing the constant protects against a reworded message, but not against a new stub entry point that formats its own text: that stub would be classified as a runtime gmsh failure.
findings.proposal: Return a typed variant (GeometryError::BackendUnavailable { backend }, or a kernel-gmsh error enum) from every stub, and match it structurally.

findings.statement: TetSpatialIndex::build(nodes, elems, tol) pads its AABBs by tol but keeps neither the mesh nor tol, so locate/locate_counted make the caller pass the same nodes, elems and tol again. The same-mesh contract is checked only by two debug_assert_eq! on lengths, and the same-tol contract is not checked at all. A query tol larger than the build tol under-pads the boxes and breaks the documented guarantee of results bit-identical to locate_element_p1; the doc calls under-padding "not possible here". volume_refine::TetShape has the same shape: its doc concedes the proof token "does not pin which mesh", so refine_with_size_field_validated and project_per_element_sizes_to_vertices carry a prose same-mesh caller contract.
findings.proposal: TetSpatialIndex<'a> borrows nodes/elems and owns tol, and locate takes only the point; likewise TetShape<'a> carries its &VolumeMesh.

findings.statement: qoi.rs is 2,423 lines. 1,613 of them (67%) are the #[cfg(test)] module, whose non-comment code reaches only crate-root-public items (the QoI types and trait, QoiError variants, P1TetMeshRef, point_in_tet_p1, tet_volume_p1, IsotropicElastic), so it gains nothing from living in the file. The 810-line production half is 52% comment lines, and part of that prose answers reviewers rather than informing the next change: measured release behaviour ("evaluate returned Ok(NaN) and dual_load a g with 12 of 15 entries non-finite"), a discarded alternative's cost ("~100 MB of transient allocation per refinement iteration"), the predecessor variant's name, and per-test "# TDD red->green" step histories copied from the 2026-09-14/15 RED/GREEN commits.
findings.proposal: Move the test module to crates/reify-solver-elastic/tests/qoi.rs as an integration test (no heuristic-13 symptom: every item it uses is re-exported at the crate root). Move measurement and rejected-alternative prose into the task record or commit messages, keeping the PRD section pointers.

findings.statement: Comments in this slice point by file:line and describe plan-step status, and most of them have drifted. 6 of the 7 path:line pointers in the read production regions no longer land on what they name: analysis.rs -> dynamics_ops.rs:41 (the const is at :44); volume_refine.rs -> mesher.rs:535-544 (map_geometry_error is at :652) and "~line 199" (refine_with_size_field_validated is at :696); constitutive.rs x2 -> materials_fea.ri:94-103 (load-order prose, not the Poisson bound); shell_result.rs -> solver_elastic.ri:366 (structure def ShellStress is at :686); interpolation.rs -> assembly/tet.rs:182. Status prose has gone false the same way: mpc.rs says T10 is "pending"; shell_result.rs's header says it "ships the data-only contract; T18-T20 are responsible for actually populating these fields", yet shell_element_stress populates them; and error_estimator.rs's two_tet_fan_mesh doc says "Both tets have volume 1/6" (tet1 has volume 1/3), which qoi.rs's copy of the fixture documents instead of fixing.
findings.proposal: Replace file:line pointers with symbol paths (mesher::map_geometry_error), delete plan-status prose from module docs (it belongs in task records), and correct the error_estimator fixture doc.
