findings.statement: The Rust ShellStress container (pub, re-exported at the crate root) has no production consumer. Outside shell_result.rs's own tests and a lib.rs doc example, nothing constructs or reads it; the DSL-side `structure def ShellStress` in solver_elastic.ri is filled through flatten_shell_channels' four Vec<f64> buffers in reify-eval's compute_targets/shell_solve.rs, not through this type. Its file header still tells the next agent the two definitions "must stay shape-aligned" and promises a cross-assertion from "T18-T20" that does not exist.
findings.proposal: Delete ShellStress, its crate-root re-export and its doctest line, and remove the shape-alignment obligation from the shell_result.rs header.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: ee76e7e27a (#8528, done) deleted the Rust ShellStress container, its crate-root re-export and the lib.rs doctest. git grep finds ShellStress in solver-elastic only in doc prose naming the stdlib structure (shell_result.rs:7, shell_solve.rs:39). 78c7c9d1c7 ('chore: save WIP before requeue rebase', which landed on main) rewrote the shell_result.rs header so it no longer promises shape alignment.; task store: [('8528', 'done')]

findings.statement: shell_extract_compute_fn is a ~270-line function that interleaves the five-phase extraction pipeline with the PRD §7 error-to-diagnostic table. It has 13 `return ComputeOutcome::Failed { diagnostics: vec![Diagnostic::error(format!(..)).with_code(..)], structured_detail: vec![] }` exits, each hand-built inline, plus 5 cancellation polls; the mapping from each phase's error enum to a DiagnosticCode has no home of its own.
findings.proposal: One small mapping fn per phase error type (medial, mid-surface, prune, mesher, segmentation) -> Diagnostic, and a pipeline that runs on `?` over Result<_, Diagnostic> and converts once into ComputeOutcome::Failed.

findings.statement: A Diagnostic carries no structured link to its constraint. Retracting a stale `constraint {subject} indeterminate` claim after a verdict upgrade therefore parses message text, and three consumers do it with three different matchers. replace_superseded_constraint_diagnostics uses `d.message.starts_with(claim)`. Engine::build's 4229 merge loop (engine_build.rs, the two `d.message.contains(&needle)` sites) uses a bare substring match. reify-cli main.rs uses an exact-subject parse (indeterminacy_subject_in / is_falsified_indeterminacy). The CLI leg was moved to the exact parse by task 5748 precisely because a substring match let a verdict for `Foo#constraint[1]` delete the still-true warning for `Foo#constraint[10]`. The engine_build leg still has that defect today. The grammar is produced at two independent format! sites: reify-constraints/src/lib.rs (SimpleConstraintChecker) and engine_constraints.rs::Engine::dispatch_constraints. It is then rewritten by Engine::labeled_diagnostics through `message.replace(id_str, label)`. Task #7991 tracks the convergence and is pending at low priority.
findings.proposal: Do what #7991 describes, at higher priority. Attach the ConstraintNodeId to verdict diagnostics structurally at push_constraint_result / the checker boundary, then replace all three matchers with one structural comparison so the engine_build over-match disappears.

findings.statement: solver.rs is 11788 lines: 4686 production lines and 7103 embedded test lines, with a field-set pin test module sitting in the middle of production code. The production code holds nine separable concerns: trial-value folding, residuals, the alpha robustness floor, gamma interval derivation, centrality/cost function, the Nelder-Mead core, the tradeoff blend, uniqueness verification and the ConstraintSolver API. They are not layered. The floor concern calls back into the core (constraints_witness -> solve_core_with_sd_tolerance under FeasibilityWitness), while the core calls the floor (synthesise_floor_constraints, floor_infeasible_diagnostic, objective_is_money), so the two form a call cycle. derive_param_intervals needs effective_bounds from the cost/bounds region while that region needs derived_seed_box from derive. The 143 embedded tests reach 34 of the file's 70 private items directly (e.g. solve_core, verify_uniqueness, classify_uniqueness, resolve_bounds, derive_from_expr, ConstraintCostFunction), so they pin internals rather than ConstraintSolver behaviour. The file carries 105 commits since 2026-07-06; the core function alone is ~450 lines. Its name, solve_core_with_sd_tolerance, describes a parameter every caller now passes as NM_SD_TOLERANCE, and it returns `unique: true` as a documented placeholder for callers to overwrite.
findings.proposal: Partition into a solver/ module tree layered trial < residual < derive(+extract_initial_point) < bounds/cost(+effective_bounds, default_bounds_for) < floor < core(+constraints_witness, which closes the cycle by living with the core or taking the re-solve as a closure) < tradeoff < uniqueness < api. Move tests to the ConstraintSolver seam or the layer's own interface, and rename the core once the tolerance parameter is gone.

findings.statement: Production prose in this slice is 42-72% of non-blank lines, and much of it is reviewer-answering text: measurements, rejected alternatives, 're-measured (task #5711 step-7)', 'History (task #4700 -> #4710)'. That kind of prose drifts. 24 of the 105 commits on solver.rs since 2026-07-06 exist only to correct, retire or re-measure its own comments ('Fix stale line-number cites', 'drop two stale claims from the comments just added', 'correct the three claims this branch falsified'). Drift is present elsewhere at this tree: all 7 cross-file line cites in manifold kernel.rs to reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs land on unrelated code (456-466 is the history-buffer struct; get_shape is at 870, extracted_faces at 644); engine_constraints.rs cites itself at ':42-62' and measure_dfm_rules at ':842-854', and both are wrong; dispatcher.rs's module doc says ReprKind has 4 variants and bounds the BFS at 4 expansions, but ReprKind has 5; kernel_real.rs cites 'line ~120' for a clear() now at 469. reify-audit's PCITE lane covers capability-manifest cites only, so nothing gates source-comment line cites.
findings.proposal: Move reviewer-answering prose (measurements, rejected alternatives, task histories) into commit messages and task records. Keep rationale that must persist in docs/ or the PRD behind one symbol-anchored pointer. Replace path:line cites with symbol anchors, as docs(6990) did for solver.rs.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: ManifoldKernel's catch-all arms in execute, query and export all return STUB_MSG. It reads 'Manifold query/export not yet implemented for v0.2; boolean ops and tessellate are wired ..., but query/export are follow-up work'. In fact query answers 11 GeometryQuery variants (Distance, Contains, GeoEquiv, SurfaceArea, FaceNormal, EdgeTangent, BoundingBox, AdjacentFaces, SharedEdges, CenterOfMass, InertiaTensor) and export writes STL and 3MF. So for the other 25 of 36 query variants and every other export format, users and agents get an error that misstates the kernel. The module doc's '## Task-9-pending stub semantics' section says propagate_attributes returns Ok(Discarded) with a warn reason="task_9_pending". The body has walked MeshGL64 provenance and returned Propagated since c7b7242690 (2026-06-04), and task_9_pending no longer appears in any production code.
findings.proposal: Make the catch-all messages name the unsupported variant or format (e.g. `unsupported query {query:?} on manifold`), and replace the stale module-doc stub section with a one-line description of the current behaviour.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: Removed by #8529 (done): e38074ad09 'manifold catch-alls name the rejected variant instead of STUB_MSG' and 284b330feb 'drop false manifold stub claims'. git grep STUB_MSG|task_9_pending|Task-9 in crates/reify-kernel-manifold = 0; execute/query/export catch-alls now read 'unsupported op {kind_name} on manifold kernel' / 'unsupported query {kind_name}' / 'unsupported export format {format:?}'. The same cost survives in OpenVDB (see new finding on kernel_real.rs::VOXEL_BOOL_STUB_MSG).; task store: [('8529', 'done')]

findings.statement: Every gmsh mesher must follow a library-session protocol, and each entry point restates it by hand. The order is: init::lock, init::ensure_initialized, MeshSizeScope::entered, ffi::clear, General.Terminal=0, LogCapture::armed (which must come right after the Terminal write), then mesh_generate_with_recovery (which no caller LogCapture seam may also cover), then read_tet_connectivity and a trailing best-effort clear. mesh_to_volume, refine_volume_with_size_field, mesh_surface_to_volume_with_attribution and mesh_plane_2d each repeat it. The invariant is enforced by prose that enumerates the callers by name (mesh_generate_with_recovery's doc: 'None of this function's four callers ... Each ... arms one LogCapture right after its own General.Terminal write'). The copies have already diverged: mesh_plane_2d has no trailing clear, and refine_volume sets ElementOrder before Algorithm3D where the others do the reverse. The P1->1.0/P2->2.0 ElementOrder mapping is copied 3 times. The P1->4/P2->10 tet stride is copied 3 times in-crate (init, fill_metrics, through_thickness) beside reify_ir::VolumeMesh::nodes_per_element, and init.rs's own doc acknowledges that with no task cited.
findings.proposal: Introduce one session constructor in init.rs that performs lock + init + size scope + clear + terminal + capture, returns a session type the meshers take, and owns the trailing clear on drop. Move the element-order tables to the reify_ir type that owns the fact.

findings.statement: Engine names its kernels by String, and the production constructor files its picked adapter under the sentinel string Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME ("__reify_eval_default_kernel"). Engine::with_registered_kernel is that constructor, used by reify-cli cmd_check/cmd_build and the GUI. The sentinel encodes a construction mode, not a kernel. Production code branches on it in engine_build.rs (`default_kernel_name == Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME` selects backward-compat fallback vs NoKernelChain) and in realization_content.rs::resolve_realization_kernel, where a canonical-name miss falls back to the sentinel. Because the sentinel resolves to nothing in the static registry, the engine cannot ask its own kernel's CapabilityDescriptor. Task 6169 therefore added Engine::repr_capable_kernel: Option<bool>, recorded by two constructors, plus a registry fallback with a benefit-of-the-doubt rule. Explaining why the lookup cannot work takes 64 doc lines on has_repr_capable_kernel and unmeasured_reason.
findings.proposal: Key geometry_kernels by KernelId (or keep the KernelRegistration alongside each adapter), and make the backward-compat mode an explicit enum on Engine rather than a reserved string, so capability is read from the held kernel's descriptor.

findings.statement: Engine::check runs eval() and then three check-time passes: dispatch_constraints' RepresentationWithin interception, measure_gdt_conformance and measure_dfm_rules. Their verdicts are read from Engine fields that eval() never writes or clears. achieved_repr_tol is written only by tessellate_realizations and cleared only on the Tessellate* surfaces. realization_handles is written by build and cleared only on the Build/BuildSnapshot surfaces (engine_build.rs reset match: the 'build<->tessellate asymmetry'). capture_repr_tol is set by a separate setter. check()'s own doc states the ordering contract: callers must call set_capture_repr_tol(true) then tessellate_realizations before check(). measure_dfm_rules is a no-op unless a prior build() stamped realization_handles. A check() after an edit without a fresh build injects handles from the previous build, keyed by RealizationNodeId, into the GD&T and DFM measurements.
findings.proposal: Pass the realized geometry view (handles + achieved deviations) into the check passes as an explicit argument produced by build/tessellate, instead of reading retained Engine fields.

findings.statement: The guard-activation policy (Bool(true) activates the then-branch, Bool(false) the else-branch, anything else neither) is implemented three times over two different data shapes. Engine::collect_active_constraints walks TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups via guard_value_cell and serves check(), check_snapshot, check_constraints_post_geometry and measure_gdt_conformance. EvaluationGraph::active_constraint_ids (graph.rs) walks graph.guarded_groups via guard_cell and serves recheck_active_constraints, i.e. check_constraints_with_values (edit_check) and upgrade_indeterminate_verdicts. invariants.rs::guard_inactive_members restates it over members/else_members with a doc comment saying it 'Mirrors'. No shared predicate exists, so the check() path and the edit/upgrade path pick active constraints by independent code.
findings.proposal: Give the guard decision one home (a function from guard Value to an active-branch enum), and have all three walks call it. Better still, derive the edit/upgrade path's active set from the same template walk check() uses.

findings.statement: measure_dfm_rules already knows each measurement's kind statically (DfmRuleKind::Overhang/Draft, thickness pair). It still reports through reify_stdlib::dfm_diagnose with a builtin-name string ('unsupported_overhang_faces', 'min_draft_angle', 'min_wall_thickness', 'min_feature_size_measure') and an untyped Value verdict whose meaning varies by arm. For overhang, wall and feature, Bool(true) means violation, the opposite of fits_build_volume's polarity. For draft the verdict is List[Bool draft, Bool undercut] by position. dfm_diagnose's `_ => Vec::new()` arm means a misspelled name emits nothing. Under the C1 rule ('never a false Violated') emitting nothing is also what a conforming or unmeasurable verdict does, so a typo is indistinguishable from a pass. Rule recognition is likewise duck-typed by field-name strings ('severity' as Enum 'DFMSeverity', 'applies_to', 'max_overhang_angle', 'draft_angle', 'min_feature_size'), and the severity/applies_to prelude is repeated in dfm_rule_spec and dfm_thickness_spec.
findings.proposal: Have the engine call typed violation constructors (overhang_violation(severity), draft_violation, ...) or a typed DfmVerdict enum, and keep the string entry point only for the language-level builtin hook in reify-expr.

findings.statement: dispatch_constraints implements one algorithm: peel RepresentationWithin, bucket the rest by registered target, run each bucket, and weave results back by index. Around that sit three performance short-circuits (no-registry/no-RW fast path, all-RW, no-RW-after-peel) plus the no-registry pass-through. Each short-circuit rebuilds a ConstraintInput and calls self.constraint_checker.check itself. The function has 6 exits, 5 checker invocations and 5 ConstraintInput constructions in 205 code lines, plus 220 comment lines, most of them defending the fast-path guards' allocation cost.
findings.proposal: Keep the single peel-bucket-weave path, with the fallback bucket as one checker call, and drop the special-case exits or reduce them to one guard. Move the cost argument to the commit history.

findings.statement: measure_gdt_conformance rebuilds three engine views that already exist elsewhere. First, a prelude+module trait registry, built inline twice (here and in enumerate_gdt_callouts) although structural_query::build_trait_registry exists and check_constraints_against_templates uses it. Second, a prelude+module template_by_name map, built twice with the same 'module wins' override. Third, a live-realization-handle injection keyed by realization.name, also done in measure_dfm_rules into a different container, with a comment pointing at it by a stale ':842-854' cite. The 'is this a GeometricTolerance' test (template lookup + satisfies_trait_bound) appears three times.
findings.proposal: Build one GD&T context (trait registry, template lookup, augmented values) once per check and pass it to enumerate_gdt_callouts, measure_gdt_conformance and measure_dfm_rules.

findings.statement: geometry_ops.rs's child test module (34,226 lines, 542 tests, `use super::*`) drives geometry_ops through its internals rather than its entry points. It calls 41 private and 25 pub(crate) functions directly, at 609 call sites. This pins the current factoring of a 13,242-line file that is already an h14 alarm and is the area's top fix-churn file (fix-history lead: geometry_ops/tests.rs 69 commits, geometry_ops.rs 60). Any move of a helper into a submodule or change of its signature breaks tests that do not test behaviour at the seam the engine uses (compile_geometry_op, try_eval_*).
findings.proposal: Re-home helper-level tests next to the helper's new module during the split. Convert the rest to drive compile_geometry_op / try_eval_* (or an Engine fixture), and treat a new direct call into a private helper as review-blocking.

findings.statement: Within the first `impl OcctKernel` block, the same logic is copied several times instead of shared. (a) The sweep-history decode (6 buffers, cap indices, 3 counters, take-last) is copied verbatim into extrude_with_history, revolve_with_history and sweep_with_history, about 45 lines each, plus a loft variant. decode_six_buffer_history already factors exactly this pattern for the boolean and local-feature histories. (b) Revolve's five validation checks and their messages are duplicated verbatim between the execute Revolve arm and revolve_with_history; Extrude and Loft have the same pairing. (c) The curated handle-to-canonical-index mapping is copied into 5 methods (fillet_edges, chamfer_edges, chamfer_asymmetric_edges, draft_faces, shell_solid_faces) using two different algorithms (linear position vs HashMap). (d) extract_edges, extract_faces and extract_vertices are three near-identical bodies differing only in cache field, FFI getter and BRepKind. (e) The finite-positive check is open-coded 17 times beside 15 calls to validate_positive_finite, sometimes with the same message text.
findings.proposal: Add decode_sweep_history(history) mirroring decode_six_buffer_history; one validate_revolve_params / validate_extrude_distance shared by both paths; one map_selection_to_indices(parent_ids, selection, label); one extract_subshapes(kind) behind the three extract_* methods.

findings.statement: lib.rs embeds a 10,013-line test module (244 #[test], 65.7% of the file), contrary to the sheet's embedded_test_lines=0. At least 84 of those tests reach private state: store_raw, insert_null_shape, get_shape, raw ffi::ffi constructors such as make_circle_wire and make_box, and decode helpers. Meanwhile the crate maintains a second, public fixture surface for the same need: the test-fixtures-gated `impl OcctKernel` with 16 store_*_for_test methods (~360 lines), used by about 70 tests/harness_occt* files. So there are two fixture APIs over one store, and kernel tests are split between a private-reach home and a public-seam home.
findings.proposal: Move the about 160 public-surface tests to tests/harness_occt*, keep in-file only the tests that must see private invariants (warm-state destructure, IsNull injection), and build those on the same test-fixtures constructors.

findings.statement: stdlib geometry builtins report failure in two separate string dispatches over the same names. eval_geometry(name, args) returns a bare Value::Undef with no reason, from 84 return sites over 47 names. diagnose(name, args) re-dispatches on the name and re-classifies the args to reconstruct why, for only 19 of those names. The other 28 names (e.g. frame3, transform3 with a wrong-kind arg) are silently Undef. Where both arms share a classify_* Result (affine_map) the reasons agree by construction; elsewhere the eval arm's early `return Some(Value::Undef)` guards and the diagnose arm's checks are independent code. diagnose itself is 229 lines, 112 of them prose (49%), largely rulings, escalation ids and task histories (A7, esc-5791-3, RULING #6126) answering reviewers. The same eval_X/diagnose twin pattern recurs in at least 7 stdlib modules with three different signatures.
findings.proposal: Have each builtin arm return Result<Value, Rejection>, and derive both the Undef and the Diagnostic from the Rejection at the single call site in reify-expr. Move the rulings prose to the PRD/docs, with a pointer.

findings.statement: New evidence on the prior name-dispatch finding: the remaining string dispatch is now concentrated in selectors, inside one file. TopologySelectorHelper has no from_name. try_eval_topology_selector carries a 43-name string->variant match, and symbolic_eval_helper_for_name carries an independent 25-name match. All 25 also appear in the 43, so adding or renaming a selector needs two edits in the same file plus the compiler-side registrations. Arity is a third copy: TopologySelectorHelper::expected_arity on the eval side vs compiler builtin_signatures. Both name-miss and arity-miss return None, which becomes silent Undef. The constructor half of the prior finding is fixed (enum-keyed tables with a uniqueness test).
findings.proposal: One `impl TopologySelectorHelper { fn from_name(&str) -> Option<Self>; fn is_kernel_free(self) -> bool }` replacing both matches, with arity read from the compiler's builtin signature rather than restated.

findings.statement: Production comments in lib.rs navigate by line numbers that have all drifted. extract_length_f64 points to `geometry_ops.rs:482`/`:523` for required_length_value(s); those now sit at 615/839, and lines 482/523 are unrelated code. shell_solid_faces says "Structural copy of draft_faces (lib.rs:1597)"; draft_faces is at 1995. The execute arms cite "lib.rs:2167-2174", "lib.rs:2398-2418 pattern" and "lib.rs:2742"; each now lands inside unrelated code. The production half also carries 43 task/escalation references in comments.
findings.proposal: Replace each line cite with the symbol name (e.g. `draft_faces`, `required_length_value`).

findings.statement: stubs.rs's module doc says the stubs "provide the same public API surface as the real OcctKernel and OcctKernelHandle", but they do not. The stub OcctKernel has 24 public methods against the real one's 50; 26 are missing, among them reset, repr_of, shape_count, make_compound, execute_split and every *_with_history. The stub OcctKernelHandle has 16 against 33; 17 are missing, among them reset, extract_edges, extract_faces, make_compound and query_many. Parity is asserted by prose and checked by nothing.
findings.proposal: Correct the doc to state the real contract (only the GeometryKernel/WarmStartable surface is mirrored), or add a compile-time parity check.

findings.statement: OcctKernel::execute picks each result's BRepKind by exit path, not by a stated policy. 27 of the 53 constructive arms fall through to the shared tail `Ok(self.store(shape))`, which stamps BRepKind::Solid whatever the input or result kind; the other 26 return early with a fixed, classified or delegated repr. Affected fall-through arms: the transform arms Translate, Rotate, Mirror, Scale, RotateAround, AffineApply and ScaleNonUniform; the pattern arms; and Extrude, Revolve, Sweep and Pipe. The sibling ApplyTransform arm instead inherits the source repr via apply_transform_to_handle. The DSL translate() lowers to GeometryOp::Translate (geometry_ops.rs::transform_translate), so translate(rectangle_profile(..)) is stamped Solid; repr_of then misroutes Centroid away from the face-centroid branch. The same stamp lets translate(union(disjoint a, b)) pass run_local_feature_with_history's Solid-input guard. That guard's own comment claims the opposite: "apply_transform_to_handle propagates the repr, so fillet(translate(union(a, b)), ...) is rejected too". That route is not taken, and no test pins it. Separately, the all-edges Fillet/Chamfer arm (empty `edges`) calls ffi::fillet_all_edges/chamfer_all_edges directly and bypasses that guard. The curated-edge path enforces it, so the same op has two different preconditions.
findings.proposal: Remove the default tail. Have each arm return (shape, ReprPolicy) with ReprPolicy = Classify | Inherit(source) | Fixed(kind), and store once after the match, so a new arm cannot compile without choosing. Default transforms to Inherit and patterns/sweeps to Classify. Route the all-edges Fillet/Chamfer through the same Solid-input check, and correct the run_local_feature_with_history comment.

findings.statement: Point-, vector- and bbox-valued GeometryQuery answers cross the kernel/eval boundary as JSON-shaped strings and are parsed back by hand-rolled parsers. This includes Centroid, CenterOfMass, BoundingBox, EdgeTangent, FaceNormal, ClosestPointOnShape and FaceNormalAt, all encoded as `Value::String("{\"x\":..}")`. Typed variants already exist: Value::Point, Value::Direction, Value::BoundingBox and Value::Matrix. The same query() already uses Value::Point/Direction/Plane/Axis for FaceAnalyticDatum/EdgeAnalyticDatum. centroid_json's doc says other arms keep inline format! because "no cross-arm equality contract applies". Yet the four inline arms emit the identical shape precisely because one eval parser (topology_selectors::parse_xyz_value) consumes them all, so the contract exists and is held by convention. FaceSurfaceKind/EdgeCurveKind also return enum names as strings, decoded downstream by try_from_str.
findings.proposal: Return Value::Point / Value::Vector / Value::BoundingBox / Value::Matrix from query(), with one typed accessor in reify-ir per shape. Delete the 11 parsers, and return the surface/curve kind as Value::Enum or a typed enum.

findings.statement: get_shape is documented as the single chokepoint that refuses null/IsNull topology "loudly" (fix 5211): it returns OperationFailed("shape handle .. wraps null/empty topology (IsNull)"). Every query-side caller discards that through `.get_shape(id).map_err(|_| QueryError::InvalidHandle(id))`, so a corrupted but present handle is reported to the user as an invalid handle. export/tessellate do the same into ExportError::InvalidHandle/TessError::InvalidHandle. The guard's test (get_shape_rejects_null_topology_and_queries_return_err) asserts only `is_err()` on the query paths, so the message loss is unpinned.
findings.proposal: Add one `fn shape_for_query(&self, id) -> Result<&OcctShape, QueryError>` mapping InvalidReference(id) to InvalidHandle(id) and OperationFailed(msg) to QueryFailed(msg), with sibling helpers for ExportError and TessError. Replace the 54 sites and assert the message in the existing null-topology test.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: Fixed by #7379 (done): 4095ba9c2e 'query paths propagate get_shape's GeometryError with ?', 668182fd5d (export/tessellate), dea320330f (execute_split), 4348115507 (null-pointer message names the handle). git grep 'map_err(|_| (Query|Export|Tess)Error::InvalidHandle' in crates/reify-kernel-occt/src = 0; get_shape (lib.rs:873) doc now says 'Propagate with ?'. Remaining InvalidHandle hits are doc comments and tests.; task store: [('7379', 'done')]

findings.statement: The OCCT geometry warm-start machinery (impl WarmStartable for OcctKernel, about 250 lines) has no production consumer. Its own comment states that nothing outside the crate's tests sends OcctRequest::WarmState/WithWarmState; no `kernel.warm_state()` or `with_warm_state()` call on a geometry kernel exists in crates/*/src. It nevertheless shapes the kernel's state design: every OcctKernel field must be classified in three exhaustive destructures (reset, warm_state, with_warm_state). It also carries a debug completeness cross-check and a documented latent next_id-lowering aliasing hazard, and it absorbed 22 of the 110 lib.rs commits since 2026-07-06. Most of its prose is reviewer-answering (a 50-line justification of the bounded-payload filter, including "Verified at the time this filter was added (task #5162): no in-tree production caller").
findings.proposal: Either wire OCCT warm start into a real consumer, or reduce the impl to the trait's no-op (return None) behind the existing inventory registration and drop the persistence logic until a consumer exists.

findings.statement: Geometry kernel query replies for points, directions and bounding boxes (GeometryQuery::Centroid, BoundingBox, FaceNormal, EdgeTangent and others) cross the GeometryKernel seam as Value::String JSON text, and reify-eval decodes that text with four independent hand-rolled tokenizers: topology_selectors::parse_flat_number_object (wrapped by six pub(crate) parse_* functions and reached from geometry_ops, selector_vocabulary_v2 and engine_constraints), engine_build::parse_bbox_all_extents, primitive_attribute_seed::parse_normal_z and primitive_attribute_seed::parse_bbox_xyz_min. engine_build's own doc says parse_bbox_xyz_min 'parses the same format' and was left out of scope. Structured carriers already exist: Value::Point and Value::BoundingBox{min,max}. geometry_ops::dispatch_bounding_box turns the JSON string back into Value::BoundingBox. The parsers disagree on edge cases (parse_flat_number_object rejects unknown keys; the bbox_z variant tolerates the other four extents by an inline whitelist), and test mocks already carry a different shape ({"min":{..},"max":{..}} in harness_stress_scenarios/stress_query_consistency.rs) that the production parsers would reject.
findings.proposal: Make the GeometryKernel reply typed for these queries: kernels return Value::Point/Value::Vector/Value::BoundingBox (or a GeometryQueryReply enum), and the four tokenizers and six wrappers are deleted. dispatch_bounding_box becomes a pass-through.

findings.statement: Production realization goes through GeometryKernel::execute_with_history. engine_build.rs calls it at lines 836, 1125 and 8712, all before its #[cfg(test)] blocks. For OCCT, the decision of which ops have a history-aware primitive is made inside the kernel-thread match loop of OcctKernelHandle::spawn, not in OcctKernel, and that loop lowers the ops itself. It reads Extrude.distance, Fillet.radius and Chamfer.distance with Value::as_f64. OcctKernel::execute reads the same three fields through extract_length_f64, which runs reify_ir::check_length_field (the units-length tripwire) and emits the canonical non_numeric_kernel_field_message. So the production path is blind to the detector for these fields, and its error text ('fillet radius must be numeric') differs from the canonical one. The doc on OcctKernelHandle::execute_with_history says it is 'Channel-routed to the kernel thread's inherent OcctKernel::execute_with_history dispatcher', but no such method exists: git grep finds execute_with_history only in handle.rs, stubs.rs, reify-ir and test mocks.
findings.proposal: Move the op-to-history dispatch into lib.rs as OcctKernel::execute_with_history and share per-op field extraction (extract_length_f64 plus validation) with execute. The actor arm becomes a one-line forward like every other request.

findings.statement: Each kernel capability routed across the OCCT actor channel is written out by hand four or five times in handle.rs: an OcctRequest variant, an inherent sync method that builds it, an optional _async twin, a match arm in spawn() that unpacks it and calls OcctKernel, and a GeometryKernel trait method that forwards to the inherent method. The no-OCCT stubs.rs is a sixth copy, and it already lags: it defines neither measure_mesh_deviation nor make_compound, so those silently fall back to trait defaults in non-OCCT builds. This boilerplate is what makes handle.rs 1999 production lines.
findings.proposal: Replace the per-method enum with one closure request, Run(Box<dyn FnOnce(&mut OcctKernel) + Send>), behind a generic call<R>(f) -> Result<R, ChannelDied> and its async twin. Inherent methods become one-liners and the spawn loop becomes a single arm.

findings.statement: Selector resolution is implemented twice. resolve_with_attributes (live kernel) and resolve_against_carried_topology (kernel-free) each carry their own copy of the Union/Intersect/Difference composition with first-seen order and HashSet dedup. resolve_leaf_against_carried re-implements the ByNormal predicate of faces_by_normal 'byte-for-byte', so the PRD §7.2 two-way parity that the doc says holds 'by construction' actually depends on two copies staying identical. Inside resolve_leaf, the ByRole, CreatedByFeature and SplitByFeature arms repeat the same collect-filter-sort-map table walk three times. The resolver also closes a module cycle: resolve_leaf calls crate::selector_vocabulary_v2 twelve times, while selector_vocabulary_v2.rs imports seven names back from topology_selectors.
findings.proposal: Factor one generic compose(node, leaf_fn) over SelectorNode, used by both resolvers; extract a shared normal_within(normal, target, tol) predicate. Put the resolver in its own module above topology_selectors and selector_vocabulary_v2 so both become leaves.

findings.statement: The geometric-relation and motion-joint vocabularies are bare strings matched independently in three crates. is_motion_joint_cell_type hardcodes six joint type names that mirror reify-compiler's pub(crate) joint_signatures::joint_ctor_result_type. Its own doc says that adding a joint kind there without updating this list is 'silent drift, no compile error', and that the unit test pinning the list is 'tautological'. Relation names are matched the same way: RelationInstance.name is a String, and describe_demand routes on 'concentric'/'flush'/'tangent'/… with an `other => other.to_string()` fallback. reify-constraints dispatches residual forms on the same names, and reify-compiler relation_signatures.rs has at least four more match functions over them.
findings.proposal: Introduce RelationKind and JointKind enums in a crate both compiler and eval depend on. The compiler resolves names once; RelationInstance carries the enum, and every match becomes exhaustive.

findings.statement: The sketch slot-kind rule is stated twice. SketchConstraint::operands and SketchEntity::defining_refs in sketch.rs are declared 'the single statement of which slot takes which kind' and drive validate(). SystemBuilder::emit_sketch_constraint then re-resolves every operand through four nested per-kind lookups (point/curve/arc/line, plus the Fix arm), using string labels ('point', 'circle or arc', 'arc', 'line', 'point or line') that duplicate SketchSlotKind's Display. Both files admit the two 'describe the same rule in two places'. If they ever disagree, release builds log tracing::error and skip that constraint (the debug_assert fires only in debug). That is a partial lowering that still solves, which is exactly the outcome validate() exists to forbid.
findings.proposal: Have validate() return a ValidatedSketch whose constraints carry already-resolved typed operands (an EmittedEntity kind per slot), so the emitter matches on types rather than re-deriving kinds. The drift guards then become unreachable by construction and can be deleted.

findings.statement: In this slice's eval modules, production code is outweighed by prose, and the prose is largely reviewer-answering history rather than rationale the next agent needs: 'The divergence is deliberate and is pinned by…', 'Residual risk … accepted on the same terms', 'verified 2026-06-27', 'Do NOT fix the extra level…', 'Measured, not assumed, by…', 'This used to be a mirror… Task #6170 retired it'. classify_cell carries 181 doc lines and 24 body comment lines over 27 code lines. relate_solve's fix history since 2026-07-06 is dominated by repairs to this prose rather than to code.
findings.proposal: Move decision rationale to the cited PRDs (precision-nominal-representation-guarantee, declared-intent-consumption-accounting) and the measurement or defence prose to commit messages and task records. Leave each function a short contract plus a pointer.

findings.statement: tolerance_combine.rs is named and documented as the 'Output-occurrence × active-purpose tolerance combiner', but combine_demanded_tolerance is one of five unrelated responsibilities it hosts. The others: RepresentationWithin recognition, evaluation, C-BOUND bound table and export refusal; a trait-refinement walk (conforms_to_trait/conforms_to_output, consumed by bom_report); and Output export-spec extraction (OutputTarget/OutputExportSpec), which routes on string type and variant names ('OutputFormat', 'STEP', 'STL', 'ThreeMF', 'Display', 'STEPVersion', 'AP203', …). The trait walk and export-spec reader say they were co-located to satisfy a task directive ('share one Output-recognition path'). Nothing about tolerance connects them.
findings.proposal: Split along the five groups: representation_within.rs (matcher, eval, C-BOUND, refusal), output_spec.rs (typed from the compiled enum, not variant strings), the trait walk deleted in favour of reify_compiler::satisfies_trait_bound, and tolerance_combine keeping only combine_demanded_tolerance. Each split file passes heuristic 13 because the only cross-import is downward, from tolerance_scope to the matcher.

findings.statement: The achieved representation-deviation table is a BTreeMap<String, f64> keyed by an entity_path string (written in geometry_ops.rs at line 13219). eval_representation_within resolves a subject to a key two ways: realization_ref.to_string() on the value path, or a prefix scan through realization_belongs_to on the type path. realization_belongs_to's own doc says its grammar (first '#realization[' marker after a struct-name prefix) deliberately differs from reify_core::RealizationNodeId::FromStr, which splits on the last marker. It accepts that a sub-scoped 'Asm.part#realization[0]' is not matched (C-BOUND-2). So one identifier has two parsers with different answers, and the refine loop (#6171/#6168) must use the string predicate to stay in step.
findings.proposal: Key the table by RealizationNodeId (or a typed (struct, index) pair) and answer 'belongs to' with a typed comparison of entity components. Delete the string predicate.

findings.statement: conforms_to_trait re-implements the transitive trait-refinement check that reify_compiler::satisfies_trait_bound already provides. Its doc justifies this by saying the compiler functions 'are pub(crate) and unreachable from reify-eval'. That has been false since a4ad1bcfda (2026-06-12) made satisfies_trait_bound public, re-exported at reify-compiler/src/lib.rs:79. The eval copy was written a day earlier (4da1a1341b, 2026-06-11) and then generalized and given a second consumer (873616a313, 2026-06-26) without switching to the compiler function. Export-driver eligibility and BOM lifecycle classification therefore use a different walk from the compiler's conformance checker.
findings.proposal: Delete conforms_to_trait/conforms_to_output and call reify_compiler::satisfies_trait_bound with a registry built from module.trait_defs. Remove the false doc paragraph.

findings.statement: WarmStatePool's public interface has accreted back-compat wrappers, and the ones that silently reset cost_per_byte to 0.0 (the regression #3468 fixed) are still public with no production callers: donate_preserving_lru has none (engine_edit.rs only mentions it in docs, including a stale line-788 doc naming it for the cache-miss path while line 806 calls donate_preserving_lru_with_cost), and checkout_with_lru_stamp is called only from engine_edit's test module. The doc on contains() contrasts it with a retrieve method that does not exist. The production struct carries a #[cfg(test)] field (test_events_cap) and a test-only constructor seam.
findings.proposal: Remove the cost-dropping wrappers (or make cost a required argument), fix the stale docs, and move the test cap into a constructor parameter instead of a cfg(test) field.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: Removed by task #8753 (done). ec720e2574 deleted the cost-dropping donate_preserving_lru / checkout_with_lru_stamp wrappers. 34f6cf3896 replaced the cfg(test) test_events_cap field with the constructor parameter with_limits(budget, events_cap). The contains() doc no longer mentions retrieve. The no-cost donate() at warm_pool.rs:305 remains as a documented zero-cost entry point; it is not one of the finding's wrappers.; task store: [('8753', 'done')]

findings.statement: The reify-kernel-openvdb crate doc, the first thing a reader of the crate loads, states under '# v0.2 scope' that 'Real OpenVDB FFI is deferred to a follow-up task' and that the crate ships 'a stub OpenVdbKernel that returns descriptive errors'. The same lib.rs conditionally compiles kernel_real.rs: 988 lines of real libopenvdb 13.x FFI (realize_voxel_from_mesh, marching cubes, VDB I/O, densify_grid_to_sampled), which is what has_openvdb builds use.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the crate doc to describe the two cfg arms (kernel_real under has_openvdb, kernel stub otherwise) and drop the stale v0.2-scope paragraph.

findings.statement: Vector-, box- and kind-valued GeometryQuery results (Centroid, FaceNormal, EdgeTangent, BoundingBox, FaceSurfaceKind, EdgeCurveKind) cross the GeometryKernel seam as Value::String text. Each kernel hand-formats JSON with format!("{{\"x\":{}...}}"), and reify-eval re-parses it with an ad-hoc parser: topology_selectors::parse_flat_number_object does a naive split(',')/splitn(':') and rejects unknown keys. selector_vocabulary_v2 then picks a bbox axis by passing a b'x'/b'y'/b'z' byte tag (Axis::as_byte) into parse_bbox_axis_extents_json, which maps it to key strings. The typed shapes already exist on both sides of the seam: the cxx bridge declares `struct Point3 {x,y,z}` and `struct BBox {xmin..zmax}`, and reify-ir already has FaceSurfaceKind/EdgeCurveKind enums, which selector_vocabulary_v2 recovers through try_from_str. So the structure is serialized to text and re-parsed inside one process.
findings.proposal: Give these GeometryQuery variants typed result values (Value::Point/Vector, a BoundingBox value, Value::Enum for surface/curve kind) produced directly from the FFI Point3/BBox structs. Delete parse_flat_number_object and its siblings, and pass Axis, not a byte tag.

findings.statement: SolverRegistry::solve_inner, the single dispatch core for solve and solve_ranked, is mostly prose. Lines 349-794 are 58% comment lines (261 of 446). One 150-line comment block (lines 492-641) sits over a 7-line ResolutionProblem struct literal and narrates task history ('When task #5720 landed the filter…', 'LAYER 2 … CLOSES that gap'), a cost measurement ('roughly FOUR ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE'), and a rejected alternative ('Restructuring … would therefore trade a real drift guard'). Commit 86f79d3fa6 'docs(5721): record the measured spread-cost tradeoff at all three sites' put that measurement into code. The function also takes a `want_optimality: bool` flag and returns an unnamed 4-tuple (SolveResult, Option<OptimalityStatus>, Option<f64>, Option<Vec<RankedCandidate>>) whose slot meanings live only in its doc comment. It re-tests `auto_params.is_empty()` / `components.is_empty()` even though the prelude's ObjectiveConsumption verdict already encodes both.
findings.proposal: Move the history and measurements to the task records and commit messages, keeping a one-line pointer per invariant. Replace the 4-tuple with a named struct and the bool with an enum or two entry points, and branch the early exits on ObjectiveConsumption.

findings.statement: The geometric-relation vocabulary is a bare string (RelationInstance.name: String) matched independently in at least five places, with no shared enum: reify-compiler relation_signatures.rs (RELATION_FN_NAMES, relation_delta_dof, relation_delta_dof_kinds, relation_operand_datum), reify-constraints relate_solve.rs::residual_dispatch, and reify-eval relate_solve.rs's phrase match. residual_dispatch ends in `_ => Vec::new()`, so an unmatched name yields zero rows and the partition then files it as redundant. The single-metric operand is also derived differently on the two sides: constraints takes `scalars.last()` over non-datum operands, while the eval phrase builder takes `scalars.first()` over `sub.is_none()` operands. nominal_delta_dof travels as data only because relation_delta_dof is pub(crate). Pending #6669 (LoweringTable keyed by RelationKind) owns the residual side, but its files_to_modify list omits reify-eval/src/relate_solve.rs, the phrase-match site.
findings.proposal: Mint a RelationKind enum in reify-ir, parsed once by the compiler, carried on RelationInstance, and matched exhaustively in residual_dispatch and the eval phrase builder. Fold this into #6669's scope including reify-eval/src/relate_solve.rs.

findings.statement: SingleKernelHolder's INVARIANT comment says it 'must delegate EVERY GeometryKernel method' and that this is guarded by `delegates_all_capability_methods_to_inner_kernel`, which 'invokes every method through the holder'. Neither claim holds. The impl overrides 18 of the trait's 27 methods. Nine fall through to trait defaults: register_mesh_handle, volume_mesh, mesh_surface_to_volume, mesh_surface_to_volume_attributed, store_volume_mesh, closest_point_on_shape, vertex_point, realize_mesh_from_voxel, surface_options_content_hash. The parity test calls only the 18 forwarded ones. This is the same class task #4363 fixed for measure_mesh_deviation, so the defect has recurred as the trait grew.
findings.proposal: Add the nine forwarding overrides and extend the parity test to all of them. Better, make the test enumerate trait methods mechanically (e.g. a macro that generates both the forwards and the test), so a new trait method cannot be skipped.

findings.statement: The not(has_occt) stub surface is compiled by no gate step. Since #6343, check-manifold-deps.sh makes OCCT absence fatal on every RUN_RUST verify, and the stub's contract suite is `#[cfg(all(test, not(has_occt)))]`, so the INV-GEO-4 stub arm (assert_kernel_contract!(stub; …)) never runs in the merge gate. The bare stub OcctKernel mirrors 24 of the real type's 68 inherent pub fns ('Mirrors the real … signature so call sites compile'). Yet bare OcctKernel has zero non-comment references outside reify-kernel-occt, and inside the crate under not(has_occt) it is constructed only by stubs.rs's own tests. The mirror serves no compiled consumer, and nothing tells an agent whether it has drifted.
findings.proposal: Either add one cheap gate step that compiles and tests reify-kernel-occt with OCCT_LIB_DIR/INCLUDE_DIR emptied, or cut the stub to the consumed surface (OcctKernelHandle + GeometryKernel impl + factory) and delete the bare OcctKernel mirror.

findings.statement: The shared kernel-seam contract suite (reify-test-support assert_kernel_contract!: dangling-handle taxonomy, query_many length invariant, extract determinism) has a stub arm and a B-rep-shaped real arm (it assumes extract_* succeeds on a valid Box). Only OCCT instantiates it. FidgetKernel and ManifoldKernel, both registered production kernels, dropped assert_stub_kernel_errors! when they gained real ops and replaced it with a hand-written Send+Sync test. No shared contract fits a non-B-rep kernel, so Fidget's error taxonomy is pinned by nothing shared. Its invalid-handle errors differ by path: execute gives InvalidReference, evaluate_sdf_at gives QueryFailed, iso_mesh gives TessError::InvalidHandle, and query answers QueryFailed for every input.
findings.proposal: Split assert_kernel_contract! into a representation-neutral core (Send+Sync, dangling-handle taxonomy, query_many length) and a B-rep extension. Instantiate the core for Fidget, Manifold, Gmsh and OpenVDB.

findings.statement: Builtin diagnostics form a second name-keyed axis that the builtin registry does not cover. reify-stdlib re-exports 10 per-family `diagnose` classifiers (stackup, dfm, tolerancing, fea, geometry, orientation, flexure, dynamics, snapshot …). Each is hand-wired into one of four reify-expr functions: emit_undef_builtin_diagnostics (post-Undef only), emit_flexure_diagnostics, emit_dfm_diagnostics, emit_snapshot_diagnostics (both-path). Which bucket a family belongs to, and the claim that 'the six name families … are disjoint', are stated only in comments. docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md has no diagnostic column, so the family-by-family migration leaves this axis string-keyed. A family without a hook fails silently: eval_sweep has 29 `Value::Undef` exits with no diagnose classifier, so every malformed sweep/dim/sweep_grid call yields a bare undef.
findings.proposal: Add a diagnostic column (kind + hook) to the builtin registry row, or a single stdlib-side `diagnose(name, args, result) -> Vec<Diagnostic>` that dispatches internally, so reify-expr calls one function.

findings.statement: Joint kind is a string field on a Value::Map ('kind' => "prismatic"/"revolute"/…). The kind-to-motion-dimension mapping is re-matched in sweep.rs twice (driving_joint_kind and wrap_value_for_driving_joint, each with a dead "planar" arm), in snapshot.rs (wrap_midpoint_for_joint, wrap_jointvalue_for_joint), in loop_closure.rs::value_for_joint (93.8% line-similar to snapshot's wrap_jointvalue_for_joint), and in dynamics/eval.rs. All this while a typed JointKind enum exists in loop_closure_value.rs, whose from_str doc says 'if a new kind is added there, a variant must be added here too'. sweep.rs also reaches its siblings by string name through the 24-family fall-through chain (eval_builtin("bind"), eval_builtin("snapshot")). The in-flight #7188 branch (SingleDofKind) touches joints.rs and snapshot.rs only, and pending #7974 names loop_closure.rs only. Neither names sweep.rs.
findings.proposal: Have #7188's SingleDofKind (or JointKind) be the only kind parser, and route sweep.rs's two helpers through it in the same consolidation as #7974. Call snapshot/bind kernels directly rather than via eval_builtin strings.

findings.statement: Within reify-constraints, `collect_value_refs` names two traversals with different rules. dependent_reads::collect_value_refs (via CompiledExpr::walk) collects ValueRef only and descends into Lambda bodies. The IR method CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs() also collects CrossSubGeometryRef and, for Lambda, emits captures without descending. Decomposition connectivity, objective expansion and the dependent-cell analysis use the first. lib.rs's undef classification and solver.rs's bound-derivation MENTIONS test (collect_underivable_in_leaf) use the second. The free fn's doc mentions only the CrossSubGeometryRef difference.
findings.proposal: Rename the free fn to say what it collects (e.g. plain_value_refs), and decide and document whether lambda-body refs count, in one place.

findings.statement: The Sdf/Voxel arm of project_realization_read_handle bypasses the three helpers the other content arms share (resolve_realization_kernel, memoize_projection, degrade_projection). It inlines its own memoize and two degrade tails, and resolves the kernel by the hard-coded openvdb_kernel_name() rather than node_data.produced_kernel. The surrounding prose is stale. The module header says 'γ … will REPLACE the Mesh/VolumeMesh arms', but γ has landed. degrade_projection's doc says it is shared with 'the not-yet-wired Sdf / Voxel arm', which is wired and does not call it. RealizationProjectionStore and its get/insert carry `#[allow(dead_code)] // … silenced until step-4 wires it` although project_realization_read_handle now calls both.
findings.proposal: Route the Sdf/Voxel arm through memoize_projection/degrade_projection, resolving the kernel from produced_kernel. Delete the stale allows and header lines.

findings.statement: sub_consumers_the_reverse_index_drops re-implements the reverse index's GeomRef::Sub resolver (deps.rs resolve_geom_sub_edge / resolve_sub_ref / resolve_sibling_ref). It routes on the same meaningful string, a '.' in the operand selects cross-entity vs same-entity, using its own split_once('.') and its own exporter map. The two are kept in step by a mirror test (the_dropped_operand_rule_agrees_with_the_reverse_index), not by sharing code, although both live in reify-eval and the resolver is only module-private.
findings.proposal: Expose a pub(crate) `deps::sub_operand_resolves(name, consumer, &member_index) -> bool` and call it here. Longer term, give GeomRef::Sub a structured {sub: Option<..>, member} payload.

findings.statement: Operation history crosses the cxx bridge as one accessor fn per (op family × face/edge × modified/generated/deleted [+caps/counts]), each returning a flat Vec<u32> in 'groups of 3' / 'groups of 2' layouts described in comments. Four opaque history types (boolean, local_feature, loft, sweep) carry 37 such accessor declarations. lib.rs repeats the six-accessor decode block at every call site (sweep's appears at three call sites alone). cxx shared structs can carry Vec fields, as TessResult already does in this bridge.
findings.proposal: Return one cxx shared struct OpHistoryRecords {face_modified, face_generated, face_deleted, edge_*, caps…} per history type, decoded by one Rust function.

findings.statement: The file's subject is the slot-timeout emission contract: Sections A, B, C and H, about 804 lines and 67 asserts. Sections D, E, F and G are 3,413 of its 4,384 lines (78%) and 76 asserts. They implement a line-oriented regex static analyzer over every tests/infra test_*.sh plus its .py sibling, made of 29 named F_*/G_* ERE constants, a worklist fixed-point invocation closure, an exec-forwarding-lib rule, bash and Python diversion dialects, and a two-pass awk block scanner. It is maintained by hand through a 12-entry D_ROSTER and a 9-row, three-array, index-aligned G_MEMBERS/G_SITE/G_SCAN table. The analyzer exists only so that no infra test's stderr carries the column-0 string `@@REIFY_SLOT_TIMEOUT@@`, because dark-factory classifies a verify by grepping log text for it. Section H's own preamble calls this per-site layer 'whack-a-mole by construction', with run_all.sh's re-emission sanitizer as the systemic backstop.
findings.proposal: Move the classification boundary to structured data. Have slot_acquire write its timeout event to a dedicated fd or event file (as run_all's pool worker already does via inherited fd 2), not as a grep-able column-0 log line, and have dark-factory read that channel. The per-member leak analyzer (D4, F, G) can then be deleted, with Section H's sanitizer kept as the only defence for legacy text. Until then, extract Sections D-G into one scripts/ tool with its own tests, so the slot-contract file stops depending on every other test's source.

findings.statement: The suite's lane-isolation invariants (no seed invocation writes the machine-shared /tmp/.reseed-trash, no lane is bare /tmp) are asserted exactly once, at a fixed position in Block R: R1 `_assert_no_shared_trash_use`, R3 and R6 `_assert_no_bare_tmp_lanes`. Blocks W (task 6889, 2026-08-30) and X (task 7227, 2026-09-10) were later appended after Block R. They make 7 seed invocations that no detector observes, which is the failure Block R's own ordering note warns about, guarded only by that note. The five sibling warm-lane suites run the filesystem guard `assert_no_shared_trash_litter` as their last assertion. This suite never calls it against the real shared trash; it uses it only in R8's redirected control.
findings.proposal: Run the suite-wide detectors from one end-of-suite hook, a cleanup or test_summary wrapper that calls `_assert_no_shared_trash_use`, `_assert_no_bare_tmp_lanes` and `assert_no_shared_trash_litter`, so placement cannot matter. That makes the suite uniform with its five siblings.

findings.statement: test_test_helpers.sh is the unit test for test_helpers.sh, yet about 750 lines (622-1372) hold 89 check() calls that grep the source of seven other files. The checks cover the CONSUMERS list, tests/sync_comments_test.sh and tests/infra/sync_ref_helpers.sh, and assert refactor-era shapes: 'does NOT define assert() locally', 'has no defensive non-empty guard', '[ -z "$ref_fn" ]' present. At least three checks pin comment text: 'has cross-directory sourcing comment' (grep -B3 ... 'test script.*not.*build'), 'head -1 pipeline has single-reference documentation comment', and 'test_helpers.sh documents pipeline divergence'. tests/infra/README.md 'Assert behaviour, not source prose' forbids exactly this. test_run_all.sh Test 6 does the same to itself: five asserts grep the file's own source that dead variables `t2_rc`/`t3_rc` stay removed.

findings.statement: Tests 19 and 25 reach into run_all.sh's private pool bookkeeping. They point TMPDIR at a private dir because, as they note, `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/reify-run-all-pool.XXXXXX"` is 'the ONLY use of TMPDIR in run_all.sh'. They then glob `reify-run-all-pool.*`, scan `*.rc` while skipping `*.retry.rc`, and gate on non-empty content because run_all 'opens each .rc file with > (truncate) and then writes the exit code as a separate step'. The test describes this as a mirror of `_ra_partial_failed_names`' read logic. None of this is a declared interface of run_all.sh.
findings.proposal: Give run_all.sh a declared observation seam for tests, such as a REIFY_RUN_ALL_EVENT_LOG file receiving one structured line per member start and finish, and have T19 and T25 wait on that seam, not on the workdir layout.

findings.statement: Scenarios (d), (e), (f) and (g) are copy-transpositions of one recipe: git-init repo, marker assembled from vars, inline sqlite3 CREATE TABLE plus seed, run, UPDATE to pending, rerun, sentinel. Scenarios (e), (f) and (g) emit @@HARDGATE_E/F/G_PASSED@@ sentinels, with comments claiming they fix silent_pass_on_failure, but no consumer exists. test_reify_audit_ptodo_orphan_hardgate.sh greps only C and D, so the stale-binary property is unpinned for (e) through (g).

Then either have orphan_hardgate.sh assert every emitted sentinel, or drop the unconsumed ones.

findings.statement: Each block hand-rolls the base fixture: base parent via mktemp under bare /tmp, `_TMPDIRS+=`, `mkdir -p`, and an empty `printf 'RUSTFLAGS=\nINVOCATION=\n' > .warm-base-meta` sidecar. findings.statement: Assertions K and L derive verify.sh's role -> profile -> binding-wall semantics by regex and awk over verify.sh's SOURCE TEXT, not through any behaviour verify.sh exposes. The accepted role set is split out of the unknown-role error message string ('want task|merge|offline|background', verify.sh:949). The per-role PROFILE default comes from an awk window over the `if [ "$PROFILE_EXPLICIT" -eq 0 ]` if/elif block (verify.sh:887). The walls come from column-0 regexes on `_VERIFY_TEST_TIMEOUT="$(_resolve_timeout_knob ... 60m` (verify.sh:532-533) and from an `if [ "${DF_VERIFY_ROLE:-x}" = "y" ]; then ... fi` window. The heavy-excluded roles come from a `_GATE_HEAVY_EXCLUDE=""` ... `^fi$` window (verify.sh:970). Residual acceptance is read out of a COMMENT paragraph in .config/nextest.toml (`# ACCEPTED RESIDUAL` entry lines). The file's non-vacuity half then sed-mutates copies of verify.sh to prove those parsers still bite. The same walls are already rendered and asserted behaviourally through `verify.sh --print-plan` per role in test_occt_flock_gate.sh (T1-T18-BG). So the fact has two oracles, one behavioural and one a shadow parser.
findings.proposal: Give verify.sh one structured query, for example `verify.sh --print-role-walls` emitting `role profile debug_wall_s release_wall_s heavy_excluded` rows computed by the same code that renders the plan, or derive the same facts from the per-role --print-plan renders test_occt_flock_gate.sh already captures. Move the residual allowlist out of a TOML comment into a data key or manifest row. K/L then compare data, and the 8 extractors plus 5 mutators go away.

findings.statement: NativeDep's discovery data is declared twice: once in Rust match arms (include/lib candidates in priority order, include/lib sentinels, the /snap/freecad fallback root and its sentinel->subdir map, the empty-override rule) and once as a hand-kept bash mirror in scripts/check-manifold-deps.sh marker blocks. Parity is enforced by tests/infra/test_occt_deps_preflight.sh, which parses lib.rs as TEXT with awk anchored on `fn <name>`, a 4-space `^    }$` closing brace, quote-splitting of string literals, `let snap_subdir = match sentinel`, and `// BEGIN native-dep-variants` comment markers. lib.rs's doc comments exist largely to explain this arrangement. Inside find_dir_with_override, the snap fallback dispatches on the sentinel STRING ('Standard_Failure.hxx' / 'libTKernel.so') rather than on the NativeDep variant. If OCCT's sentinel is renamed consistently on both sides, both snap maps still agree with each other, parity stays green, and the fallback goes dead in both.
findings.proposal: Hold the per-dep table in one data file, for example crates/reify-build-utils/native-deps.tsv or .toml, with columns dep, env names, candidates, sentinels and snap subdir. lib.rs reads it with include_str! and parses it once, and check-manifold-deps.sh reads the same file. Parity then holds by construction, the six source parsers and the mirror prose go away, and the snap fallback becomes a per-dep column keyed by variant, not by sentinel text.

findings.statement: The file is named and headed for scripts/cargo-test-occt-gated.sh, yet 867 of its 1,368 lines (129-995) are verify.sh --print-plan contracts for timeout knobs and role walls (Tests 10-13, 17, 17b and T1-T18-BG). Those are unrelated to the wrapper, which .config/nextest.toml says is 'NO LONGER invoked by verify.sh'. The file runs two overlapping numbering series (Test 14-17 for the wrapper, T14-T17 for verify.sh), and a prose NOTE is needed to tell them apart. Two of its wrapper checks pin comments rather than code: Test 5 (`grep -q 'flock -x'`) and Test 7 (`grep -q 'exec'`) match only comment lines in the wrapper, so they turn red on a reworded comment and stay green on a code regression. scripts/occt-touching-crates.txt and scripts/release-sensitive-crates.txt still describe the wrapper as 'the flock wrapper used for gated passes' and 'used for the OCCT-touching release crate (reify-eval) which stays flock-gated in release'.
findings.proposal: Move the T-series and Tests 10-13/17/17b into a verify-timeout-knobs test, and carry occt_plan_grep_or_dump into plan_capture_lib.sh under a neutral name. Delete the comment-matching source greps, since Tests 8/9/18 already drive the behaviour. Correct the two crate-list headers.

findings.statement: One 2,645-line file holds three things with three purposes. (1) A guard ENGINE: 10 functions from _wallclock_assert_roots to _wallclock_uncovered_test_roots, 662 lines of which 440 are comments. (2) That engine's hermetic self-test suite: Sections 1, 2 and 4a-4f, about 1,500 lines. (3) The live gate: Section 3, with _LIVE_ROOTS, the baseline and _ESC_ALLOWLIST_SIZE. 1,426 of its 2,645 lines (53.9%) are comments, and much of that prose answers reviewers: the history of a #6438 review pass, 'an earlier draft', 'considered and rejected', 'Verified before this was fixed', dated measurements. Under the Comments stance that belongs in commit messages or the PRD. Sibling guards in this directory already separate engine from test (harness-layout-lib.sh, nextest_absent_lib.sh, cited-test-path-lib.sh).
findings.proposal: Split along the h14 partition recorded below. tests/infra/wallclock_rust_guard_lib.sh takes the engine; a test_wallclock_rust_guard_lib.sh sources it and runs Sections 1, 2 and 4a-4f; Section 3 stays as test_no_new_wallclock_rust_deadlines.sh and sources the lib. Each import goes downward, so there is no h13 symptom. Rehome the review history to commit messages or the PRD and keep the rule statements at the engine.

findings.statement: find() reads two env vars per dep (include_env, lib_env, both private), but declares neither as a cargo rerun input, and it does not own the has_<dep> cfg either. So every consumer re-derives the cfg by hand: 10 `cargo:rustc-cfg=has_<dep>` sites plus 10 matching check-cfg declarations across 8 build.rs files. The 3 kernel build.rs files hand-write 6 env-name literals (OCCT_INCLUDE_DIR and the rest) that duplicate the private include_env/lib_env. emit_rpath_* declares rerun only for lib_env. So reify-cli, reify-eval, reify-kernel-conformance, reify-mesh-morph and gui/src-tauri, which gate has_<dep> on find(), do not re-run when only *_INCLUDE_DIR changes, while the kernel crates do. has_<dep> can then disagree between a kernel and its consumer, and the consumer's cfg(has_<dep>) tests drop out silently: the silent-vacuity class this crate's own doc warns about. reify-mesh-morph's build.rs says its RPATH half 'is copied from crates/reify-solver-elastic/build.rs'.
findings.proposal: Add a single entry point, for example `pub fn detect(dep: NativeDep) -> Option<LibLoc>`. It emits rerun-if-env-changed for both envs, the check-cfg declaration and `cargo:rustc-cfg=has_<dep>`, with the cfg name derived from NativeDep. Kernels and consumers call it in place of the hand-rolled blocks, and the env literals are dropped from the kernel build.rs files.

findings.statement: The file captures both verify.sh plans with a single shot, `$(bash verify.sh ... --print-plan | grep -v '^#')`. That is the capture shape task 6247 retired in test_occt_flock_gate.sh, because a truncated capture under load reads as 'pattern absent' and fires a misleading contract failure instead of a retry. tests/infra/plan_capture_lib.sh (capture_print_plan + plan_capture_complete) is the shared fix, yet 38 of the 52 infra tests that invoke --print-plan do not use it. Separately, sections hD-hH (lines 155-858, about 700 of 1,179) re-test brace-depth, string, char-literal and cfg(test) lexer behaviour that now belongs to scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh (task 6202). That behaviour is already tested by test_rust_production_view_lib.py and again in test_compute_trampoline_registration_wired.sh.
findings.proposal: Route this file's two plan captures through capture_print_plan/plan_capture_complete, and make that the one capture form, for example a lint over tests/infra that flags a raw `--print-plan |` capture. Trim hD-hH to a wiring smoke (the gate uses the lib, as hN already proves) and leave the lexer matrix to the lib's own test.

findings.statement: This 2,140-line bash file mixes three test populations. (1) Behavioural daemon tests that start and kill the real balancer on mktemp FIFOs (Blocks 1-4, 11, 12, 16, 18, 19, 19b). (2) 13 Python heredocs that importlib-load scripts/jobserver-balancer.py and call its functions directly, including the private `_transfer_burst` (4 call sites), with 590 lines of Python embedded in bash. (3) grep-the-source checks over scripts/setup-dev.sh and scripts/verify.sh (Blocks 5, 6, 17, 23), which do not test the balancer at all. Population (2) is the shape the CLAUDE.md policy routes to a stdlib-unittest .py, and its private-name reach is a Tests-stance interface smell.
findings.proposal: Move population (2) into tests/infra/test_jobserver_balancer_units.py, a stdlib unittest that imports the module once, plus the required .sh wrapper and manifest row. Expose `_transfer_burst` publicly or test it through decide(). Move population (3) to a setup-dev test. The bash file keeps the daemon behaviour (see h14 partition).

findings.statement: run_all.sh runs members in four top-level branches: H9 --scope host-infra, REIFY_RUN_ALL_MEMBER_SUBSET, the concurrent pool and the legacy serial path. Each branch has its own inline copy of member invocation and PASS/FAIL recording. Cross-cutting concerns were added branch by branch instead of through one runner. Output re-emission through _ra_emit_sanitized runs in 2 of 4 branches (subset, pool), _ra_collect_fail_detail in 2 of 4 (subset, pool), and the worktree-removal check _ra_interrupt_if_worktree_gone in 2 of 4 (pool, legacy). The H3 host-infra exclusion runs in 2 of 4, retry and content-skip in 1 of 4. Each gap is documented in prose: the sanitizer header lists its site scope as 'NOT --scope host-infra (H9) and NOT the legacy'. Several later commits exist only to carry a feature into another branch: 3ef7845834 'collect FAIL-detail on the subset retry path', 7439d071b2 'sanitize subset branch re-emit', 746b4474ea 'wire the git-env scrub into both execution sites', 889910ef1d 'apply both slot rules at _ra_collect_fail_detail, the second site'. The helper functions also talk to the branches through shell globals rather than arguments. _ra_skip_engine rewrites the pool branch's _h2_discovered_list in place. _ra_skip_state_write reads `failures`. _ra_partial_failed_names reads _H2_WORKDIR and _h2_discovered_list.
findings.proposal: Write one `_ra_run_member <name> <capture-file> [opts]` that spawns (scrub, FD hygiene, env isolation), captures, sanitizes, records rc, and collects fail detail. Turn the four branches into member-list producers plus a scheduling policy (serial, concurrent, retry-once) that call it. Pass the discovered list and the results to the skip, ledger and term helpers as arguments, not globals.

findings.statement: test_harness_kloc_cap.sh is a test file, but it is also the merge-gate guard's implementation and the normative home of the harness-layout contract. Lines 387-1175 define the rule functions (_emit, harness_layout_violations, run_harness_layout_scan, harness_path_attr_violations, harness_undeclared_member_violations, harness_stale_selector_violations, harness_layout_orphan_rows, harness_layout_malformed_rows, harness_warn_ratchet_violations) plus the CAP_LINES, WARN_PCT and _KLOC_WARN_KNOWN ratchet data. Lines 1175-3307 test them and then run them over the live tree. The shared lib harness-layout-lib.sh holds only part of the logic. The test's rule functions call the lib's underscore-private helpers (_harness_layout_mod_decls, _harness_layout_norm_path, _harness_layout_row_crate) and read their out-param globals (_HL_NORM_OUT, _HL_ROW_CRATE). The test also defines its own helpers under the same `_harness_layout_*` prefix (_harness_layout_row_exists, _harness_layout_row_in_scope, _harness_layout_scan_baseline_rows), so a reader cannot tell lib-owned from test-owned names. The roughly 295-line C1/C2 contract header (naming, the #[path] mandate, I1-I3, the verdict grammar consumed by run_all.sh's fail-detail regex) is cited as the canonical source by 35 files under crates/. The two ratchets use different mechanisms: the grandfather baseline is a manifest file, while the WARN-set ratchet is an in-script array that each harness-split task edits (2c9e3315fe, 93afaf6631, 35fbd8ea98).
findings.proposal: Move the rule functions and the ratchet data into a guard lib, either harness-layout-lib.sh or a harness-layout-guard-lib.sh that sources it. Give the lib's helpers public names (or have the functions return values) so callers stop reading _HL_* globals. Rehome the C1/C2 contract to docs/ and point the 35 crate headers there. Keep test_harness_kloc_cap.sh as the hermetic self-test plus live scan.

findings.statement: The predicate that decides what run_all.sh discovers (glob test_*.sh, skip a non-file, exclude test_helpers.sh) has four separate implementations: classification_discovered_set (used by the pool branch and the manifest coverage guard), and three inline loops in run_all.sh (the SUBSET_COUNT_ONLY probe, the member-subset branch and the legacy branch). The H9 branch uses a fifth predicate: the manifest bucket intersected with files present. The lib's header says it 'mirrors run_all.sh's for-loop exactly' and that 'H2 will refactor run_all.sh's discovery to consume this function directly'. That refactor happened for the pool branch only. run_all.sh says the count-only and subset predicates 'MUST stay in sync'. The repetition is visible enough that a Python test docstring (test_flake_density_report.py) cites the three glob lines by number. Because discovery globs only test_*.sh, each Python test also needs a hand-copied .sh wrapper (7 read, 32-40 lines each, about 10 of them code) and a manifest row. Four of the Python tests also carry the same 10-line importlib loader.
findings.proposal: Have every run_all.sh branch and the count-only probe consume classification_discovered_set (or one `run_all_discover` in the lib), with the subset and H3 filters applied to its output. Once discovery lives in one place, #7445 becomes one change, and the wrapper template can then be retired or generated.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: run_all.sh now discovers through classification_discovered_set only (single call site at the discovery block, ~1643); the inline loops were deleted by 0786e24773 (#8678), and adoption-ratchet.manifest row 'inline-discovery-loop' (ceiling 0, tests/infra/run_all.sh) holds it. The symbol is still present but the multi-home cost is gone.; task store: [('8678', 'done')]

findings.statement: The ROW decision policy is split across Python and bash, and the copies have drifted. cpu_gov_instrument.slowdown_within_bound (floor <= s <= k*floor and s < 10) is called only by its own _selftest, which Cycle SELF asserts on. The live ROW3-1 verdict instead uses the bash _row3_within_bound (s <= k*floor and s < 10, with no floor check), even though its comment calls it 'the SINGLE source of truth'. psi_below_band, which per its docstring mirrors cpu-admit.sh, also has no caller outside the selftest. The ROW1-1-VACUITY-1/2 assertions re-implement the saturation comparison in inline awk instead of calling the comparison the live ROW1-1 assert uses, so changing the production comparison would not fail them. That contrasts with the ROW3 bound, which was extracted to prevent exactly that. The instrument also re-exports jobserver-tuning-harness's private _read_proc_stat, and SELF-3 pins it as a 're-export contract', yet no consumer imports it through the instrument. The header documents the knob REIFY_CPU_GOV_TEST_MIXFACTOR as 'UNUSED', and nothing reads it.
findings.proposal: Give each ROW verdict one predicate with one home, preferably the Python instrument, where it can be unit-tested. Delete slowdown_within_bound and psi_below_band or route the bash calls through them. Point the vacuity asserts at the production predicate. Drop the _read_proc_stat re-export, its SELF-3 pin and the dead knob doc.

findings.statement: The policy for adding OCCT and deps-tree directories to LD_LIBRARY_PATH is copied into four places, and the copies do different things. The cargo runner prepends both the FreeCAD snap dir and /opt/reify-deps/lib. scripts/run-gui.sh, which says it 'Mirrors .cargo/run-with-occt.sh', prepends only the snap dir. gui/test/visual/lib_e2e_smoke.sh, which says it 'mirrors the .cargo/run-with-occt.sh logic', prepends only the deps dir. scripts/verify.sh computes its own phase-scoped export. The runner's rationale is false at this tree: it says 'No rpath is baked in', but reify-build-utils::emit_rpath_for_tests and emit_rpath_for_bins emit -Wl,-rpath from six crate build.rs files. It frames /opt/reify-deps as where 'OCCT 7.9 is installed', while CLAUDE.md's OCCT invariant says reify links system OCCT 7.8 and 7.9 is only gmsh-transitive. verify.sh's own scope contract calls /opt/reify-deps/lib 'a whole conda prefix' that is 'HOSTILE to every non-Rust subprocess', and the runner exports it to every cargo-run binary and that binary's children.
findings.proposal: Put the decision in one sourced helper that prints the dirs to prepend and their order, with the 7.8/7.9 and RUNPATH facts stated once in docs. Have the runner, run-gui.sh and lib_e2e_smoke.sh call it, and either state in the helper why verify.sh's phase scoping differs or derive verify.sh's value from it too. Correct the 'No rpath' claim.

findings.statement: The file is named for, and its header describes, the INV-FEA-1 trampoline-registration drift guard (Part A, lines 1-~1430). About 590 lines of it (Part B, '(b0)'-'(b15)') test something else: that scripts/verify.sh's test plan executes the reify-gui --features gui suite. That covers semaphore bracketing, timeout wrapping, FD close, narrowing on --scope branch/staged, a closure that fails wide, and --test-threads pass-through. A sibling member, test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh, already tests the gui-feature compile-check region of the same verify.sh plan. Part B shares only the TEST_PLAN_FULL capture with Part A. It also cites verify.sh line numbers (verify.sh:2223, verify.sh:1853-1862) that no longer point at the cited code; the compile-check line is now at 4088.
findings.proposal: Move Part B into its own member, e.g. test_verify_gui_feature_test_pass.sh, beside test_verify_gui_feature_check.sh. It needs one extra --print-plan capture. Replace the verify.sh line cites with the function or marker they mean.

In run_all.sh, all 11 self-citations (9 distinct numbers) are stale: ':274' for _ra_emit_sanitized (now ~555), ':384' for lane_x_flock_release (now ~1426), ':517' for the EXIT trap (now ~1725), ':230'/':231' for _RA_INBOUND_ROLE, ':461', ':1440'/':1452' for the subset site, and 'lines ~988-997' for the Summary emit block (now ~2059).
