findings.statement: verify.sh exposes its scope classification to tests only as the prose comment line '# scope decision — RUN_RUST=$RUN_RUST RUN_GUI=$RUN_GUI RUN_OCCT_GATE=$RUN_OCCT_GATE RUN_GUI_VITEST=$RUN_GUI_VITEST' (scripts/verify.sh, plan-header emission). test_verify_scope.sh asserts on it by grepping the unanchored ORDERED substring. The field order is therefore a contract enforced only by a comment in verify.sh: 'every existing assertion greps this as the unanchored substring … survives a trailing append and does not survive a reordering', with the same note for the narrowing line. Plan_capture_lib has a typed per-field reader for exactly one field (plan_narrow_active). Every other field, and command-order claims such as freshness-before-cargo in test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh, are read by substring or byte offset (ts_offset_of / ts_last_offset_of on 'cargo ') over prose plan text. GUI-lane assertions pin literal shell text ('cd gui && .*npm ci && npm run typecheck'').
findings.proposal: Emit the scope decision as a machine-readable record, either a stable '# scope-kv' line with unordered key=value tokens or a --print-plan=json mode. Give plan_capture_lib a plan_scope_field <dump> <NAME> reader, and make assertions compare per field. Express leaf-ordering assertions over a parsed leaf list rather than byte offsets in prose.

findings.statement: The e2e suite's tree-sitter readiness gate re-implements tree-sitter-generate.sh's 'up to date' predicate. It is meant to guarantee that every nested verify.sh hits generate.sh's fast path, which was its fix for flake mode-1, per-section regeneration under load. The copy has gone stale. generate.sh's _stamp_is_current now also requires src/.generated_outputs.stamp to exist, name exactly the three outputs, and hash-match each on disk (#6992, 904a069a44, 2026-09-06). _ts_ready_check checks only that the outputs are non-empty and that the grammar hash matches. The suite's own 'healthy' fixture (_make_fake_ts_dir healthy) writes no outputs manifest, so its unit tests pin the stale predicate. The file was edited again on 2026-10-07 (a612418e0a) without the drift being noticed. Its comments cite tree-sitter-generate.sh:50-63 and :167-172, and both now land on unrelated code (the OUTPUTS_STAMP_FILE declaration and _write_stamps).
findings.proposal: Give tree-sitter-generate.sh a read-only --check mode (exit 0 iff _stamp_is_current) and have ensure_tree_sitter_ready call it rather than restate it. Build the e2e fake fixtures by running the real generate script or through ts_outputs_manifest_lib.

findings.statement: Every --print-plan sandbox hand-copies verify.sh's transitive source closure, one cp line per lib. copy_list_preflight_lib.sh already computes that closure (derive_source_closure), but callers use it only to ASSERT the hand list is complete, never to produce it. Inside test_verify_scope.sh, make_fixture and make_branch_fixture carry byte-identical 20-line cp blocks. Across tests/infra the same list exists at 8 build sites, which is why one new source line in verify.sh costs N edits.
findings.proposal: Add copy_verify_sandbox <dest> to copy_list_preflight_lib.sh: it copies derive_source_closure's output plus a declared data-file list, then runs the assert. Every sandbox builder calls it, so there is one inventory and the hand lists disappear.

findings.statement: test_tree_sitter_pipeline.sh is one of only 2 test_*.sh members that run their own harness instead of test_helpers.sh (test_slot_timeout_marker.sh is the other). Its failures print '  ASSERTION FAILED: …' followed by a bare 'FAIL' line. run_all.sh's _ra_collect_fail_detail extracts only '^\s*FAIL:' or '<TOKEN> FAIL' lines; it feeds the FAILED-DETAIL block that verify.sh and the merge-gate block reason quote. So when this member fails at the merge tier, the detail block is empty. Simulated: the extractor regex matches 0 lines of this harness's failure output and 1 of test_helpers' output. The harness also discovers cases with `declare -F | awk '/test_/'`, so any function whose name merely contains 'test_' (including one in a sourced lib) runs as a test. That rule is kept only by three warning comments here and a header promise in ts_outputs_manifest_lib.sh. Assertions are hand-rolled if/echo/return blocks inside 400-460-line functions, so the first failing sub-case hides every later one.
findings.proposal: Move the file onto test_helpers.sh's assert/test_summary. Keep run_guarded_cargo_check's tri-state as a small adapter that maps to assert. Split each numbered sub-case of the large functions into its own asserted step so a failure names itself and the later steps still run.

findings.statement: warm-lane-audit.sh reads two dark-factory-produced records with hand-written parsers: _record_scalar (sed) for .lane-state/<lane>.json, and _plan_anchor, an awk tokenizer that walks plan.json in document order. The test fixtures reproduce the producer's byte layout by hand and say which details are load-bearing. make_plan copies plan_tools.py's json.dumps(indent=2) shape, notes that `prerequisites` must precede `steps` because 'plain document order is what gives the anchor scan its … traversal', and writes pending commits as unquoted null. make_lane_state copies LaneRecord.to_json's field order, and L_CASES hard-codes LaneState's six values. No reify test reads a record the real producer wrote. The lane-state reader has a compact-form case; the plan.json reader has none. Its make_plan_raw cases cover only truncated, not-json and escaped-prose input.
findings.proposal: Check in a golden plan.json and lane-state record produced by dark-factory's real serialisers and refreshed by a DF-side test, then drive the audit over it. Alternatively, let the audit parse JSON with python3 -I when it is present and fall back to the hand parsers. Either way, add a compact and a key-reordered plan.json case.

findings.statement: The navigation prose in this slice's large files is unverified and has mostly rotted. File:line cites into large scripts are nearly all wrong: every verify.sh line cite now lands on unrelated code. Examples: verify.sh:1283 for the tree-sitter-generate leaf, now 3858; :3636/:3661 for the plan markers, now 4559/4593; :718/:725 for the scope diff sites, now 1751/1758. The six 'caller obligation, scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh:63-79' cites now point at the FD-9 lock contract, while the obligation text is at line 85. gc.sh 'line 417/461' are now 600/500, and run-all-classification.manifest:229 now names another member. Header block indexes omit most blocks: warm_lane_audit lists 1 of 20, warm_lane_pool 6 of 16, warm_lane_gc 16 of 17 (no H). The slice also carries 18 esc-NNNN pointers as rationale, which no dispatched role can read. test_verify_scope.sh states the policy once ('no line number: the previous cite had already drifted'), but no gate enforces it.
findings.proposal: Cite by function or symbol name, not line, as test_verify_scope.sh already does for cited_test_path_citations. Add a cheap lint, in the ptodo-ratchet style, that rejects '<file>.sh:<digits>' in tests/infra comments. Drop header block indexes and keep the in-place '# Block X' headers as the map.

findings.statement: test_warm_lane_gc.sh rebuilds the same per-block fixture inline. The base-generation layout that refresh-warm-base.sh owns (target -> target.gen.1 plus a sibling target.gen.1.lock) is hand-built at 29 sites. The seed-script stub exists as the helper _seed_stub_body (15 uses), yet 12 blocks still inline an identical 109-character copy. Each copy hard-codes the seed's positional contract (LANE_DIR="$2").

findings.statement: The rule that maps a changed path to the crates it affects has three homes, and the Python copy has silently drifted from the bash one. affected-crates-lib.sh's header calls _file_to_crate 'the mapping's SPOT'. reify_overlap_detector.py says its _is_global/_file_to_crate 'mirror the bash equivalents verbatim. Keep them in sync'. verify.sh::decide_scope is a third case ladder. In today's tree, bash _file_to_crate maps examples/*.ri to the six RI-corpus crates (task 7427); the Python copy returns None for it, so the path becomes a path: member and no crate overlap is recorded. Python's _reverse_closure docstring says it 'Mirrors the BFS algorithm embedded in affected-crates-lib.sh:_reverse_closure'. That claim is false: bash now delegates to _reify_compile_closure, a second Python closure program embedded as a heredoc string in occt-scope-lib.sh that keeps normal and dev edges separate, while the overlap detector follows every dep kind transitively. The parity test TestRuleParityWithAffectedCratesLib 'does not parse or source affected-crates-lib.sh, so parity with the bash side is maintained manually'. It pins only the Python side, through private names (rod._is_global, rod._file_to_crate).
findings.proposal: Give path classification and the compile closure one implementation: a stdlib Python module (lift _REIFY_COMPILE_CLOSURE_PY out of the bash heredoc) with a small CLI. affected-crates-lib.sh calls the CLI, reify_overlap_detector imports the module, and verify.sh's decide_scope consumes its class output. Failing that, make the parity test source the bash lib and compare both sides over one shared path corpus.

The remaining third home, verify.sh::decide_scope's case ladder, is fk-73c909381788 and S18 beta #9097. The detector itself is retired by #8886 (pending).; task store: [('8662', 'done')]

findings.statement: The probe runner reports its own outcomes as text inside the captured stderr, and every consumer recovers them with substring and regex matching. run_probe stores 'launch failed' and 'timed out' by writing _BINARY_NOT_FOUND_SENTINEL / _PROBE_TIMEOUT_SENTINEL into ProbeRun.stderr. observe_with_evidence and grammar_substrate_usable branch on `SENTINEL in run.stderr`, and grammar_substrate_usable gets the errno detail back with `run.stderr.split(_BINARY_NOT_FOUND_SENTINEL, 1)[1]`. Across the module boundary, prd-decompose-verify.py::fixture_absent_evidence reads pcc._BINARY_NOT_FOUND_SENTINEL (a private name) and decides FIXTURE_ABSENT by regex over stderr lines. α's _json_record leaves out the probe's `fixture`, so it then has to recover the fixture with pcc.fixture_argument(command[-1]), which reads argv back by position. Its own docstring concedes 'The principled fix is for α to tag the record structurally at probe time', and says the residual mis-routing (a FAIL quoting ENOENT text on the fixture's line drops BLOCKS to INCOMPLETE) and grammar probes (#8122) stay uncovered.
findings.proposal: Make the outcome a field. ProbeRun/Result get a typed `harness_failure` (LAUNCH / TIMEOUT / SETUP, carrying errno text as data) and a `fixture_present` bool measured by α at probe time. _json_record emits `fixture` and those fields, and pdv's classify_record reads the fields instead of re-parsing stderr.

findings.statement: A 'resolves' premise with an empty match binds without complaint and PASSes against a `reify check` that fails, which is the silent-accept vacuity this harness exists to catch. bind_premises refuses an empty match only under `premise.assertion_kind == "rejection"`. _ASSERTION_KIND_MAP binds resolves to (check, present), and α's match_predicate returns True for {}, so observe('check', exit 1, {}) is PRESENT and the verdict is PASS. The Enumerator prompt documents resolves as 'reify check passes (exit_code:0)', but PREMISES_SCHEMA only requires `match` to be some object, and load_probe_set validates match content only for the value kind. The 'a probe must constrain something' rule is therefore enforced three different ways: a load-time validator for value, an ad-hoc if for rejection, and nothing for resolves.
findings.proposal: Give each _ASSERTION_KIND_MAP entry its required match (resolves -> {exit_code: 0}, rejection -> {exit_code: 1}), merged under any premise-supplied keys, and move the non-vacuity check for check-kind probes into α's load_probe_set beside the value validator, so every binder meets the same rule.

findings.statement: The gate's closed vocabularies are re-spelled in each file and language, and two copies have already drifted. Verdicts: α defines PASS/FAIL/UNPROVABLE as public constants, but HARNESS_ERROR as the private _HARNESS_ERROR, even though it is emitted on the wire. pdv writes `_BLOCKING_VERDICTS = frozenset({"FAIL", "UNPROVABLE", "HARNESS_ERROR"})` and `verdict == "HARNESS_ERROR"` as literals, under a comment reading 'Verdict constants reused from α (imported via pcc above)'; nothing is imported. The .mjs repeats them in RESULT_RECORD_SCHEMA's enum and in prompt prose. Assertion kinds: _ASSERTION_KIND_MAP keys, the .mjs PREMISES_SCHEMA enum, the Enumerator prompt prose, and two pdv docstrings (Premise and _parse_premises_file). Both docstrings list 'rejection|parses|resolves|produces|ir' without 'value'. BatchVerdict keys: the dataclass, main()'s hand-built output dict, VERDICT_SCHEMA, and the Synthesize prompt prose. The .mjs batchVerdict comment records that this exact shape of drift already happened ('a field added to one silently missed the other').
findings.proposal: Publish one vocabulary from α: public enums for Verdict and ProbeKind and a `--print-schema` CLI emitting the JSON schemas (verdict enum, assertion kinds, BatchVerdict keys). pdv imports the enums and serialises BatchVerdict with dataclasses.asdict, and the .mjs schemas are generated from or checked against α's output in one test.

findings.statement: The .mjs header says 'All load-bearing logic ... lives in the tested Python harness; this .mjs is a thin orchestration shell'. That is false. The .mjs alone computes the per-leaf disposition (BLOCKS/NOT_VERIFIED/VERIFIED/UNENUMERATED), the batch disposition (BLOCKS/INCOMPLETE/PASS), dropped-leaf accounting, leaves_probed, and the summary, and all dispositions are string literals compared by ===. Because the script exposes no importable interface, 3 test classes cut functions out of its source text at the anchor string 'const _wfResult = await' and eval them with `new Function`. Two more classes run the whole body under a hand-built mock of the Workflow globals. That tests implementation layout, not a public seam.
findings.proposal: Move batch aggregation into the Python harness as a deterministic `aggregate` subcommand (per-leaf verdicts in, BatchVerdict-with-disposition out, dispositions as an enum). The .mjs keeps only agent fan-out and relays that subcommand's JSON, so the tests drive a CLI instead of slicing JS source.

findings.statement: The runner's real inputs are ambient module state rather than parameters, so its tests reach through private names. run_probe, evaluate and build_command each call _find_repo_root() themselves. Binaries resolve from os.environ inside _resolve_reify_bin and _resolve_tree_sitter_bin, and the cache directory from tempfile and env. evaluate() rebuilds the argv with its own build_command call 'with the same repo_root that run_probe() uses', so two derivations of one argv must agree, because the injected runner returns only exit/stdout/stderr and not the command it ran. main() exposes no runner seam, so TestMain patches pcc.run_probe and pcc.evaluate, other tests patch pcc._find_repo_root and pcc._SUBSTRATE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S, and the suite reads 12 distinct private names 69 times.
findings.proposal: Introduce a ProbeContext (repo_root, reify_bin, tree_sitter_bin, cache_home) built once in main(). Pass it to evaluate and run_probe, have the runner return the argv it executed inside ProbeRun, and accept a `runner` argument in main(), so tests drive public seams with fixture directories instead of patching privates.

findings.statement: scripts/ holds two MCP clients for the same escalation server, and they have diverged. escalation_mcp.py (extracted 2026-10-04 as 'how a reify script reaches the escalation server's MCP') has McpSession, read_reply, tool_payload and escalation_url_from_mcp_config. await-merge-landing.py carries its own MergeStatusClient, _read_reply, _jsonrpc_result, _tool_payload and resolve_escalation_url. Today they differ in protocolVersion ('2024-11-05' vs '2025-03-26'), session header spelling, empty-body handling (escalation_mcp returns None; await's json.loads(b'') raises), text payload (all text items joined vs content[0] only), refusal detection (escalation_mcp rejects a payload with an 'error' key; await does not), and timeout. await bounds the whole exchange on a daemon thread because 'urlopen's timeout bounds each socket operation, not the exchange, so a reply that trickles in would outlive it'; escalation_mcp, which the unattended docs-truth-sweep timer uses, has only the per-socket 30 s timeout.
findings.proposal: Make escalation_mcp.py the one client, with a per-call wall-clock deadline (await's _within) and structured errors. await-merge-landing then uses McpSession and escalation_url_from_mcp_config instead of its private copies.

findings.statement: The set of 'load-bearing verify-pipeline' files is rebuilt from several sources by grep and regex: three hand-maintained manifests (verify-pipeline-paths.txt, doc-sync-paths.txt, verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt); a grep of verify.sh for `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/..."`; a grep for `add(_tool)?` statements fed through _SH_PATH_ERE; and a run of verify.sh --print-plan (45 s timeout, `|| true`) whose PLAN entries are eval'd shell strings, regex-scanned for '*.sh' paths. The guard's own comment block says clause 4b 'buys NOTHING' today: it is byte-identical to 4a (13 paths), a second reconstruction of the same fact kept as future-proofing. Gate scripts are recognised only by literal path text: a gate added through a variable, a non-.sh helper, or an unreached build_plan branch still needs a hand-added manifest row. The block that documents all this is about 100 lines of measurements and placement defences ('please keep it here rather than hoisting it').
findings.proposal: Have verify.sh's add/add_tool take the gate script path as a separate structured argument and emit a machine-readable gate list (`--print-gates`, one repo-relative path per line, over every build_plan branch). The guard then reads that list instead of grepping source and parsing plan strings. Move the measurement prose into the PRD or the commit history.

findings.statement: The 'this main move is sanctioned' token is an empty file in the shared common git dir. It is not bound to the move it sanctions, and only one exit path clears it. pre-commit marks it right after project-checks passes, which happens before git collects the commit message, so a commit aborted at the editor or by an empty message leaves it behind. land.sh marks it before `git merge --no-ff` even runs the gate and removes it only on the merge's non-zero return; a SIGINT or SIGTERM during the hours-long gate skips that cleanup, since no trap is set. reference-transaction accepts any existing sentinel for the next fast-forward main move in any of the ~250 linked worktrees, and test (j) deliberately keeps a 'pending sentinel' alive across moves. land.sh's own comment names the invariant ('the sentinel must not linger and falsely sanction a later, unsanctioned main move'), but it is enforced at one call site rather than by the token's shape.
findings.proposal: Write the current main tip into the sentinel at mark time, and have reference-transaction accept it only when its content equals the transaction's old sha. A leftover token from an aborted commit or land then fails closed by construction. Add an EXIT trap to land.sh as well.

findings.statement: The most-patched shell primitives carry their review history inline, and that prose drifts. seed-warm-lane.sh is 60.6% comment lines. Many of them answer a reviewer rather than explain code: measurements ('measured at 0.249s ... on the live 254-worktree store'), amendment narratives ('amendment 2, correcting this doc-comment's earlier claim'), placement defences, and repeated 'do not restate it here' cross-references. The 7-line _close_inherited_fds carries a 46-line comment. The file:line pointers in this prose have moved: seed-warm-lane.sh cites warm-lane-gc.sh:648-649 for the `2>&1 | while read` shape, now at line 690; it cites git-rerere-guard.sh:735-758 for cmd_arm, which starts at line 751; flake-density-report.py cites run_all.sh:711-715 for a record now built at 706-713. Comment-only commits make up 16 of 58 seed-warm-lane.sh commits and 5 of 16 verify-pipeline-guard.sh commits since 2026-07-06.
findings.proposal: Move measurements, amendment histories and placement defences to the commit messages or task records they answer. Keep the normative rationale in PRD §9.5, pointed to by section rather than by line, and replace file:line pointers with symbol names. The file then holds only what the next editor needs to read.

findings.statement: dark-factory decides whether a lane's seed-warm-lane.sh accepts --assume-lane-lock-held and --distinct-lock-refusal-rc by testing whether the flag string occurs anywhere in the file (git_ops.py::_seed_script_supports: `flag in _seed_script_text(...)`). The script's in-file note claims the string 'must stay a LITERAL here' in the arg parser. That misstates the dependency: the probe is satisfied by any mention, and most mentions are comments or usage text. If an agent removes or renames the parser arm and leaves one comment, the probe answers TRUE, DF passes the flag, and the parser's `-*) Unknown flag; exit 2` maps to FAULT, which DF's own docstring calls 'strictly WORSE than the rc-75 fallback'.
findings.proposal: Expose capabilities as data: `seed-warm-lane.sh --capabilities` prints the optional flags its parser accepts. DF probes that output instead of grepping the source, and the 'must stay a literal' comments go.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: cutover-reify-types.py is a 963-line 'task η one-shot cutover script'. It rewrote imports to retire crates/reify-types/ and was last touched 2026-05-27, the day of that cutover (3f3da9f03d). The crate no longer exists, and no tracked file references the script, yet it still sits in scripts/ next to live gates and turns up when agents search for reify-syntax re-exports and crate-rename idioms.
findings.proposal: Delete it; the commit history keeps it recoverable.

findings.statement: verify.sh builds the gate as PLAN, an array of shell-text lines, and three behaviours are decided by inspecting that text rather than a typed step kind. (1) The executor sends any line whose text contains `_VERIFY_NODE_BG_PID` to a main-shell eval instead of reaper_run_in_pgroup. (2) The --print-plan printer annotates by the glob `*'./scripts/verify.sh psi-gate'*`; its own comment records that task 5730's add_tool prefix silently disabled the earlier exact-match arm. (3) confirm_failed_run re-parses verify.sh's own printed plan with awk between two marker comment lines. The cargo-vs-tool distinction (add vs add_tool) is carried by a trailing `# ld-ok:` comment that test_verify_ld_library_path_scope.sh polices with grep over the source. Every new option is threaded as an 'empty-or-leading-space' string fragment so default plans stay byte-identical. The retry composer strips a fragment by suffix pattern (`${_eff_offline_select##* -E \"*\"}`), which is the stated reason _OFFLINE_NO_FAIL_FAST had to be a separate variable.
findings.proposal: Make a plan step a structured record (kind = cargo|tool|main-shell|sentinel, plus named argv fragments) built by typed emitters. Render shell text in one function that both the printer and the executor use. Dispatch on kind, not on substrings. Add a structured --print-plan (JSON lines) and move most plan-shape tests to assert on fields, keeping a few golden text renders.

findings.statement: DF_VERIFY_ROLE (task|merge|offline|background) is decided by 19 inline string comparisons at 16 decision sites in scripts/verify.sh. There are also strict `= "merge"` exemptions in scripts/cpu-admit.sh::cpu_admit and scripts/lib_test_semaphore.sh, and tests/infra/run_all.sh's _RA_INBOUND_ROLE snapshot. Each site hard-codes one per-role property: default profile, CARGO_PRIO class, heavy exclude/select, no-fail-fast, release wall, forced scope=all, jobserver FIFO, release delta skip, attempt-0 sidecar, background ledger, release selector, gui-feature skip, wholesale vs selective infra pool, and the plan NOTE. The `merge || background` disjunction is spelled out 5 times. Adding the background role (task 5210) took 4 GREEN step commits in verify.sh plus follow-up amendments correcting its rationale (b454053d8a, 6204b1e219). The run_all pre-build comment concedes that background reaches an admission-gate-free block and that the fix 'is to route background through compile_gate()/psi_gate()'. No single place declares a role's admission property.
findings.proposal: One role-policy table: a single `case "$DF_VERIFY_ROLE"` that sets named properties (ROLE_DEFAULT_PROFILE, ROLE_FORCE_SCOPE_ALL, ROLE_PRIO_CLASS, ROLE_INFRA_TIER=wholesale|selective, ROLE_HEAVY=exclude-eligible|only|none, ROLE_FAIL_FAST, ROLE_ADMISSION_EXEMPT, ROLE_RELEASE_WALL). Every site reads a property instead of comparing the role. Export ROLE_ADMISSION_EXEMPT so cpu-admit.sh and lib_test_semaphore.sh read it instead of each re-testing `= merge`.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: decide_scope classifies tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri edits by membership in two hand-maintained space-delimited literals in verify.sh. _RUST_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES (40 names) is the set of fixtures named by tracked *.rs. _GUI_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES (145 names) is the set of EXPECTED_CLEAN pins in gui/src/__tests__/reifyGrammarCorpus.test.ts. Both copy facts that live elsewhere. test_verify_scope.sh's PG-DRIFT and PG-DRIFT-GUI re-derive both sets from source and fail on divergence, so the derivation already exists, but only in the guard. verify.sh is a verify-pipeline file, so every registration forces the full gate. A crates/** change that starts reading a fixture does not select test_verify_scope.sh on the task lane, so the missing registration first surfaces in the merge-tier run_all pool. Four more copies have the same shape. select_cheap_ptodo_gate's extension list copies ptodo.rs::is_swept_ext, and its guard checks only one direction. pdiag_swept_path and pdoccover_input_path copy Rust predicates. select_harness_kloc_guard hard-codes a 5-crate literal with no drift guard at all, although tests/infra/harness-layout-lib.sh::harness_layout_consolidatable_crates is the source of truth; its comment points at the test's CONSOLIDATABLE_CRATES instead.
findings.proposal: Make the coupled sets data, not code: one tracked manifest (or the pin list moved out of the .ts into a data file the vitest test also reads) that verify.sh and the guard both consume. Alternatively, compute the Rust set in decide_scope with the guard's own git-grep predicate (sub-second on the hook path). Call harness_layout_consolidatable_crates instead of the crate literal.

findings.statement: REIFY_WARM_LANE_MOUNT names two different directories. provision-warm-lane-fs.sh defines it as the XFS mount point (default <parent>/warm-lanes; its usage says `export REIFY_WARM_LANE_MOUNT=$mount`). preflight, seed-warm-lane.sh and thin-warm-lane.sh read it that way: base at $MOUNT/base, lanes at $MOUNT/worktrees/_lane-*. warm-lane-lock-guard.sh and warm-lane-audit.sh read the same variable as the worktrees dir: lock at $MOUNT/<lane>.lock, residents at $MOUNT/*/. On this host those are /home/leo/src/warm-lanes and /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees. /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/_merge-verify.lock does not exist, and lib_lane_lock.sh::lane_lock_probe returns IDLE silently for an absent lock. So lock-guard run with the provisioned value reports IDLE, with no warning, even when _merge-verify is held. audit walks base/, worktrees/ and the rest, finds no git worktree, and reports resident=0 with exit 0. The audit runbook's recipe passes `--mount "$REIFY_WARM_LANE_MOUNT"`. gc and gc-sweep use yet other names for the worktrees dir (REIFY_WARM_LANE_GC_MOUNT; REIFY_WARM_LANE_GC_SWEEP_MOUNT with a hard-coded /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees default).
findings.proposal: Use two names for the two things. Keep REIFY_WARM_LANE_MOUNT as the XFS mount, and add REIFY_WARM_LANE_WORKTREES (default $REIFY_WARM_LANE_MOUNT/worktrees) read by audit, lock-guard, gc and sweep. Until then, have lock-guard and audit warn when $MOUNT has a worktrees/ child and no lane locks.

findings.statement: The backing-task status-oracle contract is implemented three times, each copy claiming to mirror the others 'byte-for-byte'. The contract: `"$cmd" "$id" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]' || true`, empty output means unknown, done|cancelled means terminal. The copies are preflight Check 6, audit's _task_status_raw/_status_bucket, and degenerate-ref-check's _ref_status. Audit's comments still cite warm-lane-gc.sh's _backing_task_terminal and --status-cmd as fellow consumers; task 5326 removed both, and gc.sh now has zero STATUS_CMD references. The same copy-instead-of-share applies elsewhere. _matches_glob is 'lifted verbatim from warm-lane-gc.sh' into audit, and _is_git_worktree exists in both. task/NNNN branch-to-id parsing appears in 3 scripts. Log helpers are redefined in 8 of 11 files, with three different hint() formats. The family already shares three seams correctly (lib_live_refs.sh, lib_lane_lock.sh, lib_task_citation.sh).
findings.proposal: Add scripts/lib_task_status.sh with task_status_raw <cmd> <id> and task_status_bucket <raw>, plus a task-branch-to-id helper. Source it the way lib_lane_lock.sh is sourced, and add a lib_warm_lane_log.sh for the log helpers.

findings.statement: verify.sh points at itself and sibling files by line number in 7 in-repo places, and 6 of them are stale at this tree. 'forced to scope=all at :644' is now line 1136. 'add_test_passes() is invoked (~:1618)' is now 4405. 'compile-gate line (~:1297)' is now 3906. 'lib_test_semaphore.sh:91 ... stay strict = merge' is now 109. '_RA_INBOUND_ROLE snapshotted at run_all.sh:230' is now 327. 'combined role branch at ~:1499' is now 4185. Only cpu-admit.sh:223 still holds. The lib_test_semaphore.sh cite is the only pointer to a cross-file role exemption. usage() renders --help as `sed -n '2,80p'` of the file header. The header grew (--test-threads in task 5264, --confirm-failed in task 7423), the range was re-guessed rather than delimited, and --help now ends mid-list on 'Role→FIFO selection:'. The file itself says three times to cite 'by function name, not line'. Siblings repeat the pattern: warm-lane-gc.sh cites seed-warm-lane.sh :1243, :136, :323 and :1139, all stale. warm-lane-gc-sweep.sh cites warm-lane-disk-guard.sh:130-138 (now line 191). with-jcodemunch-serve.sh cites run-gui-dev.sh:165-173 (stale).
findings.proposal: Replace each line cite with a symbol name (the add_test_passes call in build_plan, cpu_admit, test_semaphore_acquire, the _RA_INBOUND_ROLE assignment, the forced-scope block next to the MERGE_HEAD check). Render usage() from a heredoc or a marker-delimited block instead of a line range.

findings.statement: The gui-feature test pass in add_test_passes re-implements emit_nextest_pass's nextest/cargo-test arms 'by hand ... kept in lockstep deliberately'. The gen-nextest-config.sh lazy init with _die_nextest_config is written 3 times (emit_nextest_pass, the gui pass, _confirm_subset_pass). The print-plan placeholder path is written twice, and so are the --test-threads fragment and the ` 9<&-` suffix. The sidecar tree_oid reader is a sed one-liner copied into add_test_passes and confirm_failed_run, while confirm_failed_run's comment says it goes 'through the SAME tolerant extractor'; it is a copy. The profile-to-manifest/sidecar selection is written twice (confirm_failed_run, emit_nextest_pass). The stated reason for not reusing emit_nextest_pass is three structural mismatches: a prefix/suffix guard, `-E` fragments, and ~30 plan-shape tests. All three are consequences of the string-assembled plan in finding .1. emit_nextest_pass is 241 lines (92 code) and add_test_passes is 332 (70 code).
findings.proposal: Add one _nextest_config_path (override / print placeholder / memoized generate), one _read_stamp_tree_oid <file>, and one _confirm_paths_for <profile>. Build the gui-feature pass from emit_nextest_pass once plan steps are structured (finding .1).

findings.statement: warm-lane-audit.sh parses two dark-factory-owned JSON records with hand-rolled extractors. _record_scalar is a sed regex for flat string scalars in <state-dir>/<lane>.json. _plan_anchor is a 69-line awk tokenizer over .task/plan.json that pairs each 'status' with the 'commit' that follows it in document order, with backslash and quoting guards. Raw LaneState strings are mapped through a table that mirrors orchestrator/lane_lifecycle.py. The stated reason is that the script must not depend on jq or python3. The extractor's correctness rests on how the producer lays the file out: prerequisites before steps, commit after status within an entry, a flat top-level task_id. If an entry carries commit before status, no anchor is found and the lane reports '-' (nothing recorded) rather than UNKNOWN, so a stranded lane drops out of plan_stranded. Output is also hand-built JSON: 18 HEADROOM fields in two parallel positional printf format/argument lists (table and JSON).
findings.proposal: Read the records with `python3 -I` and stdlib json (the gate's own interpreter) behind one read_json_field helper that has an explicit 'unparseable' outcome, or have dark-factory expose anchor and state through a CLI. Build table and JSON output from one ordered field list.

findings.statement: _do_reclaim is one 337-line function (135 code lines) with indent depth 6. Pass 1 and Pass 2 each re-implement the same sequence: flock acquire, live_ref_present gate, act, release. Outcome accounting (reset, removed, preserved, preserved_live_ref, reset_cold) is incremented inside nested branches, with preserved_count bumped at 10 separate sites. The branch for a seed that refused to certify nests the probe, discard and rm-failure decisions five levels deep.
findings.proposal: Use per-entry functions _reset_lane and _remove_orphan that each return one outcome token, a shared _with_entry_gate <entry> <fn> for the flock and live-ref check, and a single tally case in each loop.

findings.statement: warm-lane-gc.sh's operator-facing --help names a component by its PRD leaf letter. It says 'reset via α seed primitive', '--seed-script PATH Path to α seed primitive' and 'instead of the α reflink-reseed clone'; warm-lane-gc-sweep.sh does the same with 'δ sweep', 'ε reclaim', 'γ disk-guard' and 'fail-to-α'. A reader must open docs/prds/warm-lane-pool-space-safety.md to learn that α means scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh. CLAUDE.md already rejects Greek-letter aliases in task cites for the same reason: they do not resolve without a lookup.
findings.proposal: In gc's _usage text, replace α with the seed-warm-lane.sh name and phrase the reflink-reseed clone in plain words. Apply the same change to the sweep's help text.

findings.statement: engine.rs is one file holding EngineSession plus about ten independent pure-function groups, none of which reads EngineSession state. The groups: Value-to-DTO projection, display routing/appearance, tensegrity extraction, mechanism descriptors and AST bind resolution, entity tree, value-string/unit parsing (about 700 lines incl. COMPOSED_UNIT_INDEX), write_file_atomically, line/col mapping, FEA sampling/channels (about 600 lines), startup cache sweep. Because these groups have no module boundary, tests pin them through crate-private reaches: 28 `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn *_for_test` helpers on EngineSession, used about 230 times. These include cache injectors (override_parsed_cache_for_test, override_line_offsets_cache_for_test, override_consumed_idents_cache_for_test) and CoreState invariant-breakers (break_module_name, inject_compiled). About 20 pub(crate) free functions are also imported by tests by path (apply_fea_channels 12 times, parse_value_string_for_cell 11, extract_joints_from_mechanism 6, …). Those free functions are in effect the public interfaces of submodules that don't exist yet. The 22,615-line engine_tests.rs mirrors the same groups.
findings.proposal: Split along the measured partition (h14_measurements). Each candidate is a downward-only module (engine/units.rs, engine/fea_channels.rs, engine/mechanism.rs, engine/tensegrity.rs, engine/display_routing.rs, engine/entity_tree.rs, engine/projection.rs) that takes explicit compiled/check/values arguments. EngineSession and its cfg(test) impl stay in engine.rs. Each module's pub(crate) functions become its stated interface, and its tests move beside it.

findings.statement: GuiState is built by four hand-written struct literals: set_active_fea_case, build_gui_state's cold-start return, build_gui_state's main return, and build_preview_gui_state. They are kept consistent only by comments ('via shared helpers so both paths cannot diverge'). They have diverged. build_gui_state fills display_panes and display_appearance from collect_display_routing, and gives each mesh a resolved material appearance. set_active_fea_case returns `display_panes: Vec::new(), display_appearance: Vec::new()`, and rebuilds meshes from tess_mesh_cache, which build_gui_state fills with `appearance: None`. display_panes and display_appearance are `diffed whole` and meshes are `diffed keyed` (types.rs gui_state! schema). So in a design with both DisplayOutput panes and FEA cases, a case switch publishes a delta that empties the frontend's displayPanes (engineStore.ts setState('displayPanes')) and strips material appearance from the meshes. No test pins panes or appearance across a case switch. This rebuild path has been amended at least twice already: the #5338 mass-prop re-surface ('pre-existing since task 5194') and f01ed3c474.
findings.proposal: Make build_gui_state's post-tessellation tail a single builder that takes the bare mesh set and the delta, so set_active_fea_case reuses it rather than re-listing fields. Keep display routing and appearance in the cache next to the bare meshes. Add a case-switch test asserting the pane and appearance join survives.

findings.statement: Engine-to-GUI side channels are eight separate mechanisms: AutoResolve, WarmPool, FeaCase, FeaDiagnostics, FeaConvergence, ModeShapeFrame, SolveCancellation, SolverProgress. Each is a separate trait, an `Option<Arc<dyn …>>` field, a setter and an emit helper in engine.rs, a Tauri impl in main.rs (138-236), an install line (main.rs 982-989), and a Recording* test double. Two of them duplicate a GuiState field. fea_diagnostics and fea_convergence are declared `full_reload_only("fea-…-changed emitter")`, yet both are rebuilt into every GuiState and also pushed by emitter. The same shape (a Vec snapshot) is `diffed whole` for display_panes. Routing every engine-mutating entry point through post_engine_call_telemetry is enforced only by each entry point's own behavioural test. The doc says a new entry point that skips the call 'is silently lost — nothing fails CI'.
findings.proposal: Collapse the event axis to one `SessionEvents` sink with a method or enum variant per event, installed once. Move fea_diagnostics and fea_convergence to `diffed whole` and delete their emitters. Make engine mutation return a value that can only be produced via post_engine_call_telemetry, so a skipped call becomes a type error.

findings.statement: The reload pipeline is compile → record_compile_failure on error → check_with_solve_slot → commit_state → post_engine_call_telemetry → build_gui_state. It is open-coded in load_from_source, load_file, update_source and the test-only load_from_compiled. load_from_compiled re-implements commit_state's cache resets by hand ('Replicate the cache resets from the commit_state cache-reset block') and has already drifted: it omits `geometry_derived_cache.clear()`, which commit_state documents as load-bearing defence-in-depth. The two compile helpers return their pair in opposite orders: compile_single_file_with_stdlib returns (ParsedModule, CompiledModule) and compile_entry_with_imports returns (CompiledModule, ParsedModule), so update_source swaps them by hand. Both helpers also carry an identical error-severity filter block.
findings.proposal: Introduce one `fn reload(&mut self, compiled: Result<CompiledPair, …>, file: FilePathUpdate)` that owns check, commit, telemetry and build. Return a named struct from both compile helpers. Make load_from_compiled call commit_state rather than copying it.

Make the tool set a typed table (enum or static slice) carrying name, schema and route (Engine(handler) | Frontend). Generate tools/list and dispatch from it, and export it as JSON for the TS harness, debugParity and the sidecar prompt to import. That removes the textual scanners.
findings.change_note: weakened: debug_server.rs changed only for #7816 (confinement and listener); the tool table did not change. 70 `ToolDef {` matches (the struct definition plus 69 entries). 21 literal dispatch arms in dispatch_tool/dispatch_stateless_tool, with `_ => query_frontend`. The stale '(:1019-1024)' registry pointer is still at debug_server.rs:2096. Verdict stays weakened as review-all had it; owned by S25 τ #8955.

findings.statement: INV-GUI-2 requires every reify_* write tool to reach the baseline through one of the two *_and_refresh_baseline seams and never emit beside it. Nothing in the types enforces this. Any handler has DebugServerState in hand, and with it the engine Arc and last_state, so it can bypass the seam. The invariant is held by a test that lexes debug_server.rs as text: it enumerates `"reify_*" =>` arms, follows calls one hop, and greps for PRIVATE_EMIT_IDENTIFIERS. Its module doc lists its own residuals: emits more than one hop away are invisible, emission shapes not named by the token list are invisible, and an arm both enumerations miss is silent. It needs a spliced positive control because the emit half 'went vacuous once already'.
findings.proposal: Give write-tool handlers a narrower capability, e.g. a `WriteSeam` value constructed only by write_on_engine_and_refresh_baseline that is the only route to &mut EngineSession and the bridge push. Bypassing then becomes unrepresentable and the scanner can be retired.

findings.statement: The debug publication path advances the shared baseline (compute_delta called for its side effect, its StateDelta discarded) before a synchronous query_frontend full push. Because of that ordering, a refused push leaves the baseline ahead of the frontend (bug #7). push_gui_state/frontend_ok was extracted so that 'every write tool inspects its push reply' holds structurally, but only the four reify_* tools use it. handle_set_fea_case advances the baseline through set_fea_case_on_engine_and_refresh_baseline, then calls `query_frontend("apply_gui_state", fp).await?`, discards the reply, and returns `{"ok": true}`. So an in-band `{error}` refusal is reported as success while last_state is already at S1. frontend_ok's doc lists set_fea_case as 'deliberately NOT routed', but the only reason it gives (the reply is returned verbatim) covers only open_file and load_fixture. The whole channel's correctness is restated 14 times as a serial-debug-ops assumption; #7854 (pending, low) would remove it.
findings.proposal: Immediate: route handle_set_fea_case's push through push_gui_state. Structural: land #7854 so debug writes are EvalQueue jobs published by SnapshotPublisher, which retires compute_delta-for-side-effect and the serial assumption.

Run the geometry-derived overlay and the re-check over a typed intermediate (cell id, Value, DeterminacyState, Freshness, Satisfaction) and project to ValueData/ConstraintData strings once, at the end of build_gui_state.

findings.statement: engine.rs decodes eval-produced Values through ad-hoc string-keyed parsers: 11 `type_name == "…"` tests (BucklingResult, ElasticResult, TensegrityWire, TensegritySurface), 41 `fields.get("…")` reads over 32 field names, and 13 `Value::String("…")` map-key lookups (mechanism 'kind'/'bodies'/'at'/'world', multi-case 'cases'). The DisplayStyle/Appearance finish enum is mapped to u8 by two identical `"Matte" => 0, "Satin" => 1, "Gloss" => 2` blocks (extract_display_style_data, project_appearance). resolve_driving_params_from_ast also repeats its descriptor/joint-slot scan in both BindValue arms.
findings.proposal: Have reify-eval expose typed accessors (as detect_multi_case_result already does) for the result shapes the GUI consumes, and give the finish mapping one home.
Replace the 16 line pointers with symbol names, and move the three doc blocks back onto build_values, build_template_node and emit_auto_resolve_if_any.

findings.statement: The side-panel's CSS grid track list is built by an inline IIFE in App's JSX that separately restates which children are mounted; it accounts for DesignTree, PropertyEditor, ConstraintPanel, the two splitters, AutoResolvePanel, MechanismPanel and the chat splitter+ChatPanel, but not BucklingPanel or FeaDiagnosticsPanel, which are conditionally mounted in-flow children of the same grid (their roots are display:flex with no position:fixed/absolute, unlike SolverProgressOverlay which is position:fixed). The code's own comment says a track/child mismatch 'shifts every subsequent child up a track and collapses chat into a 4px strip', and the AutoResolvePanel case was already fixed once by sharing the mount predicate (7a4aef93da); the same restatement is still wrong for two panels. The track-count invariant tests (countGridTracks === children.length) cover mechanism, auto-resolve and the debug overlay only.
findings.proposal: Declare the side panel as one ordered list of entries {id, mounted: () => boolean, track: () => string, render} and derive both the rendered children (<For> over mounted entries) and grid-template-rows from that list, so a panel cannot be added to one without the other; alternatively, put all non-resizable optional panels in a single flex column occupying one 'auto' track. Add a countGridTracks case with buckling and FEA diagnostics mounted.

findings.statement: buildHandlers is a single 1532-line closure returning 58 debug-MCP command handlers, each validating its own params by hand. The file documents 'THE BOUNDARY RULE' in a ~60-line comment that censuses twelve independent copies of the same typeof-string guard (one spelled differently, kept 'as it stood'), backed by TYPE_GUARDED_RESOLVER_TOOLS and a per-copy test row, because 'the guards are INDEPENDENT COPIES, not one shared helper'. Handlers outside that family still read params through `as string` casts the comment itself says a JSON payload can falsify (type_in_editor content, keyboard key, select_entity, toggle_select, open_file path and content). Meanwhile every tool's parameter schema (types, required) is already declared once in Rust as ToolDef.input_schema in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs, and the Rust registry and the TS handler table are kept in step only by debugParity.test.ts regex-parsing debug_server.rs's source.
findings.proposal: Validate params once at dispatch against a single declared schema per tool: either have the Rust side forward each tool's input_schema and run one validator in initDebugBridge before calling the handler, or declare the schema beside each TS handler and generate/compare the Rust ToolDef from it. Then split buildHandlers into family modules (dom/inspection, pointer, camera, layout/window, lsp probes, fixtures/injection, wait) each exporting `(ctx) => Record<string, CommandHandler>` over a shared resolve module, and retire the copy census comment.

findings.statement: App (and engineStore.subscribeToEvents) reach the IPC layer by importing ./bridge directly rather than taking it as a dependency, so every App-level or store-level test must replace the whole module with vi.mock('../bridge', factory). Dropped keys in those hand-written factories caused three recorded defects (tasks 6035, 6039, 6045, replayed in bridgeMockContract.test.ts), and the response was a source-text parser over test files (bridgeMockContract.ts) plus a coverage test, rather than an injection seam. App.tsx also imports viewPersistence twice, once as a namespace, with a comment saying the namespace exists 'so vi.spyOn in tests intercepts the call'. The codebase already has the injected pattern for some collaborators (createMechanismStore({getMechanismDescriptors}), createDefPreviewActivation, createEditorSelectionSync) but not for the bridge.
findings.proposal: Give App a bridge port (an object typed as the subset of ./bridge it uses) via a prop or context with the real module as default, and have engineStore.subscribeToEvents accept its subscription functions; tests then build one typed fake from a shared factory, tsc enforces completeness, and the source-parsing guard and the namespace-import-for-spyOn can go.

findings.statement: viewStateStore's visibility queries (getEffectiveVisibility, getAllEffective, getStalePaths, hasOverride) read nodeByPath/parentByPath, plain non-reactive Maps reassigned by rebuildTreeMaps, and three of them short-circuit on an empty map without reading any reactive key. A reactive consumer that reads them before the tree loads therefore subscribes to nothing and never re-runs. Correctness depends on a readiness counter (treeGeneration) owned by App, bumped by App after it calls regenerateAutoViews, and threaded by hand into each consumer: App's effectiveVisibility memo, the fuzzy-rebind effect, and createSelectiveDemandSync, where it is a required parameter documented by a ~72-line docblock. The missing readiness dependency was a shipped bug (esc-6045-1, fixed under #6052 in three commits), and that docblock has itself needed two correction commits.
findings.proposal: Make the tree reactive state of viewStateStore itself (store a tree signal or a store-owned generation read inside every query) so the queries subscribe on their own; drop treeGeneration from App and the createSelectiveDemandSync signature, and delete the readiness prose.

findings.statement: types.ts hand-mirrors the Rust wire types in gui/src-tauri/src/types.rs with no code generation (no ts-rs/specta/typeshare in gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml), tying the two together with prose ('Mirrors ... in types.rs') and per-field regex-over-Rust-source tests (constraintVerdictTokens.ts over engine.rs, toolDefNames.ts over debug_server.rs). Enum-valued fields cross the boundary as strings: ValueData.determinacy/kind/freshness, ConstraintData.status, DiagnosticInfo.severity, TensegrityWire/SurfaceData.kind, and EvaluationStatus.phase, which Rust stores as String after stringifying an EvalActivity enum of exactly {Evaluating, Idle}. The TS union adds 'resolving', which no producer emits, and the phase's consumers disagree on what 'active' means: engineStore.setEvalStatus treats evaluating|resolving as active, debug wait_for_idle treats only 'evaluating' as active and returns an engine_phase error for any other non-idle phase (its comment names an 'error' phase that does not exist), and StatusBar styles data-phase=resolving.
findings.proposal: Generate the wire interfaces from types.rs (ts-rs or specta), with the closed-set fields as Rust enums serialized to string-literal unions; give phase one exported isActivePhase helper used by engineStore and wait_for_idle; retire the regex-over-Rust parity helpers as fields move under generation.

findings.statement: The set of layout dimensions has no single home: it is enumerated separately in the PanelLayout type, loadPanelLayout's per-key typeof checks, createLayoutStore's initial state, its persistence snapshot, its seven setters, the DEFAULT_* constants, the DebugStores.layout structural type in debug/types.ts (which marks problemsHeight/problemsCollapsed and their setters optional although the real store always has them), the debug resize_panes DIMS table, and the debug reset_app_state body. These copies have already drifted: reset_app_state resets 5 of the 6 numeric dimensions and not problemsCollapsed, while the Rust ToolDef contract for reset_app_state promises it will 'reset layout pane dimensions to their defaults', and no test checks the problems panel after a reset.
findings.proposal: Have layoutStore export one dimension table (key, default, kind) from which PanelLayout, load validation, initial state, persistence and setters derive, plus a reset() method; type DebugStores.layout as LayoutStore, and make resize_panes and reset_app_state iterate the table / call reset().

findings.statement: initApp manages its 11 event subscriptions through 11 separate `let …Unsub` closure variables and 10 near-identical try/await/if(!alive){u();return}/assign/catch blocks, and tears them down from two hand-maintained lists that already disagree: the defensive teardown at the top of initApp clears 10 and omits debugBridgeUnsub, while onCleanup clears all 11. The same module's peers do this uniformly: engineStore.subscribeToEvents collects unlisteners from one Promise.allSettled array, and bridge.subscribeToClaudeEvents iterates an entry table with rollback.
findings.proposal: Collect handles in one array with a small track(unsub) helper (or iterate a table of [subscribe, handler, onFailure]), tear down from that one array in both places, mirroring subscribeToClaudeEvents.

findings.statement: Default visibility decides whether a let-binding is geometry by matching the regex \b(Solid|Surface|Curve|Geometry)\b against EntityTreeNode.type_name, the Display output of a Rust Type, and the manufacturing view does the same with \bMaterial\b. The function's own docblock records that the rule was dead against every real tree until #5195 added the 'Geometry' token, because the backend Displays both spellings as 'Geometry'. The same node already carries structured backend facts (trait_geometry, default_visible) for the other rules. The purpose-view path (generatePurposeViews, manufacturingReadyVisibilityFor, MATERIAL_TYPE_NAME_RE) is unreachable in production: its only production caller passes an empty purpose list.
findings.proposal: Emit a structured field on EntityTreeNode (e.g. is_geometry_value / a value-kind enum) from the backend and branch on it; delete the purpose-view path or wire activePurposes from the design.

findings.statement: unitLadder.ts re-implements the .ri quantity-literal grammar on the frontend (QUANTITY_NUMBER and buildQuantityRe, described as mirroring tree-sitter's token.immediate) alongside a hand-written floor of unit labels and dimensions that, per its own doc, 'must be re-derived by hand' when the floor changes; the backend's parse_value_string is a third grammar (it accepts '5 mm', the frontend refuses it). The file is 84% comments, much of it reviewer-answering history and rejected alternatives, and acceptsBareNumber's docblock states the same 'asymmetry that remains' argument twice under two headings.
findings.proposal: Ask the backend instead of mirroring it: a validate_parameter_literal(cell_id, text) IPC, or ship the accepted alphabet and dimension coverage inside get_unit_ladders, so the frontend holds no grammar or floor of its own; move the surviving rationale into a docs/ note with a one-line pointer.

findings.statement: SidecarSession.invokeSdk is a 279-line method that builds CLI arguments, lazily writes an MCP config temp file, emits the sandbox notice, spawns the process and wires its error listeners, writes stdin, arms the timeout, captures stderr, and parses the stream-json event stream including four content-block kinds and the result event. The per-line `try { ... } catch { /* Skip unparseable lines */ }` wraps the whole event-handling body, not just JSON.parse, so any exception thrown while mapping an event, including from this.onOutput, is discarded as if the line were malformed.
findings.proposal: Extract a pure buildClaudeArgs(config, sessionId, mcpConfigPath), a spawn helper, and a pure mapStreamEvent(event, turnState) -> {outputs, turnState} reducer; narrow the catch to JSON.parse and log anything else.

findings.statement: isPersistentViewState is copied byte-for-byte into gui/src/stores/sidecarPersistence.ts, whose header says it is 'duplicated here (rather than shared) so the two layers can evolve independently', although both validate the same PersistentViewState type. Every schema change so far has had to edit both copies.
findings.proposal: Export isPersistentViewState from viewPersistence.ts (or a small persistedViewState.ts) and import it in sidecarPersistence.ts; delete the duplication note.

findings.statement: The describe block 'viewStateStore — source comments' reads stores/viewStateStore.ts with readFileSync and asserts that a `// Mutations` divider comment is immediately followed by `function setVisibility(` and that a historical comment phrase is absent; a second test self-tests that regex. It pins comment layout, not behaviour.
findings.proposal: Delete the 'viewStateStore — source comments' describe block.

findings.statement: The width of the loop-closure Newton state is a fact computed at four sites, and the snapshot warm-start check disagrees with the other three. The solver's validate_loop_closure_inputs, solve_loop_closure's x0 construction, and snapshot's own post-solve check all use Σ JointKind::flat_len over free_b. The snapshot warm-start check (`if row.len() != free_b.len() { return Some(Value::Undef) }`) uses the free-joint COUNT. snapshot writes `free_values` rows as the full flat x (length Σ flat_len), and sweep::build_snapshot_list threads that row back as the 3-arg warm start. So for any closed-chain mechanism whose free_b holds a planar (flat_len 3), cylindrical (2) or spherical (4) joint, every sweep step after the first returns Value::Undef. extract_loop_closure_chains does put unbound multi-DOF joints into free_b, and joint_range_midpoint returns Some for them, so the cold first step succeeds. The adjacent comment ('the solver's own validate_loop_closure_inputs re-enforces it') claims agreement with a rule that is different.
findings.proposal: Delete the snapshot-side length guard, or compute it with the same helper the solver uses (expose the solver's free_joint_shapes width as one pub(crate) fn). Add a sweep test over a closed chain with a free planar joint that asserts every step is non-Undef.

findings.statement: A joint's kind is a string inside a Value::Map, and every consumer re-parses it with its own match. Per-kind behaviour (constructor, transform, analytic Jacobian, motion subspace, DOF count, storage width, value wrapping, bound-value parsing, midpoint, driving-ness, force naming, compiler result type) is spread across string-match tables in 8 files and 2 crates. Two typed forms exist, loop_closure_value::JointKind and JointValue, but they are built from the string at each use site (JointKind::from_str has 6 production call sites) instead of once at construction. Agreement between the tables is enforced by test loops over the string constant JOINT_KINDS, not by exhaustiveness. Some sites have no guard at all: snapshot::wrap_jointvalue_for_joint and sweep::driving_joint_kind end in a `_ => None` catch-all, and joint_jacobian_value ends in `_ => Value::Undef`. JOINT_KINDS' own doc says the per-kind arms in transform_at and joint_jacobian_value 'must be kept in sync with this constant' by hand.
findings.proposal: Parse once: a typed `Joint` enum (one variant per kind, carrying unit axes and ranges) built by the constructors and recovered from the Map by one `Joint::from_value`. Per-kind behaviour goes in exhaustive methods in one module (transform, jacobian_columns, motion_subspace, dof, flat_len, wrap/unwrap JointValue, midpoint, is_driving). The Map stays the serialised Value form, and every site above calls the typed methods.

findings.statement: The policy that resolves a joint's motion value (direct binding → coupling follows its parent → fixed sentinel → range midpoint) and wraps it as a transform_at argument is implemented twice. snapshot.rs has value_for + wrap_midpoint_for_joint + wrap_jointvalue_for_joint for the FK walk. loop_closure.rs has resolve_joint_value + direct_binding_value + value_for_joint for the solver inputs. wrap_jointvalue_for_joint is a line-for-line copy of loop_closure::value_for_joint, which is already pub(crate). The copies have diverged on multi-DOF. snapshot's midpoint fallback unwraps only JointValue::Scalar, so an unbound planar/spherical/cylindrical joint in an OPEN chain makes the whole snapshot Undef. The loop_closure copy resolves the same joint's midpoint for closed chains. The test snapshot_with_unbound_planar_returns_undef pins the Undef. Its doc justifies it with 'joint_range_midpoint returns None for planar … deferred to #2670', but loop_closure.rs's joint_range_midpoint_planar_returns_planar_midpoint asserts Some(Planar([0.5,0.5,π/2])), and task #2670 is status done.
findings.proposal: Make loop_closure's typed resolve_joint_value + value_for_joint the one resolver. snapshot's joint_local_transform should call `value_for_joint(joint, &resolve_joint_value(joint, bindings)?)` and delete value_for and both wrap_* functions. Rewrite the pinned test to assert the midpoint pose.

findings.statement: The diagnostics wrapper's policy is overridden by its only production caller, and its typed output is thrown away and rebuilt from strings. snapshot calls solve_loop_closure_with_diagnostics, scans report.diagnostics for DiagnosticCode::KinematicOverconstrained, and when found re-runs plain solve_loop_closure. Its comment calls the wrapper's '<6 free DOF' short-circuit 'a false positive for sub-6 effective-DOF loops'. KinematicUnderconstrained is discarded. Singularity is turned into an `is_singular: Bool(true)` key on the Snapshot Map. reify-eval's engine_eval::value_contains_singular_snapshot finds that key with a recursive string-key tree walk and mints a second KinematicSingularity diagnostic with its own message text. The solver also returns a flat Vec<f64>. To unflatten it, snapshot re-derives each free joint's JointKind from chain_b's kind strings, a third copy of the solver's private free_joint_shapes, and the third site that checks expected_width.
findings.proposal: Move the residual-subspace DOF policy into the solver, where snapshot needs no override. Have the solve return typed per-free-joint JointValues plus diagnostics. Carry diagnostics out of snapshot through the existing per-builtin `diagnose` hook (snapshot::diagnose already exists for center_of_mass) instead of a magic key and an engine-side scan.

findings.statement: The `input_shape` builtin has two TOTS-family implementations with different meanings. input_shape::eval_input_shape (the value-eval path, wired for `input_shape` and `input_shape_apply`) builds a canonical single-DOF stand-in model (canonical_tots_model, start 0 / end 1 / T 3 s, max_force hard-coded 1000.0), runs the full SQP (solve_tots, RNEA and modal simulation every iteration), and keeps only the outcome: Undef if infeasible, otherwise the INPUT profile echoed back. trampoline::input_shape_value (the engine ComputeNode path via reify-eval trajectory_ops) solves on a model built from the profile and returns a re-timed profile. Shaper-field defaults are duplicated, and a comment says they 'mirror input_shape::run_tots'. The `force_limit` field is read in one path and ignored in the other. read_scalar_si and field_f64 are each defined in both files. Family membership is decided by matching the StructureInstance type_name string. The two sites are kept in step by a 280-line #[cfg(test)] module (shaper_family_guard) that line-scans trajectory.ri with a hand-written partial grammar (prefix stripping, angle-bracket depth, `+` bound lists) and admits it misses multi-line headers.
findings.proposal: Keep one implementation. Have eval_input_shape delegate to trampoline::input_shape_value, or return Undef and leave the result to the ComputeNode. Parse the shaper once into a typed enum (Impulse(ZV|ZVD|EI|Cascaded) | Tots{params}) whose constructor is the only name match. A compiler-side registry of Shaper refiners can then replace the text scanner.

findings.statement: Loop-closure records are parsed in three places that do not share the precondition the docs say they share. mechanism_loop_closure_chains (used only by reify-constraints, via a re-export) classifies WellFormed vs Cycle. Its doc says Cycle chains must NOT be fed to solve_loop_closure. snapshot's solve path uses loop_closure::extract_loop_closure_chains instead, which does not classify, and feeds every record to the solver (snapshot's own doc calls the split 'advisory here'). strip_world_sentinel exists twice: loop_closure_solver.rs (pub(crate), used by mechanism_loop_closure_chains and snapshot::parent_conflict_closing_body_ids) and loop_closure.rs (private, used by extract_loop_closure_chains). The loop_closure.rs copy's doc says it 'mirrors reify_constraints::loop_closure::strip_world_sentinel', a module that no longer exists (reify-constraints/src has no loop_closure file). parent_conflict_closing_body_ids says 'sharing the PRECONDITION … is what makes the two call sites agree', but the solver path it must agree with uses the other copy.
findings.proposal: Keep one record parser, returning a typed record (chains, closing_joint, body_id, classification). Both extract_loop_closure_chains and parent_conflict_closing_body_ids derive from it. Delete the loop_closure.rs strip_world_sentinel copy, and have snapshot skip or diagnose Cycle records explicitly.

findings.statement: Prose about multi-DOF support was written before KCC-γ, repeated across four files, and now contradicts the code in at least 11 places. Most of it cites deferral task #2670, which is status done. False today: JOINT_KINDS doc ('explicit None arms in loop_closure::value_for_joint and joint_range_midpoint … cannot represent multi-DOF'); eval_joints joint_jacobian comment ('planar → zero column placeholder … value_for_joint returns None for planar'); joint_jacobian_value cylindrical arm ('contrasts with the planar/spherical zero-twist Map placeholder'); SINGLE_LOOP_RESIDUAL_COUNT doc ('chain_jacobian_fd already rejects chains containing multi-DOF joints'); solve_loop_closure_with_diagnostics '1-DOF chain assumption'; LoopClosureReport ('Future task 10 will be the first consumer'); snapshot wrap_midpoint_for_joint ('joint_range_midpoint returns None for planar'); snapshot value_for inline ('Multi-DOF wrapping is deferred to step-10's wrap_jointvalue_for_joint', which is never called there); the snapshot_with_unbound_planar_returns_undef doc; snapshot's warm-start comment (finding 1); loop_closure.rs strip_world_sentinel's pointer to reify_constraints. In the same files, production prose is 41.6% (joints), 51.5% (loop_closure_solver) and 48.7% (snapshot) of lines.
findings.proposal: Move the per-kind capability matrix to one place (the PRD or the typed Joint module from finding 2) and point to it from the code. Delete the step-numbered narration and the #2670 deferrals.

findings.statement: TOTS solver outcomes are named by diagnostic-code strings that the diagnostics system does not know and that never reach the user. TotsOutcome::code_str returns "W_TrajectorySolverNonConvergence" / "E_TrajectoryConstraintInfeasible". Neither exists in reify-core's DiagnosticCode, and code_str's only callers are tots.rs tests. Both input_shape dispatch arms map ConstraintInfeasible to a bare Value::Undef with no diagnostic, and NonConvergence to a normal-looking result. The PRD codes appear only in comments at those arms.
findings.proposal: Replace code_str with a typed DiagnosticCode mapping and emit it through the trajectory module's diagnose hook from the arm that produces the result.

findings.statement: Stdlib modules call their siblings by user-facing builtin name through the crate-root dispatcher (crate::eval_builtin), which walks the registry and the family dispatcher ladder. In joints.rs, transform_at's coupling arm recurses via eval_builtin("transform_at"), and the planar arm composes via eval_builtin("transform_compose"). The same function's origin step instead calls the typed crate::geometry::compose_transforms. screw/gear/rack_and_pinion call eval_builtin("couple"). loop_closure_solver::solve_loop_closure calls eval_builtin("joint_jacobian") once per free joint and discards the result; its only effect is a tracing::debug event that tests capture. Each such call is an untyped, rename-fragile edge: a failure comes back as Value::Undef, not a compile error.
findings.proposal: Expose typed pub(crate) Rust functions (transform_at(&Joint, &JointValue), compose, couple) that the builtin arms and the internal callers both use. Turn the KCC-γ availability probe into a direct tracing call, or drop it.

findings.statement: tots.rs widens its internal SQP helpers to pub(crate) even though nothing outside the file uses them. That widening exposes them to the orphan-producer audit (scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh), which is then silenced line by line with `// G-allow:` comments, and the whole module carries `#![allow(dead_code)]`. The allow hides dead production code: TotsOutcome::code_str is reached only from tests.
findings.proposal: Make the 15 helpers private, delete the 14 G-allow lines and #![allow(dead_code)], and let rustc flag what is genuinely dead.

findings.statement: snapshot.rs and dynamics::eval import each other, and the binding constructor sits in the wrong layer. snapshot imports `crate::dynamics::eval::mass_properties_from_value`, and also `crate::resolve_body_mass`, a crate-root reach-back to a function defined in dynamics/eval.rs. dynamics/eval.rs calls `crate::snapshot::make_binding`, which was made pub(crate) for that one consumer according to its doc. make_binding is a constructor for a value type (`kind="binding"`). The `bind` validation in eval_snapshot, sweep (via eval_builtin("bind")) and dynamics all depend on it, but it lives in the FK-evaluation module.
findings.proposal: Move make_binding and the binding-shape validation into a small lower bindings module that snapshot, sweep and dynamics::eval all import downward.

findings.statement: The per-joint-kind codec between JointValue and the dimensioned Value that transform_at consumes has no single home. loop_closure::value_for_joint (pub(crate)) and snapshot::wrap_jointvalue_for_joint (private) have identical bodies; the snapshot copy's doc even says it 'mirrors loop_closure::value_for_joint'. The inverse direction (loop_closure::jointvalue_from_bound_value) and a partial third encoder (snapshot::wrap_midpoint_for_joint) also match on raw kind strings. Only joint_range_midpoint and is_zero_dof_joint dispatch through the typed JointKind via joint_kind(), whose own doc concedes it is not the SPOT for the value encodings. The binding-resolution ladder (direct binding, then coupling-tracks-parent, then fixed sentinel, then range midpoint) is likewise implemented twice: loop_closure::resolve_joint_value and snapshot::value_for. The copies have drifted. resolve_joint_value returns Planar/Sphere/Cyl midpoints for unbound multi-DOF joints. snapshot::value_for keeps only JointValue::Scalar midpoints (`_ => None`), so by code read the open-chain FK path yields None (and so Undef) for an unbound planar, spherical or cylindrical joint. Its comment still claims 'joint_range_midpoint returns None for planar' pending #2670, and #2670 is done. Adding a joint kind is a compile error only in joint_range_midpoint; the other four string matches fall to `_ => None` silently.
findings.proposal: Give JointKind (in loop_closure_value.rs, where JointValue already lives) the codec as exhaustive methods: encode(&JointValue, parent kind) -> Option<Value> and decode(&Value) -> Option<JointValue>. Make one pub(crate) resolver for the binding ladder. Have snapshot's open-chain and closed-chain post-process paths call that resolver and encoder, then delete wrap_jointvalue_for_joint, wrap_midpoint_for_joint and the duplicated ladder in value_for.

findings.statement: append_body knows which closing-edge class it recorded: parent-conflict, or cycle/self-loop. It knows which body is the closing one, and which error it raised. make_loop_closure_record and make_body_record then erase that into string-keyed Value::Maps. Every consumer re-derives the class from structure. loop_closure_solver::mechanism_loop_closure_chains and snapshot::parent_conflict_closing_body_ids classify Cycle vs WellFormed by whether chain_b contains the closing joint anywhere (closing_side_contains_closing_joint). The doc comments on that predicate run about 40 lines explaining why a tail test is wrong. dynamics::eval::closed_chain_inverse_dynamics assumes 'Mechanism builder appends closing-edge bodies at the end, so the first n_tree entries are the spanning-tree bodies', taking tree_bodies = bodies[..n_total - n_lc]. append_body enforces no such order: it pushes every body in call order. So by code read, an open body() after a closing one is dropped from the tree and the closing body is counted as a tree body. reify-eval engine_eval::detect_mechanism_errors hardcodes the 'duplicate_solid' discriminator, so 'world_parented_closure' has no diagnostic (#7354, pending, covers only that error half). The record is parsed independently in two places: loop_closure::extract_loop_closure_chains and loop_closure_solver::mechanism_loop_closure_chains, each with its own strip_world_sentinel.
findings.proposal: Make the edge class, the closing-body id and the error kind typed at construction. The cheap step is to stamp a 'class' discriminator and keep the existing body_id on each loop_closure record, have dynamics select tree bodies by excluding those body_ids rather than by position, and route detect_mechanism_errors through a discriminator-to-DiagnosticCode table (the shape #7354 proposes). The deeper step is a typed MechanismRecord / LoopClosure struct carried in OpaqueState or a StructureInstance, parsed once at the stdlib boundary, with extract_loop_closure_chains and mechanism_loop_closure_chains merged into its one reader.

findings.statement: worst_case_residual_fraction is pub and #[allow(dead_code)], and has zero production callers. Its G-allow comment and doc claim it is a 'permanent internal helper of the wired trajectory evaluation pipeline (simulate_trajectory_value / solve_tots, both wired via trampoline.rs → trajectory_ops.rs:371/429)'. Neither trampoline in this file calls it, reify-eval has no trampoline.rs, and nothing under crates/reify-stdlib/src/trajectory/ outside impulse_shaper.rs calls residual_vibration, so TOTS does not score shapers through it. The module docstring repeats the claim ('Both reuse [`worst_case_residual_fraction`]'). reify-audit's new_orphans_2026_06_02_g_allow.rs then pins the orphan as allowed, 'owned by' #3869 and #3870, both done. The file layout also puts the #[cfg(test)] module between this helper and a second `use` block that opens the real trampoline code, so the file reads as two files spliced together.
findings.proposal: Either wire it, so TOTS or simulate_trajectory actually reports worst-case band residual, or delete it with its tests and the audit pin. Either way, rewrite the module docstring to describe the two trampolines this file actually holds, and move the test module to the end of the file.

findings.statement: loop_closure.rs carries a private strip_world_sentinel identical in behaviour to loop_closure_solver::strip_world_sentinel, which is pub(crate) in the same crate. Both are len < 2 rejection plus an inline kind == "world" test. Its doc justifies the copy with a false claim: 'Mirrors reify_constraints::loop_closure::strip_world_sentinel (which is private to that module); duplicated here so the stdlib helper is self-contained without crossing the constraints crate boundary'. reify-constraints has no loop_closure module; it only re-exports reify_stdlib::loop_closure_solver. Both copies inline the world predicate instead of calling the existing pub(crate) mechanism::is_world, as snapshot.rs and dynamics/eval.rs do. mechanism_loop_closure_chains, snapshot's closing-body classification and extract_loop_closure_chains all depend on the two copies agreeing; the solver's doc says sharing this precondition 'is what keeps the two agreeing'.
findings.proposal: Delete loop_closure.rs's copy and call crate::loop_closure_solver::strip_world_sentinel, or move one copy next to mechanism::is_world and have both call it. Make the predicate itself mechanism::is_world. Correct the docstring's crate path.

findings.statement: Production prose in loop_closure.rs and mechanism.rs is about half the lines, and much of it narrates history or answers reviewers rather than stating contracts, which is the drift class this repo keeps paying for. In loop_closure.rs the module docstring contradicts the function docs. It says FD chain Jacobians are correct only for 'prismatic, revolute, coupling, fixed', with planar/spherical/cylindrical 'deferred to ... #2670', while chain_jacobian_fd's doc says it covers 'all seven JOINT_KINDS post KCC-γ widening', and #2670 is done. It calls the snapshot evaluator 'future task 2585' and points five times at a nonexistent reify_constraints::loop_closure. Function docs narrate signature changes ('widened from (joint, f64) ...', 'Task 7186 changed where ... Before 7186 it was appended ...'). LoopClosureSolverInputs carries a defence of tuple-over-struct. In mechanism.rs, append_body's comments include a rejected-alternatives argument with a measurement ('measured at 1.3 m on the 5-arg form') and four pointers into an untracked plan.json. The fix history shows the cost: the task 7186 burst on these two files needed repeated comment-correction commits.
findings.proposal: Rewrite both module docstrings as current contracts: supported kinds, twist convention, and a pointer to docs/prds/v0_2/kinematic-constraints.md for rationale. Move the residual-conjugation and rigid-tie arguments into that PRD or docs/, with a one-line pointer from append_body. Drop KCC-γ and 7186 narration and the tuple-vs-struct defence, since they belong in commit messages.

findings.statement: extract_loop_closure_chains returns LoopClosureSolverInputs, a positional 5-tuple (chain_a, vals_a, chain_b, vals_b_initial, free_b). Two field pairs are parallel vectors whose equal-length invariant is not carried by the type. It is re-checked ad hoc in chain_transform, chain_jacobian_fd and loop_residual_jacobian_by_joint, and each collapses a violation to a bare None. The whole public surface of the module is Option-returning, with no reason carried. The production code has 34 `return None`, 36 `?` propagations and 7 `_ => None` arms across 8 pub/pub(crate) functions, so snapshot maps any of them to Value::Undef with no named cause. Its own comment calls this a way to 'surface the structural bug'. Meanwhile loop_closure_solver re-validates the same inputs and does produce reason strings.
findings.proposal: Replace the tuple with a named struct whose chains are Vec<(Value, JointValue)>, or an owning type built once with its invariant checked at construction. Return Result with a small error enum naming the failed field or joint. Have snapshot surface that error as a diagnostic rather than a bare Undef.
