findings.statement: value_size_estimate, the warm-state cache cost estimator feeding cost_per_byte, exists as three private copies in reify-eval: trajectory_ops.rs, dynamics_ops.rs and compute_targets/fdm_slice.rs. Each points at another as the one it 'mirrors', and they have drifted. The fdm_slice copy recurses into Value::Point and Value::Vector, while the trajectory_ops and dynamics_ops copies count those as a flat size_of::<Value>(). The trajectory_ops copy defers hoisting to 'a follow-up' with no task cite.
findings.proposal: Hoist one pub(crate) value_size_estimate into the warm_pool / OpaqueState module that owns the cost_per_byte contract, and delete the copies.

findings.statement: per_joint_jacobian_local is a pub function kept 'for future adjoint-transport composition' with zero production callers. It still shapes code elsewhere. joints.rs has comments at five sites explaining that the multi-DOF joint_jacobian returns a List rather than a Map so that it 'signals to per_joint_jacobian_local to fall back'. That is a shape-encoded protocol for a consumer that does not exist. loop_closure.rs keeps 12 tests for it.
findings.proposal: Delete per_joint_jacobian_local and its tests until adjoint composition is actually scheduled, or give it a real caller in chain Jacobian assembly. Drop the joints.rs shape-as-signal justification either way.

findings.statement: reify-gcode's rationale prose points at numbered 'plan design decision #N' and 'plan reuse-item #N' entries from a task-scoped plan that is not tracked. The only tracked candidate, docs/prds/v0_3/trajectory-input-shaping.md §8 'Resolved design decisions', numbers different decisions: 8.7 is ComputeNode wiring, while klipper.rs cites '#7' for Klipper-delegates-to-Marlin. So following a pointer lands on the wrong rationale. The 'why' behind uppercase-only Klipper matching, the '=' error sentinel, first-failure short-circuit and the raw-string KV params cannot be recovered from the tree.
findings.proposal: Inline the one-line rationale where it is load-bearing (uppercase-only matching, first-'=' split) or move it to the PRD under stable headings, and drop the plan numbers.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: A malformed Klipper KEY=VALUE token (no '=' or empty key) is reported as ParseErrorKind::InvalidParameter { letter: '=', value }. That is a magic char inside a typed error enum meaning 'not an axis letter at all'. The doc admits it is a 'semantic approximation' and says the fix is a dedicated variant, deferred because error.rs was 'out of scope for task ν'. A consumer rendering or routing on the error must know the '=' convention from klipper.rs prose.
findings.proposal: Add ParseErrorKind::MalformedKeyValue { token: String } and construct it in parse_kv_params.

findings.statement: Engine::execute_realization_ops is one 2,317-line associated fn (1,095 code lines, 1,212 comment lines) nested up to 16 levels deep. It contains the whole per-realization pipeline inline. Inside the op loop, the Ok(geom_op) match arm runs about 1,200 lines (7734-8936) and holds: selector pre-hydration, dispatch plus BRep fallback, pragma warning, the multi-stage conversion recipe (the Some(plan) arm with conversions, about 630 lines, 7959-8589, containing a labelled 'convert loop, intermediate-cache inserts and attribute forwarding closures), and execute_with_history with attribute population (about 200 lines). After the loop, the success branch is about 750 lines and adds swept-kind recording, a selector tie-scan, the morph decision, an inline VolumeMesh terminal conversion (about 250 lines) and an inline Voxel terminal conversion, then the cache insert. Each terminal repr is an inline `if demanded_repr == ReprKind::X` block rather than a stage. It has grown about 29% since the 2026-07-05 survey measured ~1,794 lines.
findings.proposal: Split along the stages already present: (a) a per-op dispatch function returning a typed OpOutcome {handle, repr, attribute_history, intermediate_inserts} that the loop folds; (b) one function per terminal conversion keyed by demanded_repr (VolumeMesh, Voxel), each returning the new terminal handle and repr; (c) a commit/rollback function that owns intermediate_cache_inserts. Put these in a free-function executor module. That needs only Engine::DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME and DEFAULT_TESSELLATION_TOLERANCE moved below Engine (see h14 partition).

findings.statement: Four entry points each hand-copy the per-template realization walk around execute_realization_ops: build_snapshot, build_with_geometry_output, tessellate_from_values and distance_between_placed. Each repeats module_named_steps seeding, step construction, demand lookups, assembling a RealizationOpsInput with up to 11 chained with_* calls, and the post-call write-back. Each makes its own inline choice per axis. Cross-let seeding: build only. Schedule-ordered BuildStep walk: build and tessellate only, built from a 30-line block duplicated verbatim in both. demanded_repr: compute_demanded_reprs in build, build_snapshot and distance; voxel_pipeline_demand_overrides in tessellate. demanded_boundary: false on tessellate. prefer_kernel: None on distance. morph_io: disabled on tessellate and distance. module_binds_selector: build paths only. realized_reprs: build only. produced_repr/produced_kernel/input_cone_hash write-back: build and build_snapshot only. mark_realization_failed: build and build_snapshot only. reset_per_build_state: absent from distance, so its dispatches pile onto the previous build's tallies (documented in engine_admin.rs). distance_between_placed carries the contract only as a comment: 'any changes to the realization execution or terminal_handles bookkeeping in build() must be mirrored here'.
findings.proposal: Model each surface as a value, e.g. a SurfacePolicy built from BuildSurface (seeding set, schedule source, demand source, morph enablement, write-back sink). Have one per-template walk take the policy and a write-back sink trait, so each axis is a single decision in one table, not inline at four call sites. Engine-scoped postures (mesh_contract_mode, long_chain_threshold) would then be read once by the walk instead of being threaded per call.

findings.statement: tessellate_from_values collects produced_repr_out and then throws it away, so tessellate_realizations and tessellate_snapshot never update eval_state.snapshot.graph.realizations[id].produced_repr. The inline comment says this was benign only while every tessellate demand was BRep. It says the symmetric write 'MUST close before ζ ships', tracked by #3437. #3437 is done, yet the discard is still in place. Meanwhile the tessellate path now demands non-BRep reprs: voxel_pipeline_demand_overrides (task 5033 Gap D) sets Voxel/Mesh demands for isosurface-pipeline realizations. realization_content.rs projects readable content by matching on node_data.produced_repr, and BRep is identity-only with no content. A tessellate-only session (GUI tessellate_snapshot) for a voxel-terminal realization therefore leaves the node at its construction-time BRep default. The same path also drops kernel_error, so no Freshness::Failed is recorded. Not reproduced at runtime, so this is PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED.
findings.proposal: Return Vec<(RealizationNodeId, ReprKind, Option<ErrorRef>)> from tessellate_from_values and apply it in tessellate_realizations/tessellate_snapshot through the same write-back helper the build surfaces use. This falls out of finding 2's single write-back sink. Add a test that pins produced_repr after tessellate_snapshot on a voxel-terminal fixture.

findings.statement: engine_build.rs production code is 49.1% comment lines, much of it reviewer-answering or history prose, and some of it has drifted. probe_realization_cache is 46 code lines under 135 comment lines. Both its rustdoc and its inline comment say INV-BUILD-1 is 'still `proposed`' and that 'type-level enforcement via a `reset_per_build_state` exhaustive destructure is future work, not yet test-enforced', so the release-mode share of INV-BUILD-3 is unguarded. Yet reset_per_build_state in the same file does that exhaustive destructure, and docs/invariants.md lists INV-BUILD-1 as enforced(type) and says INV-BUILD-3's release-mode standing is strengthened by it. The file has 51 comment lines framed as reviewer/amendment answers. reset_dispatch_tallies is kept as #[allow(dead_code)] solely to anchor a doc link.
findings.proposal: Leave invariant status only in docs/invariants.md, with a one-line `INV-BUILD-3 (docs/invariants.md)` pointer at the assert. Move measurement and rejected-alternative prose into commit history. Delete reset_dispatch_tallies; the lockstep contract already lives in reset_per_build_state and bump_dispatch.

findings.statement: DiagnosticCode has 214 variants carried by 4,449 doc-comment lines (median 18 per variant, max 77). That makes diagnostics.rs 8,021 lines at 73.5% prose, and 90.6% of its 5,160 production lines are prose. Much of the doc restates facts that live elsewhere and drift. There are 206 'Origin:' emitter pointers; 26 of them are file:line coordinates, and both line coordinates I sampled are stale: expr.rs:670-681 now holds the CmpOperandKind constructor, not unbound-identifier, and guards.rs:155 is a parameter list while the UnresolvedType emitter is at :176. One pointer names the retired crate crates/reify-types/src/value.rs::SampledField. There are 166 'PRD-prose mnemonic' lines, and 9 'Minting rationale' paragraphs that repeat why adding a variant is non-breaking. Of the inline tests, 136 of 151 are per-variant exists/attach/serde-PascalCase checks of derived behaviour, with no table-driven all-variants test.
findings.proposal: Make the doc one line per variant: meaning and severity. Emitter location is derivable by `git grep DiagnosticCode::<X>`, so drop Origin/line pointers. Move PRD mnemonics to the PRDs, or to a strum-derived table if tooling needs them. Replace the per-variant serde tests with one EnumIter/strum-driven round-trip test (ty.rs already derives EnumIter for TypeDiscriminants). Moving DiagnosticCode to its own file is symptom-free; see h14.

findings.statement: reify_core::Type (41 variants) has no shared child traversal. So 'does any nested type satisfy P' is re-implemented as separate exhaustive matches that list the same inner-Type-bearing constructor set and differ only in the leaf predicate: type_mentions_conflicted_param (type_compat.rs) vs type_carries_type_param and type_carries_dim_param (reify-core overload.rs). Five more walkers repeat the same constructor classification: unify, substitute_type_params, normalize_type_guarded, walk_type_for_applied, Type's Display. Their doc comments say they are kept 'in lock-step' with each other. Exhaustive matching makes the compiler flag a missing arm, but not a misclassified one: a new inner-bearing variant listed as a leaf in one walker compiles fine.
findings.proposal: Add a `Type::children(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item=&Type>` (and `Type::any_descendant(pred)`) in reify-core, as the single exhaustive classification. Express type_carries_type_param, type_carries_dim_param and type_mentions_conflicted_param as one-line predicates over it. type_carries_trait_object's deliberately narrower walk stays explicit.

findings.statement: type_compat.rs opens with `use super::*;` and imports only EnumDef and two overload predicates explicitly. Type, BinOp, UnOp, CompiledFunction, CompiledExpr, Diagnostic, DiagnosticCode, DiagnosticLabel, SourceSpan, HashMap and HashSet all reach it through the reify-compiler crate root. That root itself glob-re-exports 28 sibling modules (`pub(crate) use <module>::*;`), including `pub(crate) use type_compat::*`. So the crate is one flat namespace: reading this file alone you cannot tell which module or crate a name comes from, and every sibling sees every pub(crate) item of every other.
findings.proposal: Replace `use super::*` with explicit imports, starting with the files under change. Retire the lib.rs `pub(crate) use X::*` globs a module at a time, so dependencies are named and grep-able. Track this as a crate-wide stream; see seams.

findings.statement: AST operators reach the compiler as strings (reify_ast ExprKind::BinOp/UnOp `op: String`). type_compat.rs then parses them ad hoc in several places that must agree with each other: resolve_binop and resolve_unop map strings to BinOp/UnOp, is_comparison_op keeps its own string set ("<","<=",...) that must match resolve_binop's comparison arms, and is_syntactic_zero_literal tests `op == "-"`. Outside this file, type_resolution.rs const-folding matches op.as_str() on "+","-","*","/" (line 449) and on unary "-" (line 488) without going through resolve_binop, and expr.rs:1858 tests `unary_op.as_str() == "-"`.
findings.proposal: Parse operators into BinOp/UnOp at the syntax boundary (ts_parser) so ExprKind carries the enum. is_comparison_op then becomes a method on BinOp, and the string parsers are deleted.

findings.statement: ty.rs, the definition of the most widely shared type in the workspace, opens with a 305-line //! module doc before its first `use`. That doc declares itself 'the single normative home of the quantity-slot conformance rule', a rule implemented in reify-compiler's conformance/mod.rs (an upper layer). It is mostly ruling history and measurement prose: 'the corpus gate was re-run green at this HEAD', 'Task 6159 had corrected only what task 6159 itself authored', and an 'expired premise' section. It also points at the retired crate `crates/reify-types/src/value.rs` for Value::infer_type, which now lives in reify-ir/src/value.rs. Production prose share is 67.3%.
findings.proposal: Move the quantity-slot ruling to docs/ (or to the PRD it came from, dimensioned-construction-strictness.md §12) and point at it from conformance/mod.rs, the implementing site. Keep a short //! in ty.rs describing the type. Drop the measurement and history prose.

findings.statement: reify-core exports a domain-specific, unwired public API: HexWedgeMeshOutcome plus hex_wedge_mesh_diagnostic, a hex/wedge swept-mesh outcome mapper belonging to the reify-eval volume-mesh dispatcher. It has no caller outside diagnostics.rs. Its 'Dead-code note' says wiring is 'blocked on VolumeMesh realization (task #2947)', and #2947 is cancelled. It also says it mirrors p2_substitution_diagnostic's status 'task #2991', which is done. The real blocker for the sibling helper is now #4746 (pending), cited only at engine_build.rs::p2_substitution_diagnostic. The cancelled cite is prose, not in TODO form, so the PTODO ratchet does not see it.
findings.proposal: Move HexWedgeMeshOutcome and hex_wedge_mesh_diagnostic next to p2_substitution_diagnostic in reify-eval, re-cited to #4746 (or delete them and let #4746 author them at the wiring site).

findings.statement: kleene.rs is the single source for the AND/OR/IMPLIES/NOT truth tables, but not for the left-operand absorption rule that drives short-circuit. That rule (False absorbs AND, True absorbs OR, False vacuously satisfies IMPLIES) is written out separately in reify-expr lib.rs eval_and/eval_or/eval_implies and in dual_eval.rs (the `absorbed` match, 'matching `eval_and`/`eval_or`/`eval_implies` exactly'), and both must agree with the kleene tables.
findings.proposal: Add `kleene::left_absorbs(op, lk: KBool) -> Option<KBool>` (with a small Kleene-op enum or taking BinOp) and call it from both eval paths.

findings.statement: Which calls eval_expr intercepts before reify_stdlib::eval_builtin or eval_user_function_call is defined only as inline string-guarded match arms: 23 named FunctionCall arms plus 4 UserFunctionCall families (solve_load_cases/5|6, option_recovery::is_combinator, map_or/3, map_err/2). dual_eval.rs must give 'the same answer in the same place, on the same operand shapes' (its own module doc), so it restates that table by hand: is_intercepted_user_fn repeats the 4 UserFunctionCall gates byte-for-byte, field_reduction_kind/reduction_kind_of/is_kink_builtin repeat the 8 field-reduction arms, and eval_binop's strict-Undef precheck is re-added at two sites. The module doc says a missed mirror fails silently with a WRONG PRIMAL. The guarding test (the_dual_intercept_gate_covers_exactly_the_families_eval_expr_intercepts) lists the families by hand, so it cannot see a fifth family added to eval_expr. The prose that holds the mirror together cites lib.rs by line number, and every cited line is stale. The table is also invisible to the compiler: a user `pub fn map_or(a,b,c)` compiles to UserFunctionCall and is silently replaced at eval, and reserved_name_lint covers type names only.
findings.proposal: Make the interception decision a typed classifier exported once from reify-expr, e.g. `fn classify_call(name, qualified, args) -> Option<Intercept>` for FunctionCall and `fn classify_user_call(name, arity) -> Option<UserIntercept>`, with eval_expr matching on the enum. dual_eval then calls the same classifier, and the compiler's reserved-name lint can query it. A new variant becomes a compile error in every exhaustive consumer, and the line-number prose can be deleted.

findings.statement: compile_expr types every geometry-constructor call (is_geometry_function: box, cylinder, union, sweep, ...) as Type::dimensionless_scalar(), a placeholder that misstates the value's kind. Every consumer that needs the truth has to undo it, either by re-checking the callee name or by overriding the type. conformance/mod.rs (3 sites), geometry.rs (2) and geometry_traits_inference.rs (2, is_geometry_operand) call is_geometry_function on the FunctionCall name. entity.rs sets cell_type explicitly to Type::Geometry and List<Geometry> in two Let-arm branches because 'the general expression compiler types geometry-function calls as dimensionless scalars'. A list literal of geometry calls is typed List<Real>, which a geometry_traits_inference test pins as 'the shape real compilation produces'. The conformance doc points at `expr.rs:782` for the placeholder; the arm is actually at line 3627.
findings.proposal: Type geometry-constructor calls as Type::Geometry in the ladder arm, and remove the name-sniffing fallbacks and entity.rs overrides that compensate for the placeholder. If some consumer depends on the scalar placeholder for content-hash or diagnostic reasons, give it its own explicit marker instead of borrowing a value type.

findings.statement: compile_entity (3,800 lines) works out each let's kind (geometry let, selector let, geometry-list let, rejected list let) as HashSet<&str> locals that live across three passes and a deferred sub-pass. It does not classify each member once. is_geometry_let is called again with known_geometry_lets at 5 sites in compile_entity, plus 1 in the guarded-member helper and 2 in build_structure_def_skeleton. Pass 1 fills the set incrementally (doc: 'order-sensitive (incremental accumulation)'), but pass 2 (line 2929) and pass 3 (lines 4516, 4660) query the completed set. A forward alias (`let shifted = base` declared before `let base = box(..)`) is therefore non-geometry in pass 1's scope registration and geometry in pass 2/3. The pinned test cyclic_ident_alias_does_not_crash covers only the cyclic case. build_structure_def_skeleton re-implements the incremental classification so ctor `lets` stay consistent. Its pointers to the authoritative path (entity.rs:623, 853-856, 822-831, ~631) are stale, and the function doc still describes 'Two-pass compilation'.
findings.proposal: Classify each member once, in pass 1, into a typed per-member `LetKind` (Geometry | Selector | GeometryList(shape) | Rejected | Value). Every later pass and build_structure_def_skeleton reads that classification instead of re-running is_geometry_let against a set, so passes cannot disagree and the skeleton reuses the authoritative answer.

findings.statement: The stdlib function solve_load_cases has four implementations spread across four crates: a placeholder .ri body (fea_multi_case.ri, two overloads), the @optimized trampoline reify-eval/compute_targets/multi_case.rs, a name-intercept fallback in reify-expr (eval_solve_load_cases, resolve_load_case_options, invoke_solve_elastic_static) and a permanent Undef stub in reify-stdlib fea.rs. reify-expr is described as a 'pure recursive evaluator', yet it reads LoadCase fields by string ('name', 'loads', 'supports', 'options', 'cases'). It repeats the empty-cases and duplicate-name diagnostics that multi_case.rs also emits, and multi_case.rs says it 'mirrors resolve_load_case_options in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs'. invoke_solve_elastic_static finds 'solve_elastic_static' by name and arity only. It evaluates the contract body, bypassing @optimized dispatch, and on ANY Undef it returns a field-less stub ElasticResult. Its own comment labels this a KNOWN LIMITATION that masks genuine solve failures. The intercept gates on arity 5|6 only, so the 3|4-arity body:Solid overload is never intercepted.
findings.proposal: Give the per-case semantics one home, in reify-eval next to the trampoline, and have reify-expr route nested calls through the existing compute_dispatch hook instead of re-implementing the driver. Then delete the stub-on-any-Undef fallback.

findings.statement: Value::Field stores its payload in a slot named `lambda: Arc<Value>`, and what the slot holds depends on `source`. For Restricted and Composed it is a positional 2-element List. For SafetyFactor it is List[field, yield]. For AsPrintedZones it is a 7-element List whose third item is itself a positional 7-number List [walls, top_bottom_layers, layer_height, line_width, bx, by, bz]. The only contract is a doc table on reify_ir::Value::Field. sample_field_at and sample_as_printed_zones decode the payload by index (`items.len() == 7`, p[0]..p[6]) and return Undef on any shape mismatch. Two producers, as_printed_material.rs and as_printed_material_r0.rs, each hand-pack the same 7+7 layout. The doc table has already drifted from the code: it says Imported stores Value::Undef, but sample_field_at samples Imported fields as Value::SampledField.
findings.proposal: Replace the positional payloads with typed variants, e.g. `enum FieldPayload { Lambda(..), Sampled(SampledField), Composed{outer, inner}, Restricted{inner, region}, AsPrintedZones(ZonePayload) }`, built and decoded through one constructor, so the layout lives in the type.

findings.statement: expr.rs and entity.rs both open with `use super::*;`, which pulls in reify-compiler lib.rs's 30 `pub(crate) use <module>::*` glob re-exports. Every unqualified identifier in these files can therefore come from any sibling module. expr.rs uses unqualified names from 17 other modules this way (units 27 names, type_compat 19, types 14, orientation_signatures 5, math_signatures 5, ...), and entity.rs uses them from 14. The pattern is crate-wide: 27 reify-compiler modules glob-import their parent, the layering heuristic 13 names as a reach-back. It also hides a misleading name: the result-type ladder's family predicates (is_geometry_query, is_dynamics_query, is_field_op, is_fea_envelope_query, ...) live in units.rs, which reaches expr.rs through the glob.
findings.proposal: Replace the lib.rs globs with explicit `use crate::module::{..}` lists in each consumer, starting with expr.rs and entity.rs. Move the builtin-family predicates out of units.rs into a module named for what it holds.

findings.statement: New evidence that the registry migration has stalled. The NoUserFunctions result-type ladder still has 23 sequential name-predicate arms before the first-arg fallback. Only one of them is the reify-builtins registry, which holds 7 rows. The other 22 arms consult 30 hand-maintained `*_NAMES` slices whose mutual exclusion rests on a hand-written pairwise-disjointness test. Arm-ordering rationale is restated at the arms (the precedence list at 3420-3440 and 'pinned disjoint ... so this arm's position is unobservable' at 7 arms). Separately, the FunctionCall arm intercepts some/filter/cost/generate by bare name ahead of overload resolution, and each intercept carries its own `!functions.iter().any(|f| f.name == ..)` shadowing check. expr.rs has the highest fix count in the slice, 38 commits since 2026-07-06 by the seat's fix-grep.
findings.proposal: Continue registry τ/ω: move each remaining family into reify-builtins rows, delete the arm it replaces, and replace the disjointness test with registry-key uniqueness.

findings.statement: The value layer's rule that arithmetic failure yields Undef, never a panic or a non-finite value, is enforced arm by arm, with no shared mechanism for Int. neg_scalar uses checked_neg and maps overflow to Undef, but eval_add, eval_sub and eval_mul use bare `a + b`, `a - b` and `a * b`. eval_pow uses `base.pow(exp as u32)`. eval_div computes `a % b == 0` and eval_mod computes `a % b` with only a zero-divisor guard. The workspace profile disables overflow checks only for dependencies, so these panic in dev and test builds and wrap silently in release. `i64::MIN % -1` panics in every build mode, so eval_div and eval_mod can panic in release on an Int pair a user can form (e.g. (-9223372036854775807 - 1) % -1).
findings.proposal: Route every Int arm through one helper, `int_op(a, b, i64::checked_*) -> Value` returning Undef on None. It covers add, sub, mul, div, rem and pow alike.

findings.statement: The production part of reify-expr lib.rs (lines 1-4865) is 38.5% comment lines. One rationale accounts for much of that: helpers are #[inline(never)] to keep eval_expr's frame under the 3 MiB test stack at MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH. It is restated in a separate paragraph on 17+ helpers ('3 MiB' appears 17 times and eval_user_fn_recursion_depth_exceeded 22 times). Other docstrings list which test pins each guard (eval_worst_case_dispatch's doc enumerates 7 pinning tests), or carry reviewer-facing history ('suggestion 2', 'review esc-5385-3'). The lib.rs:NNN self-references have drifted too, e.g. 'lib.rs:206' and 'lib.rs:2848'.
findings.proposal: State the stack-budget rule once, in the module doc next to MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH, so that #[inline(never)] needs no per-site prose. Leave pin lists to the tests and move reviewer history to commits.

findings.statement: GeometryKernel is a 27-method trait. Only 4 methods are required (execute, query, export, tessellate); the other 23 are defaulted capability methods that return 'does not support' / 'does not accept' errors. A delegating wrapper therefore loses a capability silently whenever someone adds a method and does not also add a forwarder; the compiler sees nothing wrong. The repo states the invariant ('SingleKernelHolder must delegate EVERY GeometryKernel method', reify-geometry/src/lib.rs) and claims a guard (parity test delegates_all_capability_methods_to_inner_kernel). At this tree SingleKernelHolder forwards 18 of 27 methods, and the parity test lists exactly those 18. The nine methods added since are not delegated and not tested: closest_point_on_shape, vertex_point, register_mesh_handle, volume_mesh, mesh_surface_to_volume, mesh_surface_to_volume_attributed, store_volume_mesh, realize_mesh_from_voxel, surface_options_content_hash. Through the holder, an inner OcctKernelHandle that overrides closest_point_on_shape/vertex_point answers with the trait's 'not supported' error. The holder is used in 55 files, mostly reify-eval integration tests. A second, unchecked encoding of capability exists in CapabilityDescriptor.supports: nothing ties a declared (Convert{from: Mesh}, X) pair to an ingest_mesh override.
findings.proposal: Make delegation total by construction. Either (a) group the capability methods into sub-traits (MeshIngest, VolumeMeshing, PointProjection, ...) exposed through one accessor per capability on GeometryKernel (`fn mesh_ingest(&mut self) -> Option<&mut dyn MeshIngest>`), so a wrapper forwards a handful of accessors and the descriptor's supports pairs can be checked against which accessors return Some; or (b) remove the defaults from the wrapper's path by generating the holder's impl from one macro list that the parity test also iterates. Either way, the parity test should enumerate the trait's methods, not a copied list.

findings.statement: The mesh contract (INV-GEO-1) has one checking body behind four public entry points (validate, into_validated, check_mesh_contract, check_mesh_contract_welded) and two proof newtypes (ValidatedMesh, WeldRemap), but no consumer requires the proof. All 6 Mesh-consuming GeometryKernel methods take a raw &Mesh, and ValidatedMesh appears in zero signatures outside geometry.rs. Enforcement therefore depends on each wiring site remembering to call a validator. Today three sites do: the engine_build conversion handoff (tessellate source only), the Manifold ingest, and the gmsh preflight. OpenVDB's ingest_mesh_at_resolution re-implements a partial IndexValid length check by hand. Both production callers of `validate` discard the minted witness. Because validate clones the whole mesh to mint the witness, both pay a full Mesh clone for nothing. One of them sits on the BRep->Mesh conversion hot path, which validate's own doc says to avoid. into_validated and check_mesh_contract have zero production callers. The checking body itself is one 343-line function (check_contract) that runs five obligation passes in sequence.
findings.proposal: Make the witness load-bearing. Have the Mesh-consuming trait methods (or a validating front door at the dispatcher) take &ValidatedMesh, so a kernel cannot be handed an unchecked mesh. Collapse the four entry points to the borrowing check plus the by-value mint. Split check_contract into one function per obligation so a new obligation is a new function, not an edit inside a 343-line body.

findings.statement: GeometryOp handles 'where a numeric quantity is decoded and unit-checked' two ways. 27 variants carry their numbers as untyped `Value` (47 Value fields): Box, Cylinder, Fillet, Extrude, Shell, the profiles and others. The kernel extracts f64 from these and runs a warn-only LENGTH tripwire. 10 variants carry pre-extracted `f64` / `[f64; 3]`: Translate, Rotate, Scale, RotateAround, ScaleNonUniform, Revolve, LineSegment, Arc, Helix, Surface. For those, only the eval-layer gate applies and the kernel tripwire cannot see them. The tripwire is duplicated per kernel. reify-ir's kernel_validation.rs defines `define_kernel_length_extract!` and documents that 'before this existed the two bodies were copy-pasted', yet the macro has zero invocations. reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs::extract_length_f64 and reify-kernel-fidget/src/kernel.rs::extract_length_f64 are still hand-copied bodies that differ only in the tracing target. The macro arrived in a 'chore: save WIP before requeue rebase' commit (702c4605e6).
findings.proposal: Pick one decode point for quantity fields. Either carry a typed length/angle newtype in GeometryOp, built only through the eval-layer gate, so kernels receive SI f64 they cannot misread, or keep Value everywhere and route all kernels through the one macro. In the short term, invoke define_kernel_length_extract! in both kernels and delete the copies.

findings.statement: GeometryKernel::query returns an untyped `Value` for all 35 GeometryQuery variants. Each reply's shape (Value::Real / Bool / List of Int / String) is specified only in variant doc prose, 34 such statements, and each consumer re-decodes it. FaceSurfaceKind and EdgeCurveKind show the cost most clearly. reify-ir already defines both typed enums, yet the OCCT kernel returns them as `Value::String` straight from the C++ FFI (occt lib.rs:4160). reify-eval then re-parses the string through try_from_str at three production sites: selector_vocabulary_v2.rs (errors on unknown names), feature_datum.rs:410 (silently ignores parse failures), and geometry_ops.rs (user-argument parsing). Each nine-name vocabulary is written out in four places: the occt_wrapper.cpp switch, try_from_str, the hard-coded 'expected one of Plane/Cylinder/…' literal in geometry_ops.rs, and the test-support mock.
findings.proposal: Parse at the boundary. Add typed reply variants (e.g. Value::SurfaceKind(FaceSurfaceKind), or a typed `QueryReply` enum keyed by query) and decode the FFI string once inside the OCCT kernel. Derive the diagnostic name list from the enum (strum EnumIter) instead of a literal.

findings.statement: StructureInstanceData keeps engine metadata inside its public user-field map under reserved string keys: MATERIALIZED_ANNOTATIONS_KEY = "@@materialized_annotations" (a nested Value::Map keyed by Value::String) and SOURCE_SPAN_KEY = "@@source_span" (a SourceSpan encoded as Value::List[Int, Int] and decoded back with `as u32` casts). The rule that these entries are not fields is enforced by a private filter, user_fields(), which compares keys against both constants. It is called at 9 sites in value.rs (content hash, PartialEq, Ord, Display). But `fields` is `pub`, and production code outside value.rs iterates it directly with no filter, e.g. reify-eval tolerance_combine.rs:533 and engine_build.rs:13170. The exclusion invariant therefore holds only for code that knows about the filter.
findings.proposal: Move the overlays out of `fields` into typed fields on StructureInstanceData (e.g. `annotations: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Value>>`, `source_span: Option<SourceSpan>`), left out of Eq/Ord/hash by construction. Then `fields` holds only user members and user_fields() disappears.

findings.statement: 'Should this trait default be advertised/injected?' is encoded as four parallel HashSet<String> skip sets on PreRegisterOutput: pass1_skipped, pass1_param_skipped, pass2_skipped and pass2_compile_errors. check_trait_conformance passes them as four separate arguments into two phases, check_phase_build_available_defaults_map and check_phase_inject_defaults. Each phase re-implements the same ladder of guards, including the cell_type.is_some()/is_none() conjunctions that make the Let guards mutually exclusive. Each set and guard pair was added by its own fix task (1914, 1951, 1952, 2208), and the guards cite those tasks inline: the 'same bug fixed once per path' shape. The set-to-guard table exists only as doc prose on PreRegisterOutput.
findings.proposal: Have the pre-register phase compute one disposition per default, `enum DefaultDisposition { Inject, SkippedSlotTaken, CompileError, … }` keyed by (name, kind), and have both phases consult a single `disposition()` accessor. A new skip reason is then a new variant, matched exhaustively in one place.

findings.statement: The conformance test module (6,076 lines, 69% of mod.rs) mostly drives internal seams rather than the compiler's public entry. Of its 79 tests, 20 hand-build a MergeContext and call individual pub(super) check_phase_* functions. 18 call the pub(crate) check_fn_arg_conformance directly. 1 goes through compile_source. Each check_phase_* has exactly one production caller (check_trait_conformance), so pub(super) visibility exists only for these tests. The module doc that justifies the arrangement is stale: it says 'All four tests in this module…' while there are 79. It concedes that two tests hand-build a RequirementKind::Let that 'no parser path produces'. It sends the reader to 'the escalate_info record for task 2033' for the rationale, a pointer the Comments stance says does not count.
findings.proposal: Express the phase-level cases as .ri fixtures through the compile entry, or through one narrow pub(crate) seam such as check_trait_conformance. Delete the tests that pin parser-unreachable states, or make those states unrepresentable. Replace the module doc with a pointer to a tracked doc, or drop it.

findings.statement: Comments in geometry.rs's production region (59% comment lines) record task-progress facts that later commits have made false, and the worst of them invert the point of truth. (1) GEOMETRY_OP_DESCRIPTORS' doc says it covers 'all 49 GeometryOp variants' (there are 55 rows and 55 variants). It also says its operation/parent_role columns are an 'unverified copy until L2 rewires geometry_op_to_operation and parent_handles_for_op … cross-check against the source functions when modifying either'. L2 has landed (7e0f2e0e5b, 4cdda71204): both functions now read this table. (2) ParentRole's doc still says 'see parent_handles_for_op for the authoritative source'. (3) FeatureId::content_hash_bytes is `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment that its only caller is the golden test; value.rs:2074 calls it in production. (4) TopologyAttributeTable::lookup_result_face says its production caller (#4263) 'has not landed yet'; reify-kernel-manifold kernel.rs:1211 calls it. (5) A `G-allow` marker on capability_kind cites task #3623 as done. Fix history on the file confirms the cost: 19 of 87 non-merge commits since 2026-07-06 are prose maintenance.
findings.proposal: Delete the drift and progress narration: the table is authoritative, ParentRole is defined by the table, remove the stale dead_code allow and the not-landed notes. Keep task-progress facts (what has or hasn't landed, counts) out of code comments; they belong in the commit or task record.

findings.statement: walk_param_against_arg_type is a second home for the argument-to-parameter compatibility rules that type_compat.rs::type_compatible owns. Of its 12 match arms, 4 defer to type_compatible (via reject_if_incompatible), while the Vector, Point, Matrix/Tensor, Field and TraitObject arms implement their own family and arity rules. Some of those deliberately differ from type_compatible: the Vector arm accepts any Tensor{rank:1} regardless of n, while type_compatible's Rule 1a/1b requires n equality. The arms explain the divergence in comments that cite type_compat.rs by line number ('type_compat.rs:83-108'). The function spans 444 lines, of which 316 are comments (71%), around 128 lines of code. conformance/mod.rs's production region is 60% comments, and 23 of its 67 non-merge commits since 2026-07-06 maintain that prose: 'retire the point3-erasure premise', 'correct two false prose claims', 'stop narrating the comments' own edit history'.
findings.proposal: Move the shape-based acceptance rules next to type_compatible as one named relation (e.g. `conformance_accepts(param, arg) -> Acceptance`) with the deliberate differences written as code, not comments. The walker then only recurses through wrappers and emits diagnostics, and the rationale moves to the PRD or language spec with a one-line pointer.

findings.statement: resolve_joint_nominal_type's Path B hard-codes a second table that maps the 10 joint-constructor builtin names to nominal joint type names (couple/gear/screw/rack_and_pinion -> Coupling; fixed; prismatic/revolute/cylindrical/planar/spherical). The same mapping already exists in the same crate in joint_signatures.rs::joint_ctor_result_type, which is what sets those calls' result_type (Type::StructureRef / Type::applied("Coupling", …)), and it is reachable from conformance through the crate-root `pub(crate) use joint_signatures::*`. Its DRIFT NOTE names the wrong sync partner: it says the table must track JOINT_KINDS in reify-stdlib (unreachable from here) and does not mention the in-crate function that is the actual source.
findings.proposal: Derive Path B from joint_ctor_result_type(name, &[]) (taking the StructureRef/Applied name), or delete Path B if Path A already covers every FunctionCall whose result_type that function sets.

findings.statement: Engine::edit_source has no production caller, yet it keeps a hand copy of each edit_param phase: guard re-elaboration, solver resolution, wave-2, post-wave2 reseed and collection resize. 301 non-comment lines sit in matching runs of 6 or more lines between the two (31% of edit_param's code, 37% of edit_source's). The longest run is the 96-line solver-resolution block. The copies are linked only by 'Paired with … change them together' / 'mirrors' comments, and they have already diverged in at least four places. (a) Post-wave2 reseed: task #4707 (d248baef96) relaxed edit_param's reseed to the full demanded downstream cone and added the same cone pass to cold eval (engine_eval.rs 'Task #4707: cold driver-ordered guarded-member downstream cone'). edit_source's copy is still 'BOUNDED to members ∩ demand — no downstream cone (matches cold semantics)', so its comment is now false. (b) Wave-2: edit_param's is guard-aware and deactivates inactive members. edit_source's still evaluates the default_expr of every wave-2 cell, which is the shape edit_param's comment gives as the reason the legacy wave was retired. (c) Eval contexts: edit_source's Phase 1 members, post-wave2 active members and collection-resize cells use eval_ctx_with_meta without determinacy or containment (4 sites). edit_param uses cell_eval_ctx there (INV-EVAL-2). This is forced by structure: PendingWarmSeedsGuard holds &mut self.warm_pool from line 3328 to line 4583, so `self` cannot serve as the ContainmentQuery. (d) Journaling: edit_source's post-wave2 active member and its collection-resize cells use bare values and snapshot inserts with no journal. edit_param routes both through commit_cell_result with CacheLeg::Skip (INV-EVAL-1).
findings.proposal: Decide what edit_source is for. If no consumer is planned, delete it with its 15 test files' calls and its instrumentation fields (last_role_flip_probes, last_diff_value_cells). If it stays, move the post-eval phases into shared methods that take an explicit structural context (reverse index, trace map, demand), and scope PendingWarmSeedsGuard so it no longer spans those phases. Then both entries run one copy with cell_eval_ctx.

findings.statement: Engine::edit_param is the production warm-edit path (reify-cli mcp_context.rs, GUI param edits). It is one 1938-line function: 883 comment lines and 977 code lines, brace depth 9, approximate decision count 115. It runs eight banner-delimited phases in sequence: main walk, composed fields, guard re-elaboration, resolution, resolution reseed, post-wave2 reseed, collection resize with forall re-elaboration, and realization eviction. They communicate through 28 function-scope locals, 12 of them `let mut` (values, new_snapshot, skipped, has_changed_parent, diagnostics, structural_mutation, phase1_reelaborated, …), each alive from its declaration to the return. The prose is mostly task provenance and review defence (142 comment lines cite task numbers; 31 are review-round or amend narratives, e.g. 'Verified (reviewer amend, round 2): a repo-wide grep…'), not a contract the next agent needs.
findings.proposal: Turn the eight phases into named methods over an explicit edit-transaction value. The value would own new_snapshot, values and the sinks, and each phase would return what the next one reads (phase1_reelaborated, structural_mutation, resolved ids). Move the provenance and review prose into commit messages or the PRD.

findings.statement: The 'Warm-Resolution back-prop' contract is held in a 109-line module-doc roster at the top of engine_edit.rs (lines 26-134). It lists six arms across engine_eval.rs and engine_edit.rs and, for each, which of eight legs it writes, and it ends with the instruction 'Check all eight legs when modifying'. No primitive enforces this. Each arm hand-rolls the solve loop and its SolveResult handling: the literal 'Constraint solver made no progress' appears at 6 code sites (engine_edit.rs ×2, engine_eval.rs ×4), and 'resolved via auto(free)' at 5. The leg differences between arms (journal vs no journal, resolved_params written or not, objective_provenance only on eval) live only in prose, so the doc has needed its own correction commits (56badf0b7c, 561d645fd6).
findings.proposal: Introduce one resolution write-back primitive (solve outcome to commits plus diagnostics plus resolved-id set), with the per-arm leg differences passed as explicit policy values, the same way CacheLeg does it for cell commits. Then shrink the roster to a pointer.

findings.statement: Three rules that change what a name resolves to are passed through thread-local ambient sets installed by RAII guards, not through arguments. They are RESOLUTION_ENUM_NAMES (EnumNameScope), RESOLUTION_SHADOWING_ENUM_NAMES (LocalEnumShadowScope) and ALIAS_DEFER_IN_PROGRESS (AliasDeferScope). Each is justified as avoiding a signature change across '~100 call sites'. The measured production callers outside the file are 23 for resolve_type_expr_with_aliases and 6 for _kinded. Whether a resolution sees enum names depends on whether some caller up the stack installed the scope: temporal coupling the call does not show. The doc lists the install sites ('installed … at exactly four sites'; 'Keep this list in sync: grep … is the authority'). That list is already stale: validate_pub_parametric_alias_def_site in the same file became a fifth production site in 77c80cdcfb (2026-09-19). The doc had already been corrected once before that (c48d38a698, 2026-09-01). That function also receives enum_names as an explicit parameter and re-installs it ambiently just so a callee can read it. A missing install has already caused a silent warning-to-error regression (esc-5429-1, recorded in the doc).
findings.proposal: Put the alias registry, structure/trait/enum name sets, the shadow set and the in-progress set into one ResolutionCtx passed by reference. That is one mechanical signature change at about 55 sites, and it removes all three ambient channels and their prose.

findings.statement: Type-expression resolution varies on two independent axes: substitution or not, and full Type vs DimensionVector result. Each combination has its own hand-written function: resolve_type_alias_expr, resolve_type_alias_expr_with_subst, resolve_type_alias_expr_to_dimension and resolve_type_alias_expr_to_dim_with_subst, plus the builtin pair resolve_parameterized_builtin_type and resolve_parameterized_builtin_type_with_subst. The 12-name parameterized-builtin table is therefore written four times: is_parameterized_builtin_name, two independent 12-arm `match name` blocks, and the drift-guard test list. The two builtin matchers have diverged. The base resolver's Scalar, Vector3 and Point3 arms classify dimension-param slots (classify_dim_slot, about 30 lines each, emitting DimParamKind). The subst variant's arms go straight to the dimension resolver. The drift test pins only the predicate's name set, so an arm added to or changed in one matcher is not caught in the other.
findings.proposal: Drive both matchers from one per-constructor table (arity, slot kinds, how to build the Type), with substitution as a parameter of a single resolver rather than a twin function.

findings.statement: Geometry builtins are identified by string names that are restated across files. compile_geometry_call_inner is one 1581-line function dispatching on 60 name arms (approximate CCN ~117). The same names appear again in units.rs GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES (65 names), in geometry.rs geometry_arg_indices (35 names, with a silent `_ => &[]` default and a prose 'IMPORTANT … MUST be registered here' warning), in check_profile_preconditions arms, in geometry_traits_inference.rs, in reify-ir GEOMETRY_OP_DESCRIPTORS, and in reify-eval geometry_ops.rs. The reify-ir descriptor table already records which builtins take a geometry argument (parent_role), so geometry_arg_indices restates a fact that has a home. The duplicates are kept consistent by cross-check tests (geometry_arg_indices_consistent_with_descriptor_table, all_dispatch_functions_accounted_for, the traits-inference coverage test). That reconciliation-by-census is the smell, not the cure.
findings.proposal: Key dispatch, arg indices and trait inference off the reify-ir descriptor (or a typed builtin enum parsed once at the call boundary), and split the match into per-family lowering functions selected by descriptor role.

findings.statement: persistent_cache.rs keeps `pub use` re-export shims for six names that moved to other crates or modules: PersistentlyCacheable (to reify-core, #3834); ElasticResult, ShellChannels, AposterioriEstimate and max_deflection_magnitude (to reify-compute-contract, #4934); and compose_engine_version_hash. The docs on these say they exist so every existing `reify_eval::persistent_cache::…` import path keeps resolving. 45 import sites still use the old paths, 18 of them in tests; compose_engine_version_hash's shim has no users at all.
findings.proposal: Repoint the 45 imports to reify_core::persistent_cache / reify_compute_contract and delete the shims.

findings.statement: persistent_cache.rs's `mod tests` (3873 lines, 66% of the file) opens with about 830 lines and 29 #[test] functions that exercise a different module, engine_hash_algo (walk_contributor, parse_cargo_lock_packages, cargo_lock_closure_parts/pins, contributor_paths, compose_engine_version_hash). engine_hash_algo.rs itself has no test module. A reader of engine_hash_algo.rs therefore cannot find its tests, and persistent_cache.rs carries a test surface that is not about the cache.
findings.proposal: Move these tests into a #[cfg(test)] module in engine_hash_algo.rs (build.rs's include!() compiles without cfg(test), so it ignores the module), or into a sibling engine_hash_algo_tests.rs.

findings.statement: reify-syntax keeps `pub use reify_ast::*;`, labelled TRANSIENT so that integration tests using `use reify_syntax::*` keep resolving AST types until a test-import sweep. That premise no longer holds. No code anywhere imports an AST type through reify_syntax: the only `use reify_syntax::*` in the tree is the doc comment describing the shim. The remaining dependents are two rustdoc intra-doc links in reify-compiler (dot_chain_lint.rs:192 `reify_syntax::MAX_MEMBER_NESTING_DEPTH`, diagnostics.rs:4 `reify_syntax::NumberClass::LossyReal`) plus prose comments.
findings.proposal: Delete the glob re-export and its TRANSIENT doc block, and repoint the two intra-doc links to reify_ast.

findings.statement: docs/invariants.md registers INV-EVAL-2 ('Engine cell-eval contexts always carry determinacy, runtime-diagnostics sink, and containment') as type-enforced by the required-args cell_eval_ctx. The optional-capability builder eval_ctx_with_meta is still pub(crate) and unrestricted, though. It is used at 22 sites in engine_eval.rs against 3 cell_eval_ctx calls. Only 1 of those 22 carries all three capabilities: the dead Engine::cell_eval_ctx method, `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))]`. 21 lack containment and 14 lack the runtime sink. This produces cold/warm divergence on the same cell kind. Cold Let evaluation (evaluate_params_and_lets_unified and evaluate_let_bindings, around 10812 and 11947) has no containment, while eval_cached's Let branch (around 8795) uses cell_eval_ctx with containment. Per the method's own doc, `sample(restrict(field, region), point)` in a let therefore yields Undef on cold eval but a value on eval_cached. Cold Param default evaluation (around 10343) has no runtime sink, while eval_cached's Param default (around 8564) has one. cell_eval_ctx.rs's doc still says the method coexists 'until delta/epsilon (#5056/#5057) migrate', and both tasks are done.
findings.proposal: Make eval_ctx_with_meta private to the module that defines cell_eval_ctx, or rename it to say it is the capability-less base. Route every engine cell-eval site through cell_eval_ctx, with the documented exceptions (record_op_contract_failures, objective_term_contributions) given their own named constructor. Delete the dead Engine::cell_eval_ctx method.

findings.statement: INV-EVAL-3 ('post-pass detectors run identically on all eval paths ... shared detector registry') has its mechanism in place: DetectorRegistry/PostPassDetector, wired into eval, eval_cached and edit_check. Only one detector is registered, though: MassPropertiesPsdDetector. The other value-scan detectors are free fns in engine_eval.rs. Five of them (detect_mechanism_errors, detect_nondriving_joint_errors, detect_kinematic_singularity, detect_unresolved_ad_hoc_selectors, detect_unresolved_geometry_consumers) are hand-listed at both Engine::eval and Engine::eval_cached, each with a 'mirrors eval() call site' comment. Four more (detect_underdetermined, detect_ambiguous_inherited_objectives, detect_robustness_floor_applied, the coupling/approximated-cluster diagnostics) run only in eval. Their eval-only status is recorded in prose that cites a function, `detect_scope_coupling`, which no longer exists anywhere in the tree, along with stale line numbers.
findings.proposal: Register the five value-scan detectors as PostPassDetector impls; they need only values plus templates and a kernel-less flag, so PostPassState gains read-only module context. Give the eval-only ones an explicit per-path applicability on the detector itself, so the asymmetry is data the registry enforces rather than prose.

findings.statement: Five eval-side re-implementations of solver-side predicates are justified in their docs by a premise that is false at this tree. has_inequality_slack mirrors collect_slack_terms; objective_is_money mirrors solver.rs::objective_is_money; scope_qualifies_for_centrality mirrors build_centrality_objective's gate; scope_qualifies_for_robustness_floor mirrors collect_floor_terms and the lambda dispatch; Engine::objective_term_contributions' sigma-fold mirrors eval_objective_set. The premise is that reify-eval cannot call reify-constraints ('reify-eval src does NOT depend on reify-constraints (only a dev-dep)'). In fact reify-constraints is a normal dependency (crates/reify-eval/Cargo.toml, promoted by task 4386), and engine_eval.rs already calls reify_constraints::objective_consumption. reify_constraints::build_centrality_objective is even pub. Each doc asks the next editor to 'apply the same change to all sides' by hand.
findings.proposal: Expose the solver-side predicates (slack-bearing constraint, Money objective, centrality and floor qualification, signed term contribution) as pub fns in reify-constraints, call them from engine_eval.rs, and delete the five mirrors and their lockstep prose.

findings.statement: Prose is 45.3% of engine_eval.rs's production lines. Much of it is reviewer-answering prose, which belongs in commit messages or the task record: review-round and amendment narratives, 'MEASURED' results, rejected alternatives, and confessions such as 'the falsehood this comment carried until amendment round 2'. Positional coordinates have already drifted, e.g. 'engine_eval.rs:609-614', 'L3119', '~line 5270', '(`:472`)'. The prose has also produced a mis-stitched rustdoc: nondriving_joint_compile_spans' doc opens with detect_error_map_diagnostics' description and algorithm steps 1-3, and detect_error_map_diagnostics' doc begins at step 4. cell_eval_ctx.rs and Engine::cell_eval_ctx's docs describe a migration state that #5056/#5057 completed. A reader cannot tell from the file which prose is a current contract and which is history.
findings.proposal: Re-home review narratives and measurements to commit messages or task records. Keep at most a one-line contract per function, with a pointer to the PRD section for design rationale. Fix the mis-stitched detect_error_map_diagnostics/nondriving_joint_compile_spans docs mechanically. Ban positional line references in favour of symbol paths.

findings.statement: Guarded-group member activation is spelled four times with different rules: Engine::eval's third-pass members loop, its near-identical else_members loop, post_solver_re_eval_guard_cells, and eval_guarded_group_param_cell. The third pass routes Param members through eval_guarded_group_param_cell, which honours and validates param_overrides. The post-solver pass, which re-runs whenever a solver is attached, re-evaluates every active Param member from default_expr and never consults param_overrides. Yet the comment at its call site says the pass is 'idempotent with the earlier pass for guards that don't depend on auto params'. Inactive Auto members are written (Undef, Auto) by the third pass but skipped by the post-solver pass. The third pass's Let and Auto arms bypass commit_cell_result entirely, with no cache or journal legs, while its Param arm commits all four legs. eval_cached sidesteps the whole question by falling back to a full eval() for any module with guarded groups (task 5240).
findings.proposal: One `activate_guarded_group(group, guard_value, phase)` that owns the per-kind active/inactive rule (Param via the override-aware path, Let, Auto) and commits through commit_cell_result. The cold third pass, the post-solver pass and a future warm path then all call it.

findings.statement: compile_modify_op routes on the builtin's name string ("shell", "thicken", "offset_curve", "draft", ...). It lowers positional arguments into CompiledGeometryOp::Modify { args: Vec<(String, CompiledExpr)> }, minting string keys ("target", "thickness", "face_{i}", "third", "faces", "angle", "plane", "open_faces"). reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs then re-finds each argument by string comparison (`args.iter().find(|(n, _)| n == "open_faces")`, lookup_named_arg_value). The key vocabulary has no shared definition across the two crates, so a misspelled key on either side compiles and degrades to None. The file also opens with `use super::*`, a glob reach-back into its parent module; 83 reify-compiler source files do the same.
findings.proposal: Make each Modify kind carry a typed argument struct (or an enum of per-kind arg records) built once at the compile boundary, so geometry_ops destructures fields instead of searching strings. Replace `use super::*` with explicit imports.

findings.statement: The only marker of connector-synthesized sub-component instances is a name prefix. It is minted once as `format!("__connector_{}", ...)` in reify-compiler/src/connect.rs. It is recognised by three independent `starts_with("__connector_")` checks: connector_pin_if_determined and is_strict_connector_instance_auto in engine_eval.rs, and resolve_order.rs. Each repeats the literal, and none shares a const or a typed flag. SubComponentDecl's fields carry no origin marker. The instance itself is found by string-stripping "<template.name>." off ValueCellId.entity, which callers precompute and pass in as a `prefix: &str`.
findings.proposal: Add a typed `origin: SubOrigin::{Declared, Connector(index)}` to SubComponentDecl at the connect.rs mint, and have the three recognisers match on it.

findings.statement: 21 of the 35 Diagnostic::warning/error constructors in engine_eval.rs's production code carry no DiagnosticCode. These include the param-override type-kind and dimension rejections, unknown-structure, the three cycle errors, 'Constraint solver made no progress', and auto(free) non-uniqueness. reify-lsp's own guidance is 'match on the code, never on this prose'. For three of them, tests do not match on a code. Instead, the Engine keeps test-instrumentation counters: last_param_override_type_kind_rejections, last_param_override_dimension_rejections and last_sub_component_unknown_structure_errors. These are reset at the top of both eval and eval_cached and threaded by &mut through GuardedParamCtx and emit_param_override_rejection_warning's signature, and they are read only by tests via cfg(test-instrumentation) accessors. Production signatures carry test state because the diagnostic is not structured.
findings.proposal: Give these diagnostics DiagnosticCodes, have tests count by code in EvalResult.diagnostics, and delete the three counters and their threading.

findings.statement: Handling of a per-scope solve outcome has six hand-maintained arms, and they implement different step sets. The arms are: Engine::eval single-scope, Engine::dispatch_merged_cluster_solve, Engine::eval_cached single-scope, Engine::dispatch_merged_cluster_solve_cached, and engine_edit.rs's edit_param and edit_source solver blocks. Only the two cold arms do these steps: call solve_ranked_with_dispatch and emit W_SOLVER_OPTIMALITY_UNPROVEN, record objective_provenance, run materialize_dependent_cells (the joint-drive write-back its doc calls the PRD section 6.3 PRIMARY INVARIANT), emit E_OBJECTIVE_UNCONSUMED, record undef-cause solve failures, and stamp SnapshotProvenance::Resolution. All four warm/edit arms omit every one of these. The auto(free) non-uniqueness warning has a shared helper (push_merged_cluster_nonunique_warnings) used by 2 arms, while the other 4 inline the identical format string. Solver-value write-back is Started/Completed-journaled on the cold arms and a bare cache record with no journal on eval_cached. governing_objective's doc nevertheless asserts eval and eval_cached build a 'byte-identical solver invariant'. The arms are not copies of one another (code similarity 0.23 to 0.36), so the divergence is in what each arm does, not in its spelling.
findings.proposal: Give 'apply a SolveResult to a scope set' one owner. It takes the problem, solve result, optimality, pinned autos, a WritebackPolicy for cold or warm let re-propagation, and whether to record provenance. It returns the resolved ids and diagnostics. Each arm then varies only by the explicit policy values, so an intentionally absent step is visible as a policy choice rather than a missing line.

findings.statement: The cold path has two Let-cell evaluators that are near-copies: the Let arm of Engine::evaluate_params_and_lets_unified and Engine::evaluate_let_bindings. Each carries the same pre-eval Pending gate, the same @optimized compute-dispatch branch (with Final-gate reuse, Ok/Cancelled/Failed outcomes and six record_subpath_started insertions), and the same arch section 9.1 catch_unwind boundary. Each also carries the same symbolic-mint fallback and commit_cell_result call. Both copies special-case `target == "solver::elastic_static"` to call insert_shell_extract_upstream. That function indexes the FEA builtin's positional signature (arg_values[1..=3], arg_values[6]) and does a fn-local `use crate::compute_targets::{elastic_static, shell_solve}::...` (a deferred import) inside the generic evaluator. Task #5238 had to migrate the main let commit onto commit_cell_result twice, once per copy (bfd1ae1a54, 9fd6cabe30).
findings.proposal: Extract one `eval_let_cell(cell, ctx, pass: LetPass)` that both passes call, where LetPass carries the real differences. Move the shell-extract upstream insertion behind a per-target hook in the compute registry, keyed by target with a typed arg-binding view, so the generic evaluator names no target string and no positional index.

findings.statement: The arch section 9.1 panic boundary (catch_unwind around reify_expr::eval_expr, with the panic mapped to Freshness::Failed plus EventKind::Failed) is applied at exactly 2 of the cell-eval sites: the cold Let arms in evaluate_params_and_lets_unified and evaluate_let_bindings. eval_cached's Let branch evaluates the same expression with no boundary, and so do its Param default, the cold Param arm, the guarded-group, structural-query and self-datum post-passes, and all 14 eval_expr sites in engine_edit.rs (which has 0 non-test catch_unwind). eval_cached is the path reify-lsp calls on unchanged content (reify-lsp/src/diagnostics.rs). So an expression panic that the cold eval downgrades to a Failed cell escapes on the warm/LSP path.
findings.proposal: Move the boundary into the shared cell-eval step (the cell_eval_ctx plus commit seam), so every cell-eval site gets Failed-on-panic uniformly. Alternatively, make eval_expr's panic recovery a property of the context that cell_eval_ctx always sets.

findings.statement: reify-compiler's crate root re-exports 28 sibling modules wholesale (`pub(crate) use X::*;`, 5 of them under #[allow(unused_imports)]), and its own comment says this exists 'for internal cross-module access via `use super::*;`'. 25 of the 56 top-level src files begin with `use super::*;`, so every pub(crate) item of 28 modules is in scope, unqualified, in each of them. Reading one file therefore never tells you where its callees live. guards.rs calls 17 crate functions unqualified from 6 different files, traits.rs 12 from 4, forall_elaborate.rs 7 from 4. The mesh also hides a module cycle. entity.rs (8,264 lines) calls guards.rs's compile_block_guard/compile_guarded_members/register_guarded_names/compile_per_decl_guard 6 times. guards.rs calls back into entity.rs's build_param_value_cell_decl, build_auto_let_value_cell_decl, resolve_auto_let_cell_type and fixup_option_none_for_let, which makes guards.rs a satellite of entity.rs rather than a layer under it.
findings.proposal: Replace the crate-root globs with explicit `use crate::<module>::{names}` per file, starting with the slice's leaves (guards, traits, forall_elaborate, geometry_list). Move the param/let cell-builder helpers that guards.rs takes back from entity.rs into a lower module that both import, so the dependency runs one way. Add a check that fails on new `pub(crate) use X::*` lines.

findings.statement: docs/invariants.md registers INV-EVAL-1 (atomic four-leg cell commit) with mechanism 'type (commit_cell_result primitive, CacheLeg::Skip)'. The module doc claims 'no call path can write a subset of the legs by omission'. That holds only for callers that choose the primitive. CacheStore::record_evaluation, record_evaluation_with_freshness and record_evaluation_propagating_freshness are all `pub`. engine_eval.rs still hand-rolls value-cell commits that write values/snapshot/cache/journal inline in at least 7 places the module doc does not list as exemptions: write_solved_pinned_connector_autos, the auto-solve result write in eval at ~6408, reeval_cone_cell (the very site DeterminacyRule::DeriveFromValue was minted for), two eval_cached arms, and evaluate_params_and_lets_unified's Auto pre-seed. These are in addition to the 4 documented failure-path writes and the documented reserve_preserving_determinacy_direct.
findings.proposal: Make the CacheStore value-write methods pub(super) or route them through a sealed handle that only cell_commit (and the named failure-shape entry point) can construct. Migrate the 7 sites or list each one in the module doc. Update the invariants.md mechanism column to match what actually enforces it.

findings.statement: CompilationScope is a clone-per-lambda/quantifier/match-arm struct with 30 `pub(crate)` fields and thin methods. Other files populate and read it directly: 188 field accesses from 11 files outside scope.rs (expr.rs 105, entity.rs 50, member_path.rs 14, connect.rs 6, ...). Its cross-field invariants are stated in field docs and kept true by callers in other files, not by the type. Examples: 'geometry_list_rejected is disjoint from geometry_list_elements by construction'; 'match_arm_groups.keys() == match_arm_group_arm_member_types.keys() is enforced by an unconditional assert! in compile_entity'; 'populated in the entity.rs Sub pre-pass'; the five sibling sub_* maps 'populated at both Sub pre-pass sites'. That doc prose is 56% of the file.
findings.proposal: Group the sub_* maps into one per-sub record populated by a single constructor from the resolved child template, and make the geometry-list pair a single enum-valued map. Then make fields private behind query methods, so invariants live in the type and the field docs shrink to contracts.

findings.statement: The reflective purpose-query kind is a closed set of three values ('params', 'geometric_params', 'material_params'), carried as String end to end: in reify-compiler ResolvedSchemaQuery.query_kind, in reify-ir CompiledExprKind::PurposeReflectiveAggregation.query_kind, and through reify-eval's expand_purpose_reflective_placeholders. compile_purpose produces the three resolved queries with an inline Param|Auto plus is_geometric_param_type / is_material_param_type filter. engine_purposes re-implements the same three-way filter as chained string comparisons for its fallback path. An unrecognised kind silently resolves to an empty member list, which makes the forall vacuously true. ResolvedSchemaQuery's own doc names a fourth kind, 'ports', which neither producer nor consumer handles.
findings.proposal: Introduce a `ReflectiveQueryKind` enum in reify-ir with one `cell_matches(kind, cell_kind, cell_type)` predicate. Have compile_purpose, the IR node and engine_purposes all carry the enum and call the predicate, and make the unknown case unrepresentable.

findings.statement: For a deferred-count `forall v in subs: connect ...`, elaborate_forall_connect substitutes the placeholder element `<sub>[0]` and flattens each endpoint to a String via resolve_port_name. It stores the strings as CompiledForallBody::Connect.left_port_template / right_port_template. At runtime engine_edit.rs::rewrite_port_placeholder produces element i with `template.replacen("<sub>[0]", "<sub>[i]", 1)`. A user-written literal `vents[0].foo` is therefore rewritten to `vents[i].foo`. rewrite_port_placeholder's own doc concedes that this diverges from the resolved (non-deferred) path, and leaves it unguarded. The same function also emits user-visible Info diagnostics that call tasks 2629, 2690 and 2717 'future scope', though all three are done. The module doc still says the Connect body is unsupported at runtime (task 2690), while engine_edit.rs materialises CompiledForallBody::Connect.
findings.proposal: Carry the endpoint as a typed path, e.g. `PortPath { root: Element | Literal(String), index: ElementIndex | Fixed(i64), members: Vec<String> }`. Then per-element materialisation substitutes the element index structurally and never touches a literal index. Drop the task citations from the Info messages.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: Removed by c225a44d88 (typed PortPath for deferred forall-connect; rewrite_port_placeholder deleted, git grep finds no rewrite_port_placeholder/left_port_template) and 2a621eb39d (Info diagnostics no longer cite done tasks 2629/2690/2717 as future scope; module doc now states Connect bodies are captured). Task #8734 done. The sibling Constraint-body placeholder collision (types.rs CompiledForallBody::Constraint doc, engine_edit.rs map_value_refs) remains, but #8792 (pending) owns it.; task store: [('8734', 'done')]

findings.statement: commit_cell_result_at encodes whether the cache leg was skipped, which its doc calls 'the journal-only source of truth', by appending `|cache-skip=<reason>` to the Started event's EventPayload::Custom string. The divergence audit that consumes it, cache_divergence.rs, parses that string with `s.contains("cache-skip=")`. The paired Completed event carries `outcome: cache_outcome.unwrap_or(EvalOutcome::Changed)` on the Skip path: a value that claims a change happened when no cache write occurred, which the code labels an 'UNSPECIFIED PLACEHOLDER' that consumers must not read. A typed answer exists only in memory (CommitOutcome.skip_reason), and CommitOutcome is #[allow(dead_code)] because no production caller reads it.
findings.proposal: Add a typed field to EvalEvent (e.g. `EventKind::Started { trace: TraceSource, cache: CacheLegKind }`) and make `Completed.outcome` an `Option<EvalOutcome>`. The module doc names both as the out-of-scope fix. cache_divergence then matches on the enum.

findings.statement: reify-ir has two sibling modules that each classify a Value against an expected LENGTH dimension and render an 'X expects Length, got Y' message, with separate predicates and separate label tables. kernel_validation::check_length_field uses got_label/value_variant_name ('Scalar<Length>', 'Point', ...). arg_acceptance::accept_arg(&v, &length_spec()) uses value_short_label ('Length Scalar', 'unknown'). kernel_validation's docs justify the fork by saying 'arg_acceptance lives in reify-eval and the adapter -> eval dependency direction is deliberately inverted ... so the code cannot be shared'. That has been false since task 5791 (done): arg_acceptance's own module doc records its move into reify-ir, the same crate. The same doc block cites `geometry_ops.rs:482/:523`, but the functions now sit at 615/839.
findings.proposal: Express the tripwire as `accept_arg(v, &spec)` plus a kernel-flavoured formatter that takes the ArgSpec, and unify the label table into one function used by both modules. Delete the false rationale paragraph.

findings.statement: member_path.rs calls itself 'The single compile-time member-shape authority' and states contract C1-iv: 'No other site may re-match member AST shapes'. Its chain walk, though (resolve_member_path with TerminalKind, Resolved, root_binding, classify_terminal and synthesized_member, about 250 lines), has no production caller and is kept alive with #[allow(dead_code)] behind TODO(#5425), which is pending. Only resolve_hop is consumed, at 2 sites in expr.rs. Production member typing still goes through expr.rs's own parallel authorities. template_has_member scans a 3-container union where resolve_hop scans 5. port_member_is_priv mirrors value_cell_visibility's Param guard by prose. Two `"count" => Type::Int` arms duplicate synthesized_member's table.
findings.proposal: Either land the first production consumer, or keep only resolve_hop and move the chain walk into the PR that consumes it. Until then, state in the module doc that expr.rs::template_has_member and port_member_is_priv are the live authorities.

findings.statement: stdlib_sources orders 47 stdlib modules by hand. stdlib_topo::compile_modules_topo is a working dependency mechanism keyed on `import` edges, yet no stdlib .ri file declares an import. Every inter-module dependency is written as comment prose beside each entry ('MUST follow std.kinematic', 'MUST be LAST'). The loader's own doc calls this an 'Ordering footgun' that is 'NOT machine-checked by the topo-sort'. Out-of-order placement is caught only indirectly: a too-early module yields Error diagnostics and load_stdlib panics. A purely positional constraint such as 'std.determinacy.purposes last' has its own dedicated test.
findings.proposal: Express each dependency as an `import` in the dependent .ri file, so compile_modules_topo derives the order. Keep only the 'purposes last' rule as a structural special case, and delete the per-entry prose.

findings.statement: Whether a member kind (18 MemberDecl variants) is supported, rejected loudly, or dropped silently is decided separately in each context by a hand-written match: entity body (entity.rs), guarded block (guards.rs::compile_guarded_members and register_guarded_names), trait (compile_trait), purpose top level (compile_purpose), and purpose guarded block (unsupported_purpose_member_info). The contexts disagree with no single policy behind them. compile_guarded_members silently drops Port/Connect/Chain/MetaBlock/ConstraintInst/AssociatedType/Fn, which is the 'port inside where{} dropped without a diagnostic' that scope.rs's field doc concedes. compile_purpose's top level silently ignores Relate/Sketch/Fn while its guarded block rejects them, even though sketch_unsupported.rs declares 'every position that admits a sketch block must reject it'. compile_purpose also carries 11 rejection arms whose message strings duplicate unsupported_purpose_member_info verbatim, and the purpose_member grammar rule makes all 11 unreachable from source.
findings.proposal: Introduce one `member_support(kind, context) -> Supported | Reject(&'static str) | Ignore` table, with an enum for context, and have every loop consult it for its unsupported arms. That deletes the duplicate strings and the unreachable purpose arms.

findings.statement: detectors.rs presents DetectorRegistry as 'the single owner of post-pass ordering (INV-EVAL-3) ... one owner, all paths'. The registry holds one detector (MassPropertiesPsdDetector). The second post-pass, run_materialization_annotation_post_pass, sits outside it. Its order relative to PSD is held by call position at two sites (eval, eval_cached), and a comment says ordering is now 'owned by the registry + this call ordering'. edit_check runs the registry but never calls the annotation post-pass, so the three serve paths run different post-pass sets. Whether edit_check needs it is unverified (PLAUSIBLE defect, CONFIRMED asymmetry). The module doc still describes wiring as 'task μ (#5062) explicitly OUT of scope', though #5062 is done and the doc later says μ wired it. Its pointers engine_eval.rs:6312 and :4400-4557 no longer point at the passes, which are now around 6848/7211.
findings.proposal: Make the annotation post-pass a registry detector by widening PostPassState with the read-only module/prelude context it needs, so with_builtins really is the single ordered list on all three paths. Replace the doc's line pointers with symbol names.

findings.statement: The file's module doc records that #6992 shipped because the tests exercised a hand-copied replica of build.rs. Four replicas remain: content_hash, stamp_write, verify_outputs, run_with_timeout. Two already differ from build.rs. The replica verify_outputs returns Result<(), String> with a different message, while build.rs's verify_outputs panics with an extra 'Check tree-sitter CLI version.' sentence. The replica run_with_timeout omits build.rs's stdout(Stdio::null())/stderr(Stdio::inherit()) configuration. Tests such as test_all_three_outputs_verified and test_subprocess_timeout_kills_hung_process therefore pin a copy, not the code cargo runs. build_support.rs already exists as the shared include!, so the mechanism to share is in place. The file is also 2,444 lines, and half of it (lines 771-1985) is tests whose subject is this file's own source text.
findings.proposal: Move content_hash, stamp_write, verify_outputs and run_with_timeout into build_support.rs, the include! shared by build.rs and the test target, and delete the replicas. The h14 partition for the rest is recorded in h14_measurements.

findings.statement: Sub-component instance cells are elaborated by unfold.rs, a second implementation of cell elaboration parallel to engine_eval.rs's template-scope path. Since 2026-07-06 the two have been reconciled one rule at a time: #5360 cee8ad1415 (nested subs resolved module-only while the top-level path used the prelude fallback), #7418 eaae8530e8/09455b16c1 (child params not visited in dependency order), #5057 49abf75ff6 (determinacy-predicate divergence) and #6662 (@optimized reuse at instance scope). Two divergences remain built in. First, elaborate_child_params_only and elaborate_child_lets_only meet cell_eval_ctx's required `containment` and `runtime_sink` arguments with a `NoContainment` null object (always None, so restricted-field samples become Undef) and a fresh RefCell that is then dropped. The template-scope let walk passes `self` (Engine's ContainmentQuery) and calls store_cell_replay_diagnostics. Second, unfold_recursive_sub evaluates guard and arg expressions with eval_ctx_with_meta, which has no determinacy or diagnostics sink. A further known wrong behaviour is recorded only in the NoContainment doc comment, with no task cite: a recursion-local name resolves its value from child_values but its determinacy from the global snapshot.
findings.proposal: Give instance and template scope one per-cell elaboration primitive, parameterised by the scope projection (value map plus determinacy view), so that containment, diagnostics capture and ordering are supplied once. In the interim, drain the child runtime_sink into `diagnostics`, store it with store_cell_replay_diagnostics, and add a differential test that elaborates one fixture at both scopes.

findings.statement: engine_admin.rs (header comment: 'Split from lib.rs (task 2032) — admin methods') is one of 19 files holding `impl Engine` blocks over the private 67-field Engine struct declared in lib.rs.
