It reads and writes those fields directly rather than through an interface. Its purpose cannot be stated without 'and'. It holds the 67-field struct-literal constructor and five other constructors; the kernel, solver, optimized, compute and morph registries; about 25 state accessors; 28 cfg(test-instrumentation) seams; the shell-GUI mesh decoder (5 fns, about 400 lines); kernel-pin diagnostics; the persistent-cache startup sweep; and undef-cause tracing. Twelve Engine fields named last_* keep per-call results at instance lifetime, and most are read only by cfg-gated accessors (heuristic 5). store_morph_source and morph_source carry `#[allow(dead_code)] // consumed by #4744 step-20`, yet engine_build.rs calls store_morph_source at 2 production sites and reads `self.morph_source` directly at 2 more, so the getter is test-only and the allow comment is stale.
findings.proposal: Split Engine state into owned sub-structs (registries, per-build ledgers, test instrumentation, caches), each with its own module and reset/accessor methods, so that satellites take the sub-struct they need rather than reaching into `self`.

findings.statement: The `ShellExtractionResult` Value produced by shell_extract_compute.rs::shell_extraction_result_to_value is decoded by two independent hand-written parsers. One is engine_admin.rs::parse_shell_extraction_result, the highest-CCN function in that file. The other is shell_extract_compute.rs::value_to_shell_extraction_result. They disagree in detail: the engine_admin parser requires the nested type_name strings "MidSurfaceMesh" and "SegmentationResult", which the other parser does not check, and it decodes triangles to usize where the other uses u32. Engine::shell_gui_mesh_data selects compute nodes by the string targets "shell-extract::extract" and "solver::elastic_static", and returns an empty Vec on any decode miss with no diagnostic. Its `// G-allow: library API; production consumer is the pending shell-extract GUI bridge` is false: gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs calls it at 2 sites.
findings.proposal: Have shell_gui_mesh_data consume the typed value_to_shell_extraction_result, move it next to that function as a free function over (&Snapshot, &CacheStore), and drop the stale G-allow.

findings.statement: deps.rs derives the question 'what does node X read' with three independent graph walks. ReverseDependencyIndex::build_from_graph_and_fields and build_trace_map_and_fields each loop over value cells, constraints, realizations, resolutions, fields and geometry links. They must agree but are built separately at every call site. They already differ: Compute nodes are registered as reverse dependents but get no trace-map entry. The third walk, DependencyMap::from_graph (used by Engine::trace_undef_causes and the dead cache::dirty_set), has different semantics again. It includes Auto cells' default_expr, which the other two skip; it ignores constraints, realizations and fields; and it dedups and sorts reads, while extract_dependency_trace keeps duplicates. #5385 factored geometry_cell_realization_links out so both main walks share it, but agreement is still pinned per edge class by tests named *_both_directions.
findings.proposal: Build the reverse index by inverting the forward trace map, so there is one walk, and point the undef tracer at the trace map instead of DependencyMap.

findings.statement: The name units.rs misdescribes its contents. Of its 1,910 production lines, lines 1-1,690 (88%) are the compiler's builtin catalogue: 16 name tables (GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES, GEOMETRY_TOPOLOGY_SELECTOR_NAMES, FIELD_OP_NAMES, DATUM_CONSTRUCTOR_NAMES and others), 15 is_* predicates and their *_result_type functions, and selector-composition type checking. Only about 220 lines (UnitRegistry, UnitEntry, UnitResolveError, resolve_unit_expr, unit_to_scalar) concern units. The file opens with `use super::*;`, and lib.rs re-exports it back with `pub(crate) use units::*;`, so its items are visible unqualified in every module of the crate. This is one instance of a crate-wide flat namespace: reify-compiler's lib.rs has 28 `pub(crate) use <mod>::*` globs, and 27 of its 56 top-level source files start with `use super::*;`.
findings.proposal: Move the builtin tables into builtin_families.rs, or straight into reify-builtins rows per docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md, leaving units.rs with units only. Replace the lib.rs glob re-exports with explicit `use crate::<mod>::{..}` imports.

findings.statement: Each builtin's facts are restated in parallel string-keyed tables, and overlaps between them are resolved by the order of an if-ladder. units.rs's 16 tables hold 177 entries but only 166 distinct names, so 11 names appear in two tables. `union` and `difference` are in both GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES and SELECTOR_COMPOSITION_NAMES. `affine_apply` is in both GEOMETRY_FUNCTION_NAMES and AFFINE_ALGEBRA_NAMES. Which family claims a name depends on where its arm sits in expr.rs's result-type ladder of about 30 arms, an ordering described in prose and pinned by tests (affine_algebra_names_never_reach_the_terminal_fallback). Per-position facts are restated too: builtin_arg_slots states index, name and dimension; its own comment says the arg names are 'COPIED from geometry.rs's lowering sites'; reify-ir arg_acceptance.rs restates the dimension at eval time; unresolved_function.rs holds a union oracle plus hand-copied signature strings. builtin_arg_slots itself is a 762-line match with 28 arms, of which 537 lines (70.5%) are comments. Much of that prose is task history and reviewer-answering text ('the FOURTH builtin…', 'MEASURED PREFIX DIVERGENCE'), and the module header declares those arms authoritative. reify-builtins (#6001) is the intended single home but has seeded only the parse and analysis families, and is_known_builtin consults both regimes.
findings.proposal: Continue the builtin-signature-registry migration so each builtin is one row carrying arity, arg slots and result. Move per-arm rationale into the row's `basis` field or the PRD, and leave a pointer in the code.

findings.statement: reify-eval's integration tests drive the engine through cfg(test-instrumentation) seams that expose its private state. Engine::cache_store_mut hands tests `&mut CacheStore`, and they `put` NodeCache entries directly. cache_store, warm_pool_mut and about a dozen last_* counters are read the same way. Engine::cell_eval_ctx is kept alive only for a parity test, via `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))]` with a comment saying its last production caller was removed. The morph_source getter is used only by morph_producer.rs tests, while production reads the field directly. Each of these seams fixes the shape of NodeCache, CacheStore and the Engine counters in place, so the redesign the prior cache.rs finding proposes (diagnostics as a required NodeCache argument) would also require editing every test that seeds the cache.
findings.proposal: Give tests behavioural seams (edit/eval drivers, fixtures that produce a given cache state through eval) and narrow or remove cache_store_mut. Delete Engine::cell_eval_ctx and the test-only morph_source getter.

findings.statement: cache.rs keeps public peers of the live invalidation path that production never calls. `pub fn dirty_set` has no caller anywhere, takes unused `_graph` and `_values` parameters, and its doc claims it is 're-evaluating and checking for early cutoff', which it does not do. check_early_cutoff and compute_input_hash are called only from cache.rs's own tests. The free function derive_output_freshness has no production caller. DependencyMap::topological_order is called only by dirty_set. Meanwhile two live dirty mechanisms coexist: the one-hop CacheStore.dirty_reasons (invalidate_dependents in engine_edit.rs; is_dirty, clear_dirty and clear_dependents_dirty in eval_cached) and the transitive dirty::compute_dirty_cone (5 production sites in engine_edit.rs). The unwired freshness walk is a third (prior finding).
findings.proposal: Delete dirty_set, check_early_cutoff, compute_input_hash and DependencyMap::topological_order along with their unit tests, and keep the derive_output_freshness truth table only behind the _with_cause variant that production uses.
findings.change_note: gone at 0e60fa138d: Removed by 2e364f0171 'reify-eval: delete dead invalidation code (dirty_set, check_early_cutoff, compute_input_hash, free derive_output_freshness, topological_order)', task #8675, done. git grep finds none of those symbols in reify-eval src or tests.; task store: [('8675', 'done')]

findings.statement: The curvature Surface→Matrix<2,2> overload decides 'face selector' by matching the inner call's function name against FACE_PRODUCING_SELECTOR_NAMES (faces, faces_by_area, faces_by_normal, adjacent_faces). It does not read the selector's type, even though since task 4118 topology_selector_result_type types 11 selectors as Type::Selector(SelectorKind::Face), and the ResolveSelector node the detector unwraps carries that type. geometry_query_arg_aware_result_type's doc still says topology_selector_result_type 'returns Type::List(Geometry) for BOTH faces() and edges()', which is no longer true. So curvature over an indexed face_perpendicular_to, mid_surface, extremal_by_bbox or similar face selector degrades to Scalar<Curvature> while the same expression over faces(...) gets the Matrix type.
findings.proposal: Classify by `selector.result_type == Type::Selector(SelectorKind::Face)` on the ResolveSelector arm, keep a name check only for the still-List adjacent_faces, and correct the doc.

findings.statement: CompiledExpr content-hash domain tags are hand-picked `pub const TAG_*: u8` values. The allocation policy exists only in prose, and the prose contradicts itself. The header says bytes 20-23 are reserved for CachedResult::content_hash in reify-eval/src/cache.rs, which uses the bare literals [20], [21], [22] and [23] rather than named constants. Yet TAG_STRUCTURE_INSTANCE_CTOR = 20 carries the comment 'Tags 20–23 were free'. No test or const assertion checks that the 26 TAG constants are distinct. If two expression kinds shared a tag, structurally different expressions with equal sub-hashes would collide, and early cutoff would treat a changed expression as Unchanged.
findings.proposal: Add a const-evaluated uniqueness assertion over the TAG_* array, name the CachedResult tags in cache.rs, and replace the reservation prose with that assertion.

findings.statement: Engine::realization_kernel_provenance formats each RealizationNodeId with `node.id.to_string()` into RealizationKernelProvenance.realization. It then sorts by re-parsing that string with `split_once("#realization[")` and `parse::<u32>`, falling back to (whole string, u32::MAX) for 'unrecognised format'. Meanwhile node.id already has the structured `entity: String, index: u32` fields, and reify-core/src/identity.rs owns the canonical parser, which uses rsplit_once and so differs from this split_once on entity names that contain the marker.
findings.proposal: Sort on (node.id.entity, node.id.index) before formatting.

findings.statement:
`Engine` is defined at reify-eval's crate root with 67 fields (2 of them cfg-gated). Because it sits at the root, every child module can read its private fields. 15 files do so directly via `self.<field>` in production code: engine_admin 50 fields, engine_eval 35, engine_build 24, engine_edit 23, engine_constraints 15, engine_purposes 10, engine_compute 9, and 8 more. There are 23 `impl Engine` blocks across 18 files.

The struct mixes about 6 independent lifetime classes:
- configuration (build_scheduler, mesh_contract_mode, max_unfold_*)
- per-build side tables (topology_attribute_table, swept_kind_table, realization_handles, achieved_repr_tol, relate_static_facts)
- per-eval artifacts (functions, meta_map, objectives, compiled_fields)
- purpose state (5 maps)
- cross-edit caches (cache, warm_pool, realization_cache)
- test instrumentation (9 `last_*`/counter fields)

Each field's class is recorded twice. It appears in its lib.rs doc comment (8 doc mentions of `reset_per_build_state`). It also appears in `engine_build.rs::reset_per_build_state`'s exhaustive destructure, which groups fields under reset-every / reset-on-build / reset-on-tessellate / MUST-SURVIVE headings. The destructure turns a forgotten classification into a compile error, but not a wrong one. That function's own comment records such a misclassification: relate_static_facts was cleared on every surface, a 'silent WIPE' (#5415).
findings.proposal: Group the fields into owned sub-structs by lifetime class, for example `EngineConfig`, `PerBuildState` (with a `reset(surface)` method), `EvalArtifacts`, `PurposeState`, `Caches` and `Instrumentation`. Satellite files then borrow the sub-struct they need, and the reset becomes the sub-struct's own method. A new field's class is chosen by where it is declared, not by a comment plus a separate destructure.

findings.statement:
The content-hash identity of a value-cell node is `ContentHash::of_str(&format!("{}", id)).combine(default_expr.map(content_hash).unwrap_or(ContentHash(0)))`. It is written out inline at 6 sites in `EvaluationGraph::from_templates`: top-level cells, collection elements, keyed members, plain subs, guard members, and else members. It is written again at 2 sites in engine_edit.rs, the collection-count re-elaboration (and its second copy). `ValueCellNode` has only public fields and no constructor. `ConstraintNodeData` is likewise built literally 4 times in graph.rs and twice in engine_edit.rs.

The cold path (from_templates) and the edit path (engine_edit re-elaboration) must produce byte-identical hashes for the same cell, or incremental cache keys diverge from cold ones (the INV-EVAL-4 class). Nothing links the two except copy discipline. structural_classifier.rs restates the formula in a doc comment and reasons about what it excludes.

`from_templates` itself is one 424-line function (322 code lines) nested 13 indents deep. It also scans the count-literal of collection subs by hand, through nested `if let` on `CompiledExprKind::Literal` and `ValueRef`.
findings.proposal: Add `ValueCellNode::new(id, kind, cell_type, default_expr)` and `ConstraintNodeData::from_compiled(&CompiledConstraint)` (with a scoped-id variant). Have them compute `content_hash`, and keep the hash field writable only through those constructors. Split from_templates per declaration kind, so that each arm calls the constructor.

findings.statement:
Active-purpose state is spread across 5 parallel `HashMap`s on Engine, all keyed by the purpose-name string:
- active_purposes
- active_purpose_bindings
- active_objective_map
- active_purpose_let_cells
- active_tolerance_scope (derived)

compiled_purposes holds the definitions, looked up by linear name scan. The field docs say these are 'populated/cleared in lockstep', but the lockstep is kept by hand. The insert half is in `activate_purpose_constraints_with_bindings_inner` (a 272-line method), the remove half in `deactivate_purpose`, and two re-injection blocks in engine_eval.rs (around L5226 and L9570) clear active_purposes, active_objective_map and active_tolerance_scope. Neither of those blocks clears active_purpose_let_cells.

Activation is temporally coupled. The `_inner` call returns `bool`, and every caller must then call `rebuild_purpose_infrastructure()`; 4 caller pairs do this by hand. `deactivate_purpose` re-inlines the same rebuild (reverse_index, trace_map, rebuild_cone, then recompute_tolerance_scope) instead of calling it.

The docs on `activate_purpose` still describe task γ as pending ('Until task γ lands…'), but `activate_purpose_with_bindings` is the γ API and exists in the same file.
findings.proposal: Replace the maps with one `HashMap<PurposeName, ActivePurpose { constraints, bindings, objective, let_cells }>` owned by a `PurposeState` type. Its `activate`, `deactivate` and `reinject_all(&mut EvalState)` methods include the infrastructure rebuild, and active_tolerance_scope is derived from it on demand.

findings.statement:
Instance paths are meaningful strings. `ValueCellId.entity` is a `String`. It is built by `format!("{}.{}[{}]", …)` at 13 sites in the compiler and eval, and by `MemberKey::path_segment` for keyed members, which writes `sub[<Debug-quoted key>]`.

It is then parsed ad hoc in at least 9 places in reify-eval production code:
- `strip_prefix` (engine_eval ×2, unfold)
- `starts_with` (unfold, tolerance_scope)
- `rsplit_once('.')` / `rsplit('.')` taking 'the last segment is the sub name' (geometry_ops, relate_solve)
- resolve_order's `strip_collection_indices`, which removes `[…]` with a character-level depth scanner

Two incompatible scopings coexist: structure-name-scoped template cells and instance-path-scoped cells. `normalize_cell_id` bridges them at every hop of the transitive walk. `build_instance_path_structure_map` re-walks the sub-component tree, 'mirroring structural_query.rs' (cited by line numbers), so that the bridge has a lookup table.

The `rsplit('.')` parsers cannot represent the grammar `path_segment` produces: a key containing '.' (for example `vents["a.b"]`) splits inside the quotes.
findings.proposal: Introduce a typed `InstancePath(Vec<PathSegment { sub: Name, index: Option<Index | Key> }>)` built at elaboration time. Have `ValueCellId` carry it, or a cheap interned handle to it, with Display used only at boundaries. Provide `structure_scope()` and `owning_sub()` as methods, replacing normalize_cell_id, strip_collection_indices and the rsplit parsers.

findings.statement:
Each geometric relation's facts are spread across parallel string-keyed tables in relation_signatures.rs:
- `RELATION_FN_NAMES`
- `is_relation_shared_verb`
- `relation_fn_result_type`
- `relation_delta_dof`
- `relation_delta_dof_kinds`
- `relation_metric_slot`
- `relation_operand_datum`
- `check_relation_arg_types` (`name == "tangent"`, `name == "distance"`)

The 'only the arity-3 form is a relation' policy for angle, distance and offset is encoded as 10 separate `args.len() == 3` guards. Agreement is kept by comment: '…so all four offset arms agree'. offset's arity-2 form is resolved in yet another file (units.rs `datum_constructor_result_type`).

The test that pins rot+trans == ΔDOF iterates a third hand-written list (`curated`), not RELATION_FN_NAMES. The constant's own doc says '**9 names**', but it holds 10 (fasten was added).
findings.proposal: Use one `RelationSig` descriptor per relation: `{name, arity: Arity, operands: OperandPolicy, metric_slot, codim: Codim}`, where Codim is `Fixed{rot,trans}`, `ByDatum(fn)` or `Tangent`. Keep them in a single static table that every resolver reads. Tests then iterate the table, so adding a relation is one row.

findings.statement:
Production engines still do not declare their compute-registration posture. It is inferred: `engine_compute.rs::soft_no_trampoline_diagnostic` emits a Warning when `compute_registry.fns.is_empty()` and an Error otherwise. An engine nobody registered is therefore indistinguishable from a deliberate opt-out.

The registration lint (`scripts/check-compute-trampoline-registration.sh`) checks only a literal table of 3 known sites: CLI main.rs, GUI engine.rs and test_runner.rs. The CLI MCP server's `ensure_engine` is a fourth production engine-construction site. It builds `Engine::new(SimpleConstraintChecker, None)`, registers nothing, and has no test pinning that posture. Its comment says it wires `set_persistent_cache_dir` so that 'MCP/GUI eval sessions also hit and populate the persistent on-disk cache'. The persistent lookup sits inside `run_compute_dispatch`, which a trampoline-less engine's eval path never reaches through `OptimizedComputeDispatcher::from_registry`.

docs/invariants.md INV-FEA-1 still names `Engine::new_production` as the mechanism, status 'proposed'; no such constructor exists.
findings.proposal: Make the posture a required constructor argument or type, for example `Engine::new(checker, kernel, Registration::Production(morph) | Registration::None { reason })`. The severity decision then reads the declared posture instead of `fns.is_empty()`. Put the MCP context's choice, and its persistent-cache comment, under a locking test.

findings.statement:
Engine exposes 28 `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-instrumentation"))]` public methods. They include raw mutable access to internals: `cache_store_mut`, `snapshot_mut`, `warm_pool_mut`, `realization_cache`, `set_build_scheduler`, `set_achieved_repr_tol_for_test` and `with_test_kernels_and_registry`. reify-eval enables the feature on itself through a self-dev-dependency, as do reify-lsp and reify-eval-fea-tests.

The production struct also carries 9 always-present counters whose only purpose is letting tests observe internal control flow: `last_guard_phase_group_evals`, `last_role_flip_probes`, `last_param_override_*` ×2, `last_sub_component_unknown_structure_errors`, `last_dispatch_count`, `geometry_revalidation_slow_path`, `last_diff_value_cells` (marked `#[allow(dead_code)]`), and `morph_source` (also marked `#[allow(dead_code)]`). It carries 2 more cfg-gated test-only fields: `test_registry_override` and `panic_on_eval_cells`. Tests reach in heavily: `cache_store_mut()` is called 121 times across 24 files.
findings.proposal: Replace the mutators with behaviour-level seams: fixture constructors that build an Engine in a given cache state through public eval calls, and a single read-only `EngineProbe` snapshot of counters returned by value. Retire the always-present counters that only tests read, or fold them into the journal (EventJournal already records evaluation events).

findings.statement:
Nine geometry-kind enums in types.rs each carry a hand-maintained private `const ALL: [Self; N]` and a `pub const VARIANT_COUNT = Self::ALL.len()`. The enums are PrimitiveKind, BooleanOp, ModifyKind, TransformKind, PatternKind, SweepKind, CurveKind, ProfileKind and SurfaceKind. Each also carries a copy of the same ~10-line 'Maintenance contract' doc paragraph, which says ALL is 'the single source of truth' and 'cannot independently drift'.

Nothing ties ALL to the enum. Adding a variant compiles with ALL and VARIANT_COUNT unchanged; only the exhaustive Display match forces an edit. The downstream registry-completeness locks (`geometry_modify` CASES assert, reify-eval `compile_geometry_op_registry_completeness`, `compile_geometry_op_characterization`) compare against the stale count and pass. So the tripwire fails in exactly the case it exists for.

reify-compiler already depends on strum, and reify-core already derives `strum::EnumCount` for TypeDiscriminants.
findings.proposal: Derive `strum::EnumCount` (and `EnumIter` where iteration is needed) on the 9 enums. Delete the ALL arrays and the 9 copied paragraphs, so VARIANT_COUNT is the compiler-derived `COUNT`.
findings.change_note: weakened: types.rs changed only in the CompiledForallBody area (PortPath). All nine `const ALL: [Self; N]` arrays, the `VARIANT_COUNT = Self::ALL.len()` consts and the copied 'Maintenance contract' paragraphs remain (types.rs:1513-1900). Review-all verdict weakened stands; #8661 pending.

findings.statement:
lib.rs is 48% comments, and the Engine struct alone is 699 comment lines out of 770. Those comments hold task history, the names of tests that pin behaviour, and file:line pointers, all of which have drifted at this tree:
- `realization_cache.rs:101-116` now points at the `ConversionSlot` enum; `lookup` is at :307.
- `types.rs:854-857` now points at `find_template`.
- `tests/tolerance_wiring_e2e.rs` has moved to `tests/harness_tolerance/`.
- The mod comments on `cell_commit` and `detectors` say 'no external callers yet', but cell_commit is called from 4 files and detectors from 2.
- `morph_source`'s doc says its consumer 'lands in #4744 step-16' and keeps `#[allow(dead_code)]`, but engine_build.rs now calls it twice.

The file also carries a re-export shim chain kept 'so the crate-root paths … keep resolving unchanged': 6 reify_compute_contract types, `pub(crate) use reify_ir::arg_acceptance`, and `graph::CancellationHandle`, which graph.rs itself re-exports from reify_compute_contract.
findings.proposal: Move each field's rationale into the PRD the field's task cites (most already have one), and keep a one-line purpose per field. Delete the line-number pointers in favour of symbol names. Retire the compat re-exports by migrating downstream imports to reify_compute_contract.

findings.statement:
`query_kind` on `ResolvedSchemaQuery` and on `CompiledExprKind::PurposeReflectiveAggregation` is a `String` carrying an enum: 'params', 'geometric_params' or 'material_params'. It is defined as a string slice at compiler expr.rs:1078, and spelled again in traits.rs, reify-ir expr.rs and 5 times in engine_purposes.rs.

When no resolved query matches, the runtime fallback string-compares the kind. An unknown kind returns an empty member list, which produces a vacuous-true `forall`, so the purpose constraint silently passes.
findings.proposal: Parse the kind into an enum `ReflectiveQueryKind { Params, GeometricParams, MaterialParams }` at the compiler boundary, and carry the enum in IR. The fallback then becomes an exhaustive `match` with the per-kind predicate.

findings.statement:
The ValueCell BFS body, including the edge-#12 Compute→output-cell expansion, is written twice: in `compute_dirty_cone` and again inside `compute_dirty_cone_with_realizations`. The second copy differs by one extra realization re-seed. Only the realization-frontier loop dispatches on `NodeId` with an exhaustive `match`; both ValueCell loops use `if let` chains, so a new `NodeId` variant is silently treated as a leaf there.

The two functions also have different transitive closure. The plain one does not walk through realizations, and the doc of the other states 'every arm rounds toward INCLUSION'. Yet `compute_dirty_cone_with_realizations` has exactly one production caller, which passes an empty ValueCell seed set (engine_edit.rs:685), so its name describes an input it is never given.
findings.proposal: Use one walker, `dirty_cone(seeds: Seeds { cells, realizations }, policy)`, with a single exhaustive `match` on `NodeId` per frontier, and name it for what the edit path actually seeds.

findings.statement: The datum-projection table ('receiver kind x member -> codomain') has three independent homes with no derivation or parity check between them: the compiler typing table plus DATUM_PROJECTION_MEMBERS in datum_projection.rs (whose doc calls it 'the single source of truth'), reify-expr's eval_datum_projection, and reify-eval geometry_ops.rs's SELF_DATUM_PROJECTION_MEMBERS (described only in prose as 'LOCKSTEP'). They have already drifted. The compiler types Frame(_).yz_plane and .zx_plane as Plane, but eval_datum_projection's Value::Frame arm has no arm for either, so they evaluate to Undef with no diagnostic. Task #6100 (pending) tracks that one instance. The three-table structure stays after it is fixed.
findings.proposal: Hold one projection table (receiver kind x member -> codomain Type + evaluator) in a crate both sides already depend on (reify-ir), and make the compiler typing, eval_datum_projection and the self-datum path all consume it. Until then, add a parity test that iterates DATUM_PROJECTION_MEMBERS x {Axis, Plane, Frame, Direction, StructureRef} and asserts that every Resolved pair evaluates to a non-Undef value of the declared kind.

findings.statement: docs/invariants.md registers INV-EVAL-2 ('Engine cell-eval contexts always carry determinacy, runtime-diagnostics sink, and containment') with mechanism 'type (required-args constructor)'. In practice the type is opt-in. The free function has 11 call sites, while 21 live production sites still hand-build contexts through the optional eval_ctx_with_meta(...).with_determinacy(...) builder. 20 of those 21 omit .with_containment, and 11 also omit .with_runtime_diagnostics. One example is the edit_source Let re-eval at engine_edit.rs:3721. The module doc says the old Engine::cell_eval_ctx method coexists 'until δ/ε (#5056/#5057) migrate their remaining call sites'. Both tasks are done. The method is now dead (cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))) and is kept only so a parity test can call it.
findings.proposal: Make the optional-capability builder unreachable for cell evaluation (narrow eval_ctx_with_meta's visibility to cell_eval_ctx.rs or rename it to a non-cell use). Migrate the 21 sites, or record a per-site exemption. Add a ratchet that counts .with_determinacy( outside cell_eval_ctx.rs. Delete the dead Engine::cell_eval_ctx and its parity test, and fix the stale coexistence paragraph.

findings.statement: Builtin result typing has two mechanisms for one axis of variation (name -> result type). One is the reify-builtins registry this module fronts, which holds 7 rows. The other is a 22-arm string-predicate ladder in expr.rs over per-family modules: orientation_signatures, joint_signatures, flexure_signatures and list_helpers in this slice. Each family module spells every name twice, once in a name slice and once in a match arm, with a placeholder `_` arm. The prose that guides a change has drifted. The ladder's precedence comment lists 17 of the 22 arms. The orientation and joint module docs, and the ladder comment, say disjointness is pinned 'in the units.rs test module', but builtin_name_families_are_pairwise_disjoint lives in unresolved_function.rs. joint_signatures cites expr.rs:1718-1730 and '~line 1793' for an arm now at expr.rs:3738.
findings.proposal: Resume β (#6002) and the τ migrations so each family becomes registry rows and the ladder shrinks to one arm. Meanwhile repoint the disjointness references to unresolved_function.rs, drop the line-number anchors, and make the precedence comment point at the code rather than restate it.

findings.statement: reify-compiler's crate root flattens the contents of 29 modules (325 top-level pub/pub(crate) items) via `pub(crate) use X::*` / `pub use types::*`, and 27 source files import that root wholesale with a top-level `use super::*;`. Eight of them are in this slice: coerce, datum_projection, diagnostics, geometry_boolean, geometry_curve, geometry_transform, ice and termination. termination.rs's only import is `use super::*`. It names TopologyTemplate, GuardState, CompiledExpr, ValueCellId, Diagnostic, DiagnosticLabel, HashMap and HashSet, and the file says where none of them come from. Its three helpers are pub(crate) and globbed into the root, although only check_recursive_termination has an external caller (post_passes.rs, by path).
findings.proposal: Replace each top-level `use super::*` with explicit imports (mechanical with rust-analyzer), shrink the root globs to the named items other modules actually use, and ratchet the count of top-level `use super::*`.

findings.statement: joint_self_check.rs is a shallow module that exports the pieces of the §7.1 DOF self-check law but not the law itself. It exposes five pub(crate) functions (residual_kinds, body_has_undecidable_kind_split, dof_kind_of, declared_kinds, check_joint_dof). The gate that makes the verdict sound (skip on a Type::Error DOF; emit E_ARG_TYPE_MISMATCH and skip on an unclassifiable DOF; skip on an undecidable rot/trans split; only then compare residual against declared) is reimplemented in compile_builder/entities_phase.rs. The module's own docs assign that duty to 'the caller' in two places. Its tests drive each piece separately, so nothing tests the composed law.
findings.proposal: Expose one entry point, e.g. joint_dof_diagnostics(joint_name, declared fields [(name, Type, span)], body, span) -> Vec<Diagnostic>, that owns both gradualism gates and the verdict. Make the pieces private and drive tests through that seam.

findings.statement: Each tensor-analysis wrapper kind's per-window kernel is written twice: once as a closure in analysis.rs's sample_*_at_point (pointwise sample()) and once in field_reductions.rs's project_*_sampled (min/max/argmin/argmax). A 60-line module doc in analysis.rs and two integration tests hold the copies together. The non-positive-yield policy for safety_factor already diverges across three paths: the stdlib builtin and sample() return a finite yield/vM for yield <= 0, while the reductions return Undef. So sample(sf, p) and max(sf) disagree on the same field.
findings.proposal: Hold a per-FieldSourceKind kernel table (window -> [f64; K], plus that kind's yield or validity policy) that both sample_tensor_grid_at_point and project_sampled_tensor_windows consume, so agreement holds by construction and the cross-file contract prose can be deleted.

findings.statement: The compiler routes geometry ops on raw name strings that are respelled at every hop. geometry.rs's router matches a literal name group and calls a satellite. The satellite (compile_boolean_op / compile_curve_op / compile_transform_op / compile_modify_op) re-matches the same names and ends in `_ => unreachable!()`. compile_boolean_op then matches the names a third time to pick a BooleanOp. Meanwhile reify-ir already has an OpDescriptor table that maps names (e.g. ["union","union_all"]) to GeometryOpDiscriminants, and compile dispatch never consults it.
findings.proposal: Parse the name to GeometryOpDiscriminants once through the OpDescriptor table at the router and dispatch on the enum with an exhaustive match, so a missing arm is a compile error rather than a runtime unreachable! (the τ9 #6011 bridge covers the name-set half).

findings.statement: Snapshot's doc makes two claims that the code contradicts. It calls the type 'An immutable snapshot of evaluation state', yet all 7 fields are pub and production code mutates them in place. Its `values` field doc says kernel handles are 're-checked at the READ boundary by the Engine' via Engine::read_value_revalidated, yet that method's own doc says it has no production caller and that GUI and other reads bypass it.
findings.proposal: Correct the type and field docs to match the code: copy-on-write via PersistentMap, mutated on the working clone, and revalidation opt-in through read_value_revalidated with a task cite. Separately decide whether production reads should route through read_value_revalidated.

findings.statement: The module doc says purpose-level ambient defaults 'are NEVER injected into a structure (DD6 — structures cannot nest in a purpose)' and calls the nested map 'the forward-compatible seam' for a later task. That later task has landed. Task 4639 compiles purpose-nested structures with Some(purpose) (entities_phase.rs) through conformance/mod.rs:214 into check_phase_inject_ambient_defaults, which calls ambient.resolve(type_name, purpose) (checker.rs:2162). So purpose-level defaults are injected, and the doc describes their own production path as dead.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the module doc to state the current behaviour (purpose-nested structures resolve innermost-wins at purpose scope, per task 4639) and point at the test that pins it.

findings.statement: Parse errors carry no structured kind: reify_ast::ParseError is {message: String, span}. So the one category that callers must tell apart, member-continuation ambiguity, is identified by a substring match on MESSAGE_HEAD through an exported predicate, and its own doc concedes 'text matching is the wrong shape'. The GUI turns ParseErrors into code-less Diagnostics.
findings.proposal: Add a kind or code field to ParseError (mapping to DiagnosticCode at the compiler and GUI boundaries) and make is_member_continuation_message compare that field.

findings.statement: Engine exposes two mirrored pass-through method sets over DemandRegistry, one for the production registry (engine_demand.rs) and one for the observed registry (observed_demand.rs). The incremental mutators add_demand and remove_demand are public with no production caller. They are temporally coupled: the caller must call rebuild_demand_cone afterwards, and they skip the mark_demand_pruned_pending prune-safety step that set_demand_selective performs. Several inspection methods exist only for tests.
findings.proposal: Collapse the production mutation surface to set_demand_selective (or a single toggle that rebuilds and marks atomically), make add/remove private or delete them, and expose one read-only demand view for tests instead of per-field inspection methods.

findings.statement:
`Finding` has no structured kind or location. Every multi-kind detector puts its kind into `summary` as a `<kind>: ` prefix (the 'PTODO kind-as-prefix convention' that lib.rs, pdoccover, pdcheck and pcite each cite), and most also embed `line N:` in that text. That string is parsed back by:
- `ptodo::fingerprint`, the key of the merge-gate ptodo-baseline.txt ratchet: `split_once(':')` plus a hand parser that strips `line <digits>: `.
- `ptodo::is_g_allow_finding`: `starts_with("g-allow-")`.
- `ptodo::g_allow_finding_line`: `split_once(": line ")`. It sits behind a `debug_assert`, so a release build silently sorts at line 0.
- the /audit skill's routing templates, which tell the agent to take `<kind>` and `<n>` from `finding.summary`.
- test helpers.
`EvidenceRef::FileLine` was added so consumers would 'read it rather than parsing it out of the summary', but only PCITE emits it. `Finding.task_id` is a name that lies: structural detectors store a file path in it. Inside PTODO it holds a path for the structural and liveness kinds and a numeric task id for the inverse kinds, while `fingerprint`'s doc says it is a path 'for all PTODO kinds'.
findings.proposal: Give Finding a typed `kind` (a per-pattern enum serialised as today's token) and require `EvidenceRef::FileLine` for located findings. Derive `fingerprint` and the sort keys from those fields, and render `summary` from them for humans only. Replace `task_id` with a `subject` enum (Task(id) | Path(path)) so the field says which it holds.

Either implement the window in one place (narrow `task_metadata` at load time, which is what P2's comment says protection requires) or delete `--since`, `TimeWindow` and `producer_branch` together with the skill's §3 mode. Give AuditContext a builder or constructor so test sites stop spelling every field.

findings.statement:
The question 'is this source line or path test-only or opted out?' has several homes inside one crate, with divergent semantics:
- cfg(test) attribute (4 recognisers):
  - pdiag::is_cfg_test_attr accepts `#[cfg(test)]` and `cfg(any(test,…))`, rejects anything containing `not(`, and explicitly rejects `feature = "test-*"` as production-reachable.
  - p2_consumer_stub::is_test_cfg_attr ACCEPTS `feature = "test…"` and `all(test,…)`.
  - pdoccover::is_cfg_test_attr accepts only exact `#[cfg(test)]` / `#![cfg(test)]`.
  - jcodemunch_client::extract_suppression uses `line.contains("cfg(test)")`.
- test path (2 rules): lib.rs::is_test_path calls itself 'the crate's *single* canonical test-path predicate' (matches `_test.rs`, `.test.`, `__tests__/`). pdiag::is_swept_path gate 4 is a different rule (a `tests` segment, or a `tests`/`*_tests` stem).
- allow(dead_code): ptodo::allow_dead_code_attr scans for a whole `dead_code` token and rejects `dead_codex`. jcodemunch_client::extract_suppression uses a substring `contains("dead_code")`.
- G-allow body grammar (3 copies, 2 semantics): ptodo::g_allow_marker_body, jcodemunch_client::extract_g_allow, and scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh `G_ALLOW_RE.search` (free-floating).
- cfg(test)-region trackers (2, deliberately different): pdiag's brace counting is literal-unaware; pdoccover's blanks literals first.
findings.proposal: Move the Rust source-shape vocabulary into one lower module, next to scan_util: a code view with comment and literal masking, a cfg(test)-region tracker, the attribute recognisers, and the G-allow body grammar. Where a detector genuinely needs a different policy (pdiag's line-granular mask), make the policy a named parameter of that module rather than a private copy. Have lib::is_test_path and pdiag's test-locus gate share one rule or carry distinct names.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement:
Of GitOps's 12 questions, 9 collapse 'git failed' into an answer (empty Vec, `false`, or `None`) with no fallible variant. Only log_grep, is_gitignored and path_tracked_on have `try_` twins, and the trait doc leaves it to each caller to know when the collapse is unsafe. `ls_files()` is among the collapsed nine, so its 7 consumers each re-decide 'enumeration failed' from emptiness, in four different ways:
- PDOCCOVER: DegenerateInputs, a High `census-empty:` finding.
- PDIAG: `pdiag-census-empty` High, but only when the baseline has rows.
- PTODO: exposes ScanStats.files_scanned for the infra test's floor and otherwise reports clean.
- PDSSENTINEL, PCITE and PPRDSTATUS: silently report clean.
- PDCHECK: reads an empty tracked set as 'every path absent' and stays quiet only because the following `last_commit_for_path` call also fails.
The P5 sweep's High verdict in check_one is likewise built on the infallible `path_tracked_on` and `task_referencing_commits`, whereas the pre-done gate routes the same failures into a Low advisory.
findings.proposal: Add `try_ls_files() -> Result<Vec<String>, String>`, or return a `TrackedFiles` value that cannot be constructed from a failure, and give the remaining collapsed questions try_ forms. Then implement 'degenerate enumeration' once, for example as a crate-level finding emitted by the dispatcher, instead of once per detector.

findings.statement:
Comment lines make up 52-59% of non-blank lines in the production regions of lib.rs, p5_phantom_done.rs, pdiag.rs, pdoccover.rs and ptodo.rs. Much of that prose is reviewer-answering: dated corpus counts, rejected alternatives, 'do not simplify' warnings, and the names of the tests that pin each property. It has drifted from the code. At least nine statements are false at this tree:
- lib.rs Pattern::PTodo says 'all Medium severity' and 'participates … at Medium severity (exit-neutral)', but Kind::severity maps untracked and bare-ignore to High, and orphaned and g-allow-orphaned are High.
- ptodo.rs's module doc says 'all emitting Medium-severity findings'.
- pdiag.rs says 'Unlike PTODO's warn-first Medium lanes'.
- lib.rs's crate doc says 'currently ships three detectors'; there are 13.
- Pattern's naming convention says every variant carries `P<N>` 'so downstream dispatch can route on prefix', but 10 of 18 variants have no digit.
- Severity's doc says Medium 'is reserved for metadata-cleanliness findings'.
- AuditContext's doc says 'the crate never owns a connection or spawns processes itself', but ptodo and pdcheck open tasks.db.
- RealGitOps's doc says 'Untested by the slice-1 integration suite', but tests/real_git_ops.rs has 13 tests.
- pdoccover's section header says 'Pure scanners (stubs — filled in by the TDD steps that follow)'.
findings.proposal: Move measurements, rejected alternatives and test-name pins into the PRDs (the files already cite §-anchors) or into the commit messages that made them. Keep one-line pointers in the code. Let the severity table be derived from code, for example a `Kind::severity` per pattern listed in `--help`, instead of restated in rustdoc.

findings.statement:
Access to the task DB (`tasks_db_path`, which honours the REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB override, and `open_tasks_db`) lives in a peer detector, ptodo. It is not a seam on AuditContext. PDCHECK and the bin import it from ptodo, and PDCHECK opens its own connection inside `check`.
Reporting of DB degradation is a PTODO-specific type (`ptodo::ScanStats` / `ptodo::TasksDbMode`). As a result the bin's `Check::TasksDbBacked` / `Detector::reads_tasks_db()` answers false for PDCHECK, which does read tasks.db and degrades with 'this is NOT a clean bill of health'. `--pattern PDCHECK --require-tasks-db` exits 125 with 'this run set does not include PTODO', so PDCHECK's degradation cannot be guarded.
The canonical-cite grammar, which PPRDSTATUS needs, also lives in ptodo and is imported peer-to-peer (`use crate::ptodo::canonical_cite_occurrences`).
findings.proposal: Move `tasks_db_path` and `open_tasks_db` into task_rows (or onto AuditContext as an optional `tasks_db` handle that the bin opens once). Make DB-lane degradation a crate-level outcome that any detector can return, and let `reads_tasks_db` be derived from it. Move the cite grammar into a lower `cite_grammar` module shared by PTODO and PPRDSTATUS.

Express the sweep corroboration as an ordered list of rescue steps (each returning Option<Verdict>) shared by both arms, and build findings from one verdict-to-Finding renderer. Use covers_path or path_present_in_tracked in the sweep as well, so P5 has one coverage rule.

findings.statement:
The exit code carries both the High-finding count (`count.min(254)`) and the infra-error code `ERROR_EXIT = 125`, so a run with exactly 125 High findings exits 125. Both doc comments say otherwise:
- ERROR_EXIT is 'Reserved so it never collides with a High-severity finding count'.
- high_severity_exit_code is 'Capped at 254 (not 255) so that exit code 125 remains unambiguously reserved'. The cap protects 255 (TASKS_DB_ABSENT_EXIT), not 125.
Consumers carry the cost: .claude/skills/audit/references/cli-invocation.md §3.1 has every caller JSON-parse stderr and check `len == 125 && all High` before trusting a 125.
findings.proposal: Make the channel injective: map counts that would land on reserved codes to a neighbour (or saturate at 124), or move infra errors outside 1-254. Fix both comments and pin the boundary with a unit test.

findings.statement: Detector internals are made `pub` so that integration tests in separate crates can reach them, and each widening is justified inline by a `// G-allow:` marker so the orphan audit does not flag it. `ptodo::resolve_liveness` exists only as a test-facing wrapper over the private `resolve_liveness_keyed` (its marker says 'its sole caller is the tests/ptodo.rs integration test'). PDOCCOVER exposes its lane grammar (extract_registries, chunk_call_mentions, known_name_index, documented_names, declared_registry_idents, RI_KEYWORDS) for tests/pdoccover.rs. p5 carries `#[doc(hidden)] pub const PRODUCTION_QUERY` for a schema-pin test. The tests therefore pin private grammar signatures rather than the `check` seam. 70 of the crate's 112 G-allow markers exist to justify test-motivated visibility.
findings.proposal: Drive integration tests through `check` and `check_with_stats` over real tempdir fixtures (pdiag's test_support::Fixture already shows the shape). Move pure-grammar tests into in-file `#[cfg(test)]` modules, where private items are visible without `pub`. Delete wrappers such as `resolve_liveness` that exist only for those tests.

findings.statement: No single function owns the user-module front end (read source, derive the module name, parse_with_stdlib, render parse errors, compile with a constraint checker, check the `module` declaration, then evaluate behind the eval guard). Each surface spells it by hand, and the copies differ in substance. The CLI MCP context (load_file, update_source, open_file) compiles with `reify_compiler::compile`. That function's own doc says it uses no prelude and is 'intended only for prelude-module bootstrapping', and that stdlib units such as mm, deg and kg, stdlib traits and stdlib enums are absent and give unresolved-name diagnostics. The same code parses with parse_with_stdlib, and every other surface compiles with compile_with_stdlib_checked plus SimpleConstraintChecker. check_module_path_decl runs only in the CLI (parse_and_compile, and module_dag on the --cfg path). No reify-lsp or mcp_context site calls it. MCP eval also runs without eval_guard::skip_reason, as eval_guard's own doc admits. The three MCP sites have three different parse-error policies: load_file returns Err with rendered messages, update_source returns success:false and changes nothing, and open_file registers the file and clears compiled.
findings.proposal: Give reify_compiler (or a small front-end module that the CLI, LSP, MCP and GUI all depend on) one `compile_user_module(source, path, checker) -> FrontEnd { parsed, compiled, parse_errors }` that includes the module-path check. Put the eval-guard question beside it, so surfaces differ only in what they do with the result. Add one cross-surface test that runs a stdlib-using fixture through each surface and compares error counts.

findings.statement: Which constraint a diagnostic is about crosses the engine/front-end boundary only inside message prose, so each consumer parses it or rebuilds it. To drop the checker's own violation lines, compute_diagnostics_with_state rebuilds the strings `constraint {id} violated` and `constraint {label} violated` and filters check_result.diagnostics by exact message equality. The checker already tags those lines with DiagnosticCode::ConstraintViolated (reify-constraints lib.rs). Two blocks later the same function filters EvalCachedGuardedGroupsFallback by code, with a comment that a copy edit to engine wording 'must never silently re-open the leak' by message matching. The CLI parses the same grammar in reverse: main.rs::indeterminacy_subject_in strips INDETERMINACY_PREFIX and INFIX to recover the subject of a ConstraintIndeterminate line. The engine rewrites ids to labels inside message text and matches claims with `starts_with` (engine_constraints.rs). The host function is one 486-line body with about eight sequential stages: parse, compile, guard, warm or cold eval, check, string-filtered merge, span-aware violations, FEA hint and freshness.
findings.proposal: Carry the constraint subject (ConstraintNodeId plus optional label) as a structured field on reify_core::Diagnostic, or key the LSP filter on (code == ConstraintViolated, subject). Have the CLI read the field instead of parsing text. Then split compute_diagnostics_with_state into per-stage functions that each return diagnostics.

findings.statement: The question 'which declaration kinds own a member list, and what is it' is answered by separate wildcard-terminated matches, each listing Structure, Occurrence, Trait and Purpose and mapping Purpose to `p.members` only. The sites are analysis::find_parsed_member_span_and_doc, analysis::enclosing_decl_name_at, two inline matches in goto_def::compute_goto_definition_with_parsed, and references::entity_members, a private helper the other files do not use. None of them descends into PurposeDef.structures. Value-member resolution therefore cannot see the members of a `structure def` nested in a purpose: goto-def, hover's find_member_decl, and find-references, rename and highlight (collect_references_at uses entity_members(enclosing)) all look only at the purpose's own members. The document outline (symbol_children) does show those members, and the name-level oracles (purpose_nested_decl_names) do resolve the nested structure itself. The crate's own docs call wildcard-terminated per-kind matches the mechanism of 'silent omission as the parser grew', and made the name-level oracles wildcard-free for that reason. The member-level ones were left as they were.
findings.proposal: Give one function the job, beside decl_name_and_span: `member_scopes(decl) -> impl Iterator<Item=(&str, &[MemberDecl])>`, wildcard-free over Declaration and yielding purpose-nested structures as scopes of their own. Route the five lookups and the outline through it. Better still, put it on reify_ast::Declaration, since reify-eval's source_location re-matches the same kinds.

findings.statement: cmd_check (544 lines) chooses its engine setup twice, inline, and the two branches disagree. Without --purpose it computes five capability flags (module_has_geometric_conforms, _representation_within, _dfm_rule, _thickness_dfm_rule, _geometry) and from them picks with_registered_kernel versus Engine::new, set_capture_repr_tol, realize_for_check, tessellate_realizations and ensure_openvdb_kernel. With --purpose it routes on module_has_geometry alone and calls none of set_capture_repr_tol, tessellate_realizations or ensure_openvdb_kernel. A RepresentationWithin or thickness-DFM module checked under --purpose therefore misses the side effects that the no-purpose branch's own comment calls necessary to avoid a silent Indeterminate. cmd_build, cmd_report, cmd_eval and cmd_explain each make their own engine-configuration choice. Each subcommand also hand-rolls its argument loop.
findings.proposal: Derive one `CheckEnginePlan` value from the compiled module (which kernel, capture flags, realize, tessellate, openvdb), with a single function that builds the configured engine from it, and use it in both cmd_check branches and the other subcommands. Then split cmd_check into argument parsing, plan, evaluation and verdict reporting.

findings.statement: compute_diagnostics is a public second diagnostics pipeline with no non-test caller, and it diverges from the one the server runs. Unlike compute_diagnostics_with_state, it does not return early on parse errors, so it compiles the partial AST. It does not filter the checker's own violation lines, emits no span-aware violation errors, no fea-not-evaluated hint and no computation-failed or computation-pending diagnostics, and builds a fresh engine on every call. Its doc says it 'shares' the trampoline-free posture, and eval_guard's module doc lists it among 'all three LSP production entry points'. Tests still go through it heavily, so they assert behaviour of a pipeline no editor runs. The posture lock even has to build a separate probe engine to stand in for its internal one.
findings.proposal: Make compute_diagnostics a one-line wrapper, `compute_diagnostics_with_state(&mut EvalState::new(), source, uri).diagnostics`, or delete it and port its 18 test callers. Then there is one pipeline, and the probe-engine workaround in the posture lock goes away.

findings.statement: No single definition of 'the value cells of a template' exists, and two LSP consumers get it wrong. Three loops in analysis.rs and eval_guard::stage_one_scanned_cells all chain template.value_cells with guarded_groups[*].members and else_members. eval_guard's doc spells out why: 'value_cells is a strict subset of what reaches the graph', and scanning the subset 'made the absence proof unsound'. compute_diagnostics_with_state iterates `template.value_cells` alone in two places. One is the freshness loop, so no computation-failed or computation-pending diagnostic is ever considered for a member inside a `where`/`else` branch. The other is the FEA hint's value_cell_exprs map, so a constraint that reaches an @optimized solver through a guarded let gets no fea-not-evaluated hint. reify-compiler has no accessor, so the chain is re-spelled across the workspace.
findings.proposal: Add `TopologyTemplate::all_value_cells()` (value_cells plus guarded members and else_members) in reify-compiler, and route these sites and the 16 workspace chains through it. Keep a bare value_cells read only where excluding guarded members is deliberate, with a comment saying so.

findings.statement: is_reserved_keyword's doc says it decides whether a name is 'a reserved Reify keyword (and therefore not a valid rename target)'. It actually tests membership of completion.rs's TOP_LEVEL_KEYWORDS, BODY_KEYWORDS and EXPR_KEYWORDS, the 26 words the editor offers as completions, which are pub(crate) only so references.rs can borrow them. The language spec's reserved-word table (§2.10, mirrored by reify-audit's RI_KEYWORDS with joint added) has 47 words. The 21 missing from the rename gate are as, chain, def, exists, field, forall, implies, in, joint, map, match, meta, module, none, out, pub, self, set, some, undef and unit. compute_rename and compute_rename_cross_file therefore accept renaming a binding to `match`, `forall` or `unit`. That breaks the gate's stated purpose, keeping the result re-parsing cleanly (Invariant 5). The rename test samples only let, param, structure and if, all from the completion lists.
findings.proposal: Have the grammar's owner (reify-syntax) export one reserved-keyword list, derived from or tested against grammar.js and the spec table. Make the rename gate and reify-audit read it. Keep completion's lists as UX tables over it.

findings.statement: Where a handler's CPU work runs is decided by hand, handler by handler, against the cost of the work. goto_definition, prepare_rename, rename and references go through BlockingWorkPlacement::run. goto_definition needs only a parse. hover and completion, by contrast, build AnalysisContext::from_parsed, which runs compile_with_stdlib_checked plus Engine::check on every request. did_open and did_change run the full compile and eval under a std::sync::Mutex. All of those run inline on the async worker that the stdio server shares across requests, and blocking_work's module doc exists to keep exactly that worker free. Only the four listed handlers are pinned: lib.rs's test enumerates exactly those requests. AnalysisContext's Send-safety note cites 'server.rs:268-284' for the hover handler. That handler is at line 565, and line 268 falls inside evaluate_and_forward_logs' doc.
findings.proposal: Run every handler that builds an AnalysisContext or compiles through `self.blocking_work.run`, perhaps via one helper that combines the document lookup, AnalysisContext construction and placement. Extend blocking_work_requests to hover and completion so the placement test covers them.

findings.statement: Production prose in this slice is mostly reviewer-answering rationale: measurements, rejected alternatives, task-scope disclaimers and task numbers. Inline it drifts, and the drift is visible. eval_guard.rs's 400 production lines are 78% comment. Doc comments contain sentences such as 'Rendering the offender in the hover panel itself would mean editing hover.rs, outside this task's file scope' (analysis.rs) and 'declaring one means a mod line in lib.rs, which is outside this task's file scope' (eval_guard.rs). Pointers are stale: 'server.rs:268-284' (hover is at 565) and 'cache.rs:482-513' twice for mark_pending (now at reify-eval cache.rs:989). Commits such as 4a15e3d4cb ('retire the four rustdoc claims this change makes literally false') and 7d4e7555f8 ('correct two overstated claims in the containment predicate's doc') show the prose being repaired after the fact.
findings.proposal: Move the measurements, rejected alternatives and scope notes into the task records and commit messages they came from, and the durable rationale into docs/ (for example a docs/notes page on the eval-guard containment), with a one-line pointer from code. Replace file:line pointers with symbol names.

findings.statement: build_cross_file_rig is documented as 'the shared cross-file rig', but only rename and references use it. goto_definition and prepare_rename each inline their own copy of the stdlib-root fallback, the ModuleResolver construction and the open-buffer-over-disk resolve_import closure. The dev-mode stdlib fallback `root.join("crates/reify-compiler/stdlib")` is therefore spelled 3 times in server.rs, and again in reify-cli main.rs (relative to the input file's parent directory) and in gui engine.rs. The document-lookup prologue (read lock, documents.get, drop) is repeated in 8 handlers.
findings.proposal: Split build_cross_file_rig into `import_resolver(root, stdlib_path, open_docs)` and `workspace_docs(root, &open_docs)`, and call the resolver half from goto_definition and prepare_rename. Resolve the stdlib fallback once, at initialize, into ServerState.

findings.statement: Completion advertises 96 builtin functions from a hand-written table of signature and doc strings, with no parity link to the compiler. reify-lsp does not depend on reify-builtins, and only 3 of the 96 names appear in the registry's seeded rows today. The builtin-signature-registry PRD measured 35 LSP signatures that the type checker contradicts and owns the fix (its success table, row 12). Until then, a compiler-side signature change leaves completion advertising the old one.
findings.proposal: Per the PRD's row 12, render completion and hover signatures from reify-builtins rows as names migrate. Meanwhile, a drift test could assert that every BUILTIN_FUNCTIONS name the compiler knows has a matching result type.

findings.statement: DiagnosticsResult returns only diagnostics, geometry_output and log_messages, so the tests that need the evaluated constraint outcomes or the engine's posture read EvalState's private fields instead. diagnostics.rs tests reach state.engine and the private last_content_hash and version_counter fields directly. The posture lock calls state.engine.check_snapshot itself to get constraint results. Elsewhere in the slice, instrumentation for tests sits inside production state: mcp_context's CliState carries a #[cfg(test)] engine_construction_count field, and server.rs exposes a #[cfg(test)] pub(crate) eval_state() accessor.
findings.proposal: Return the CheckResult (or a constraint-outcome summary) and the engine posture in DiagnosticsResult, and make the tests assert through it.

findings.statement: Each MCP write tool's contract is fused inside an anonymous closure passed to ToolRegistry::register. That contract is the JSON schema, the hand-parsed params (`params["x"].as_str().ok_or_else(..)`) and the json! result envelope. No typed request or response value exists to reuse: types.rs's UpdateResult/SetParamResult do not describe the wire envelope, and write.rs discards UpdateResult. The GUI's live MCP surface is the reify-debug HTTP server, because the sidecar allowlists mcp__reify-debug__*. That server therefore re-implements the five same-named tools (reify_update_source, reify_set_parameter, reify_open_file, reify_save_file, reify_export) with its own ToolDefs, param parsers and envelope fns. The contracts have since diverged on substance. reify-mcp's reify_set_parameter says the value is a bare number installed as the SI magnitude and that no unit suffix is parsed (task 6184, 2026-08-24). The debug server's tool of the same name says the unit suffix is REQUIRED and a bare number is refused (task 5757, the same day). The GUI's own reify-mcp path, TauriToolContext::set_parameter, goes through commit_parameter to apply_param_to_source_str, which refuses bare numbers on dimensioned cells. So reify-mcp's own description is false on the GUI host. That path is the `mcp_tool_call` Tauri command, and no frontend code calls it. Parity between the surfaces is pinned only by a GUI test that hand-transcribes key sets (`reify_write_tool_envelopes_match_the_reify_mcp_shapes`), so a reify-mcp envelope or semantics change cannot red it.
findings.proposal: Give each MCP tool a typed request/response pair plus one schema owned by reify-mcp, for example `struct SetParameterRequest`/`SetParameterResponse` with serde and a schema derived from it. Expose them for both hosts to dispatch through. Settle reify_set_parameter's value grammar once in that type. Delete or wire the dead mcp_tool_call path so only live surfaces carry the names.

findings.statement: InProcessLsp::handle_request routes on raw method-name strings in a 14-arm match (lizard CCN 39, 135 lines). Each arm repeats a parse_params/await/map_err/to_value body. The same set of method names is spelled independently in error_prefix (13 consts), gui lsp_bridge.rs::lane_for_method (8 concurrency-safe names, with unlisted names defaulting to the serial lane), gui lsp_lane_routing_tests.rs (three hand-copied const arrays of 6, 8 and 14), blocking_work.rs test_support (4) and gui/src/editor/lspClient.ts (14 calls). The fact that a method is read-only and so concurrency-safe is a server-side property (it takes state.read()), but it is declared in the GUI crate. The routing test's own docstring concedes that 'An arm ADDED there is not caught until it is transcribed here.' The handle_request doc contract already drifted: its list of Ok(Value) requests omits textDocument/references, which the match handles. It also carries a 'Breaking change' paragraph, which is commit-message prose.
findings.proposal: Define a `LspMethod` enum in reify-lsp with FromStr/as_str, an `ALL` table and a `fn is_read_only_query(self)` owned next to the handlers. handle_request then matches on the enum. lane_for_method calls the predicate, and the routing tests iterate LspMethod::ALL instead of hand copies.

findings.statement: compute_hover_in_context is one 212-line function (lizard CCN 36, 10 `return Some` exits). It inlines a hover renderer for every symbol class: members, match-arm clusters, structures/occurrences, five Declaration arms, relation builtins and keywords. The Declaration loop ends in `_ => {}`. Of the 11 named Declaration kinds that the crate's own NAMED_DECL_SNIPPETS table enumerates, hover renders 7 (Structure, Occurrence, Enum, Function, Trait, Unit, TypeAlias). Hovering the declared name of a `field def`, `purpose`, `constraint def` or `joint` silently returns None. analysis, goto_def and references each loop over NAMED_DECL_SNIPPETS so a new kind is covered automatically, but hover is not a consumer and no hover test covers those four kinds. The fix history shows the cost: TypeAlias and Unit variants existed by 2026-05-27, and their hover arms arrived as separate RED/GREEN tasks on 2026-08-20 (#6341) and 2026-09-18 (#6972). There have been 22 commits to hover.rs since 2026-07-06.
findings.proposal: Split per-symbol-class renderers into small functions and dispatch declaration-name hover through an exhaustive (wildcard-free) match on Declaration, as decl_name_and_span already does. Add hover as a consumer of NAMED_DECL_SNIPPETS so a missing kind reds.

findings.statement: The MCP wire types carry enum-valued facts as free `String`s: ParameterInfo.kind and .determinacy, ConstraintInfo.status, EvalStatusInfo.phase, and DiagnosticInfo.severity (from reify-core). reify-mcp defines no vocabulary for them, so each ReifyToolContext host invents its own. For kind, the CLI emits "Auto(free)" for a free auto cell while the GUI's cell_kind_gui_str emits "Auto" for both. For status, the CLI always emits "unknown" while the GUI emits satisfied/violated/indeterminate via satisfaction_token. Yet reify_get_constraints advertises filtering by 'satisfied'/'violated' with an exact `!=` compare, so on the CLI host that filter matches nothing. The severity filter, by contrast, is case-insensitive. ValueCellKind has no canonical keyword method. It is rendered to strings by four separate functions in three vocabularies: hover.rs "param/let/auto(free)/auto", CLI mcp_context "Param/Let/Auto(free)/Auto", and GUI engine.rs "Param/Let/Auto" and "param/let/auto".
findings.proposal: Make these fields serde enums in reify-mcp, or reuse reify-core's enums with a fixed serde rename, and give ValueCellKind one `keyword()` rendering that hover, both MCP hosts and the GUI derive from. The filter then compares typed values.

findings.statement: The language-reference topic registry is enumerated three times in this file: 19 `const X: &str = include_str!("chunks/x.md")` items, the 19-entry TOPICS slice, and a 19-arm get_chunk match (lizard CCN 20). A test also pins the bare count 19. Their mutual consistency is enforced from a different crate. reify-compiler's harness_doc_chunks/fence_gate.rs reads language_chunks.rs as TEXT, locates the TOPICS literal by the exact anchor string `pub const TOPICS: &[&str] = &[`, and substring-scans for `include_str!("chunks/<stem>.md")`. That is an ad-hoc parser of another crate's source, which reds if the file is reformatted or the registry is restructured. The 2026-10-07 split of measurement/topology out of geometry (#7344) had to touch all three lists, the count test and the gate, and a follow-up amend added the 'no get_chunk arm' panic message.
findings.proposal: Use a single `const CHUNKS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("syntax", include_str!(..)), ..]` table. Derive TOPICS/available_topics and get_chunk from it, drop the count test, and have fence_gate call `reify_mcp::tools::language_chunks::available_topics()` (as a dev-dependency) instead of parsing the source file.

findings.statement: No shipped binary ever loads a reify.toml. Manifest::load_from_path and Manifest::from_toml_str have zero callers outside reify-config and test code. The only production call of Engine::with_registered_kernels_and_manifest (engine_admin.rs with_registered_kernels) passes None. So the whole parsed schema is inert in production: kernel pins, [auto_type_params], [warm_state] and [[node_overrides]]. The crate's own rustdoc misdescribes this in both directions. It says 'no other workspace crate consumes it yet', but reify-cli, reify-compiler and reify-eval all depend on it. It also says of warm_state_budget_bytes that 'The engine consumer calls this ... env > manifest > default', a ladder whose manifest rung is never fed. Only node_overrides is documented as inert (docs/notes/reify-toml-schema.md). The defaults docs ('callers MUST consume it via Manifest::auto_type_params') are likewise unmet: the compiler uses AutoTypeParamsConfig::default() directly.
findings.proposal: Either wire one production loader (CLI/GUI resolve the project reify.toml and pass it to with_registered_kernels_and_manifest), or state the inert status once on Manifest and point the per-section docs at it. Correct the 'no other crate consumes it' and 'engine consumer calls this' sentences either way.

findings.statement: JsonRpcRequest.id is a non-optional serde_json::Value without #[serde(default)], so a JSON-RPC notification (a message with no id) fails deserialization. McpDispatcher::dispatch then answers it with a -32700 'Parse error' response carrying id null. An MCP client sends `notifications/initialized` right after initialize, and JSON-RPC requires no reply to a notification. The stdio server's handshake therefore always emits one spurious error line. No test covers an id-less message (jsonrpc_tests covers null-id and array-id only). The GUI debug server's separate JSON-RPC types model `id: Option<Value>` and handle notifications/initialized, so the workspace carries two JSON-RPC envelope implementations with different notification semantics. Within jsonrpc.rs, the response envelope is built inline 8 times, and line 106 uses the literal -32603 instead of the INTERNAL_ERROR const it defines.
findings.proposal: Model `id: Option<Value>`, treat None as a notification that produces no output line, add a test, and build responses through one ok/err constructor as the debug server already does.

findings.statement: convert_diagnostic emits a `reify_lsp::auto_type_param` tracing event only for a hand-enumerated list of AutoTypeParam* codes. The list has 6 entries, while DiagnosticCode now has 9 AutoTypeParam* variants: BoundedInfeasible, CandidateNotConstructible and ConstraintUnevaluated are silently excluded. The comment above the list says 'the four AutoTypeParam diagnostic codes'. The test asserts exactly 6 events while claiming to cover 'every auto-type-param diagnostic surface', so it pins the stale list rather than the family. DiagnosticCode has no family predicate. The same block carries a 'Behavioral note: unlike the previous #[cfg(debug_assertions)] eprintln!' paragraph, which is commit-message prose.
findings.proposal: Add `DiagnosticCode::is_auto_type_param()` in reify-core, generated from or exhaustively matched against the enum. Call it here, have the test iterate the family, and drop the stale count and the behavioral-note prose.

findings.statement: The doc lowering has no single answer to 'render this expression as text' and uses six ad-hoc strategies. Constraints and constraint defs slice the source by span. A param default splits the declaration text at the first '='. Sub-component args render as the literal `name = ...`. Realization ops render as `format!("{op:?}")` truncated to 80 chars. A purpose objective renders as the placeholder `<minimize>`/`<maximize>`, chosen from the first term only. An annotation Expr renders as `<expr>`. build_stdlib_doc_model passes an empty source string, so for the whole stdlib every param default with a value renders `<default>` and every constraint expr_repr is empty. The rustdoc also misstates the output: it promises 'Structures (in declaration order)' then 'Occurrences' as separate groups, but one loop over compiled.templates interleaves them in source order. ModuleDoc.cross_refs is always Default here, even though reify-doc's docs say ModuleCrossRefs is 'populated by the lowering slice'.
findings.proposal: Introduce one expression-rendering seam, such as an AST/IR pretty-printer reachable from the compiled side or a carried source span on CompiledExpr. Route all six fields through it, so stdlib and user modules render the same way, and correct the ordering and cross_refs docs.

findings.statement: parse_node_id's Value arm hand-rolls the `<entity>.<member>` grammar: split_once('.'), the empty-halves check and the multiple-dot rejection. Those are the same three checks reify-core's ValueCellId::from_str already implements with a typed ValueCellIdParseError. The two parsers word their errors differently and can drift independently. The command also prints `node: {node_id}` using NodeId's Display (e.g. `Foo#computation[0]`), a form parse_node_id does not accept (it wants `Compute(Foo[0])`), so the tool's output cannot be pasted back as its input.
findings.proposal: Have the Value arm call `inner.parse::<ValueCellId>()` and map ValueCellIdParseError into the user message.

findings.statement:
Each invariant's status is a hand-kept cell in two registries, docs/invariants.md and docs/legibility/design-invariants.md. Nothing links a row to the code that enforces it, and both registries have drifted in both directions. Eight of the 13 rows in docs/invariants.md marked `proposed` already have their named mechanism in the tree:
- INV-EVAL-1: cell_commit.rs commit_cell_result and CacheLeg.
- INV-EVAL-2: cell_eval_ctx.rs.
- INV-EVAL-3: detectors.rs DetectorRegistry and NodeCache.diagnostics.
- INV-EVAL-4: cache_divergence.rs and harness_cache/snapshot_cache_divergence_gate.rs.
- INV-EVAL-5: invariants.rs check_no_stale_undef.
- INV-FEA-2: the catch_unwind at engine_compute.rs:276.
- INV-FEA-3: tests/infra/test_nan_safe_ordering_guard_wired.sh.
- INV-GUI-1: the gui_state! macro, which by its own doc makes an unclassified field fail to compile, i.e. type-enforced.

Rows marked enforced misdescribe their mechanism:
- INV-GEO-4 says the stub arm is instantiated and the has_occt real arm is 'not yet wired'. The reverse is true: the real arm has been instantiated at reify-kernel-occt lib.rs:14385 since ca22b761d8 (2026-07-10). The stub arm only compiles where OCCT is absent, which the gate makes fatal.
- INV-COMP-2 reads 'registered in exactly one place … enforced(test)', but the test it relies on (reify-eval registry_drift_tests.rs) opens by stating that a name is registered in '>= 7 places'. It checks cross-crate agreement, and only for the geometry and selector families.

The design-invariants census table has the same problem:
- PPRDSTATUS is listed as 'chartered', yet reify-audit's bin dispatches it.
- PCITE and PDCHECK ship in the bin with no census row, although the doc requires 'a census row in the same change'.
- INV-PD-1 and INV-PD-2 name `reify-audit --pattern PDROP` / `PVAC` as their enforcement in the present tense; neither pattern exists.

INV-META-1 ('flip status in the same change') is itself `proposed` and has no checker. The last registry edit, 32f1c3e160 'put INV-GUI-2's registry status back in agreement with reality', was a manual repair of exactly this drift.
findings.proposal: Give each row a machine-checkable enforcement pointer (a symbol path or test path) and add one reify-audit pattern or infra test, the INV-META-1 checker, that fails when an `enforced` row's pointer does not resolve, or when a `proposed` row's pointer already does. The census table and the bin's pattern list should derive from one detector registry.
findings.change_note: not re-observed this run (prose/slug anchor or unsliced); task-store disposition only

findings.statement: reify-compiler restates the expression-nesting bound as three independent literals: recursion_guard::MAX_COMPILE_RECURSION_DEPTH = 256, dot_chain_lint::MAX_EXPR_DEPTH = 256, and shadow_lint::MAX_EXPR_DEPTH = 256. shadow_lint's doc says only that it 'Mirrors the convention in dot_chain_lint.rs'. The three copies apply opposite policies when the bound is exceeded. The guard's doc promises to 'cleanly reject anything beyond with a diagnostic' (ExpressionNestingTooDeep). Both lints instead `debug_assert!(false, …)` and then truncate silently. The lints run first: compile_with_prelude_context_checked_with_config calls them at lib.rs:535-536, before any compile recursion. So in a debug build, which is what the test suite and agents run, the guard's diagnostic path can never be reached through the public pipeline; the process panics in the lint instead. The only over-cap test (geometry.rs deeply_nested_boolean_geometry_does_not_overflow_2mb_stack, 1500 levels) calls compile_geometry_call_no_constraints directly and so skips the lints. The public-API test nests only 64 levels.
findings.proposal: Make MAX_COMPILE_RECURSION_DEPTH the single bound, and have both lints import it. Over the cap, the lints should stop walking without asserting and leave the reporting to the guard's ExpressionNestingTooDeep diagnostic. Add one test that compiles a 300-deep source through the public entry and asserts the diagnostic.

findings.statement:
Solver option defaults are declared in the stdlib .ri structure defs and then restated in Rust at up to three further homes, which already disagree.

ElasticOptions declares 17 params. Five have no reader anywhere in production code: mesh_size, max_iter, cg_tolerance, force_tet and target_quantity_of_interest. In particular `param max_iter : Int = 1000` is never consulted; elastic_static.rs uses `SOLVER_MAX_ITER = 2000`.

ModalOptions declares tol = 1e-9 and max_iters = 200. modal_ops::extract_eigen_knobs restates those as Rust fallbacks. run_mechanism_modal then discards them (modal_ops.rs:2422, `let (requested_n_modes, _, _, _) = extract_eigen_knobs(options)`) and builds `EigenSolverOptions { n_modes, ..Default::default() }` (modal_ops.rs:2284). That Default lives in reify-solver-elastic eigensolve.rs and is tol 1e-8, max_iters 1000.

BucklingOptions (10 / 1e-8 / 1000) is restated in extract_buckling_options and again in buckling_kernel's own default (lines 71-72). shell_threshold = 0.2 is restated as a Rust local at elastic_static.rs:5551.

This is the INV-PD-1 (declared-param-reaches-kernel) surface. Its owning PRD, trampoline-param-drop-closure.md (rows A6/A7/A9), records several of these sites, and its PDROP detector is still chartered.
findings.proposal: Decode each options structure once, into a typed struct whose defaults come from the compiled structure_def's default_expr values, which are already in the IR. The trampolines should read that struct, not raw field strings with literal fallbacks. Declared params with no reader become the declared-ignored set that INV-PD-1 requires.

findings.statement:
A compute target's identity and its result schema are spelled independently on each side of the .ri/Rust boundary.

Identity: the stdlib .ri carries 16 distinct `@optimized("…")` target strings, and register_compute_fns registers 18 string literals. No check relates the two sets. Two Rust targets have no .ri entry:
