- solver::tensegrity_load. Its trampoline doc says it receives inputs 'matching the future tensegrity_load signature', a signature that was never declared, so the target is registered but unreachable from .ri.
- fdm::as_printed_material_r0, which is reached only through a Rust rung-to-string map in as_printed_material.rs:500.

reify-lsp keeps a third hand copy, ALL_PRODUCTION_COMPUTE_TARGETS, in diagnostics.rs tests. Its doc admits that an addition upstream 'is NOT caught' because reify-eval exposes no enumerator over compute_registry.fns.

Result schema: 7 StructureInstance type_names minted by trampolines have no stdlib `structure def` at all: ShellExtractionResult, MidSurfaceMesh, SegmentationResult, MidSurfaceAttributes and RegionInfo (shell-extract), TensegrityLoadResult, and CarriedTopology. Their field sets exist only in the Rust minters and in the per-decoder string literals, so INV-PD-2's field census, which is keyed on the .ri declaration, cannot see them.
findings.proposal: Expose a public `Engine::registered_compute_targets()` (or a static target table). Add a compile-side or test-side check that every stdlib `@optimized` string is registered and every registered target has a .ri caller or an explicit engine-inserted allowlist. Declare the shell-extract, tensegrity_load and carried-topology result structures in stdlib .ri so that INV-PD-2 covers them.

findings.statement:
reify-core defines the wire type DiagnosticInfo with `code: Option<String>` but no constructor from Diagnostic. Each surface writes its own projection, and they disagree on the one field that INV-SF-6 (diagnostics-carry-codes) exists to protect:
- gui/src-tauri engine.rs::diagnostics_to_info writes `code: None`. It is called from 3 sites and feeds the GUI problems panel.
- reify-cli mcp_context.rs:292 writes `code: None`. It feeds AI/MCP clients.
- reify-lsp convert.rs::convert_diagnostic serialises the DiagnosticCode through serde.

The only values that ever reach DiagnosticInfo.code are ad-hoc GUI strings that are not DiagnosticCode names: "hot-reload-error" (2 sites) and "unresolved-source" (1 site). gui/src/types.ts documents `code === "unresolved-source"` as a contract. As a result, a GUI or MCP consumer that needs to tell diagnostic kinds apart has to match message text, which is the pattern behind per-area findings cg-ck.1 and tooling.2.
findings.proposal: Add `DiagnosticInfo::from_diagnostic(&Diagnostic, file_path, &LineIndex)` in reify-core that serialises DiagnosticCode the way convert.rs does, and route the GUI and CLI projections through it. Model the GUI-only states (hot-reload error, unresolved source) as DiagnosticCode variants instead of free strings.

findings.statement:
What a support kind clamps is decided in five places, with no shared decode:
- stdlib .ri structure defs FixedSupport and PinnedSupport (fea_multi_case.ri:359/384).
- reify-stdlib supports.rs, whose module doc is the stated contract: 'PinnedSupport on a shell entity … constrains translational DOFs only, leaving rotational DOFs free'.
- reify-solver-elastic shell_boundary::SupportKind {Fixed, Pinned} with build_support_bcs, which implements that contract.
- reify-eval modal_ops' own enum DeclaredSupport {Fixed, Pinned}, decoded by `support.type_name == "PinnedSupport"` with every other type falling through to Fixed, plus its face_realization beam-pin policy.
- elastic_static::loads_supports_to_bc_node_sets, which returns a bare node set and clamps every DOF whatever the kind.

The typed solver-side home is not reached for the case it exists for. The only production call of build_support_bcs, in solver shell_solve.rs, passes SupportKind::Fixed on auto-chosen root nodes. reify-eval compute_targets/shell_solve.rs has no reference to supports at all. A user PinnedSupport on a shell-routed body therefore never reaches the Pinned arm.
findings.proposal: Decode a Support StructureInstance once, in reify-eval, into reify_solver_elastic::SupportKind (extended as kinds are added). Make modal_ops' face_realization and elastic_static's BC build consume that value, and thread user supports into the shell route instead of the coordinate root clamp.

findings.statement:
reify-ir already provides `Value::as_f64` (Int, Real, Scalar -> f64, otherwise None), used on 312 production lines. Even so, 8 private helpers across 3 crates re-implement the same match:
- appearance::color_cell_f64, whose doc says 'Intentional mirror of dynamics_ops::cell_f64'.
- bom_report::value_as_f64.
- dynamics_ops::cell_f64.
- the inner fn cell_f64 in dynamics_psd.
- reify-stdlib dynamics/eval::cell_f64.
- trajectory/input_shape::read_scalar_si.
- trajectory/trampoline::read_scalar_si.
- gui engine.rs::scalar_to_f64.

Two more copies have already drifted from it: tensegrity_crack::scalar_f64 drops the Int arm, and modal_ops::read_scalar_si maps non-numeric values to 0.0. The canonical accessor is dimension-blind, so the copies cannot be distinguished by unit policy either.
findings.proposal: Delete the 8 equivalent copies in favour of Value::as_f64. If a dimension-checked read is wanted, add it once as a Value method (for example `as_si(expected: DimensionVector)`) and migrate the two drifted variants to an explicit policy.

findings.statement: The set of kernel names is defined in reify-core by KernelId::ALL, as_registry_name and from_registry_name, which is the documented single authority (reify-config re-exports it). module_pragmas.rs nevertheless keeps its own literal `KNOWN_V02_KERNELS = ["fidget", "manifold", "occt", "openvdb"]`, so `#kernel(<ident>)` validation does not derive from KernelId. The compiler stores the pragma as a String (module.kernel_pragma), and reify-eval looks it up again by string in Engine.geometry_kernels, a BTreeMap<String, _> keyed partly by the synthetic "__reify_eval_default_kernel". The name-to-KernelId bridges then disagree on unknown names: dispatcher.rs:779 `.expect()`s, while engine_build.rs:104 silently maps any unknown name to KernelId::Occt. A KernelId variant added in reify-core is therefore not accepted by the compiler, and a pragma name the compiler accepts is never checked against the registry names.
findings.proposal: Derive the accepted pragma set from KernelId::ALL, filtered by a KernelId method such as `is_user_selectable()` that states the gmsh exclusion once. Parse the pragma into KernelId at compile time, so CompiledModule carries a typed value rather than a String.
Add an intra-crate module-SCC ratchet (count and members per crate) beside assert-crate-dag.sh so upward crate:: paths are measured on every change.

findings.statement: The compute ABI crate sits above the solver it is meant to abstract. Its lib doc calls it an 'OCCT-free foundation crate' for reify-eval 'AND future non-OCCT evaluation engines'. Yet it normal-depends on reify-solver-elastic, and through it on reify-kernel-gmsh, which links libgmsh and so OCCT 7.9 per the repo's native-deps notes. The edge exists for two reasons. First, the generic StructuredComputeDetail enum has one variant, Fea(reify_solver_elastic::FeaDiagnosticDetail). Second, 2,563 of the crate's 2,883 lines are elastic_result.rs: the ElasticResult schema, the slab codec and From<PartialElasticResult>. Its only consumer is reify-eval, which re-exports every type at the old paths (the canonical engine_compute and persistent_cache shims). So the crate adds a layer without narrowing anything, and any non-FEA engine built on it would pull the FEA solver. The meshing-service PRD's ζ (#8289) removes gmsh from the solver but keeps contract -> solver.

Which geometry kernels an Engine has is decided by link-time side effects, not by the constructor's arguments. Kernel crates `inventory::submit!` a KernelRegistration, and each binary must anchor them with `extern crate X as _;`. Today reify-cli main.rs anchors occt, manifold and openvdb(cfg). gui lib.rs anchors only openvdb(cfg); occt reaches the GUI through an OCCT_AVAILABLE const read, the mechanism the CLI comment calls unreliable. reify-lsp anchors nothing.

with_registered_kernel then instantiates the lexicographically least BRep-capable registration, or failing that the least of any (kernel_registry::pick_lexmin_brep_kernel_in). Build routing also reads the process-global registry directly, through collect_registry() at 5 engine_build entry points and registry() at engine_constraints.rs:1018. That registry can list kernels this Engine never instantiated: the CLI links manifold but instantiates only the pick plus openvdb.

The result is that the production binaries carry different kernel sets: reify {occt, manifold, openvdb}, reify-gui {occt, openvdb} (no manifold dependency), reify-lsp {}. Tests are shaped by it too:
- 17 extern-crate anchors across 10 reify-eval test files;
- a test_registry_override engine field behind test-instrumentation;
- reify-eval/Cargo.toml prose forbidding dev-deps that 'would pull inventory::submit! in and break registry-size or default-kernel assertions'.

Engine assembly is repeated at 19 production sites in 5 crates, and ensure_openvdb_kernel is called separately at 3 of them.

reify-ir has a 4-module SCC {geometry, value, expr, boundary_attachment}. It exists because geometry.rs (13,364 lines) holds two strata:
- leaf geometry identifiers that Value embeds: GeometryHandleId, FeatureId, Role, FaceSurfaceKind, EdgeCurveKind, ModEntry;
- the kernel-interface layer that consumes Value: GeometryKernel, GeometryOp, GeometryQuery, ValidatedMesh.

value.rs imports those identifiers from geometry at 25 sites, while geometry.rs imports `crate::value::{SampledField, Value}` back. boundary_attachment.rs (76 lines) imports GeometryHandleId, and geometry.rs imports its BoundaryAssociation. value.rs also imports CompiledExpr, so every kernel crate compiles against a module cycle that contains the expression IR.

This also measures geometry.rs's h14 alarm. Carving the identifiers into their own module produces a file with no upward import and leaves geometry.rs importing only downward, so the candidate partition passes heuristic 13.

The reify-constraints -> reify-stdlib crate edge exists only for a re-export shim. lib.rs:31-42 re-exports 9 loop_closure_solver names and JointKind/JointValue. Its comment says reify-constraints 'already depends on [reify-stdlib] for FK primitives', but reify-constraints production code references reify_stdlib nowhere else. Only 5 test files use the shim paths, and nothing in production does. mechanism_loop_closure_chains and JointKind are never reached through the shim. Meanwhile the Newton loop-closure solver lives in the builtin-value crate: kinematics, dynamics and trajectory code is about 43k of reify-stdlib's 93k lines. So the solver crate re-exports a solver that lives in the value library.

reify-kernel-occt keeps an optional upward dependency on reify-mesh-morph, which normal-depends on reify-eval. It exists solely for OcctProjector, a 69-line impl of mesh-morph's Projector trait. mesh-morph's KernelProjector (boundary.rs:143) 'supersedes the legacy OcctProjector ... for the engine path' by adapting any GeometryKernel through closest_point_on_shape/vertex_point, and OcctProjector 'stays for its own occt-feature tests'.

The `mesh-morph` feature is enabled only by occt's own self-dev-dep. occt's Cargo comment says 'Engine wiring (task ε / 2947) enables this feature', but #2947 is cancelled. With the feature on, occt's normal closure grows from 4 to 21 workspace crates. Cargo.toml prose in gmsh, manifold, openvdb, kernel-conformance and reify-eval explains how to work around this edge.

types.ts is the TS mirror of gui/src-tauri/src/types.rs and has 0 import statements. PersistentViewState, an IPC type returned by bridge.ts readViewSidecar, nevertheless reaches up into two stores through inline import() types: stores/autoViewGenerator ViewDefinition and stores/viewportStore CameraState. types.ts:973 is the import graph's only cycle-closing deferred import, and it produces the graph's only hidden cycle, because autoViewGenerator.ts imports EntityTreeNode/VisibilityState from types. The Rust side defines both shapes in types.rs as ViewDefinitionData and CameraStateData, documented as mirroring the stores. So on the TS side the wire stratum does not own two of its own wire types.

The import graph's one hard TS module cycle runs between panels/diagnosticsView.ts and DiagnosticsPanel.tsx. diagnosticsView.ts holds the pure filter/group helpers, yet it imports the DiagnosticEntry type from the component DiagnosticsPanel.tsx. The component in turn imports filterDiagnostics, groupDiagnostics and 2 types from diagnosticsView.ts. The view model depends on the view for its own input type. DiagnosticEntry is consumed by diagnosticsView.ts, panels/index.ts and App.tsx.

Four separate mechanisms decide which geometry kernel serves a request, and only one of them reads CapabilityDescriptor.

1. **GeometryOps**: dispatcher::dispatch over CapabilityDescriptor.supports(op, repr). It is called at 3 sites in engine_build.rs (6417, 7823, 7838) and is the only production reader of the descriptor.
2. **Default kernel**: queries, export, tessellate, post-process, DFM and constraint passes index geometry_kernels by Engine.default_kernel_name. That name is 74 references in 7 reify-eval files (engine_build 48, engine_admin 11, geometry_ops 8, engine_constraints 4, engine_eval, realization_content, realize_solid_sdf).
3. **Handle provenance**: lookups go through the kernel recorded on a handle and silently fall back to the default kernel when that name is absent (engine_build 9262; realization_content 355).
4. **Hard-coded KernelIds**: Mesh to VolumeMesh and morph storage use KernelId::Gmsh (engine_build 9301, 9453). Voxel/SDF uses KernelId::OpenVdb (engine_build 9635, realization_content 242, realize_solid_sdf 149).

The map key itself varies by construction path. Engine::new and with_prelude store the single kernel under the synthetic DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME, while with_registered_kernels uses KernelId::as_registry_name. So realization_content needs a registry-name-then-default fallback chain. A request for a handle produced by a non-default kernel can therefore reach a different kernel without any diagnostic.

The descriptor declares Operations only, so query/export capability (cg-ck seam 1) and the Gmsh/OpenVdb conversions are not expressible in it. Each new conversion or kernel adds another hard-coded arm. Related canonical findings cover the trait surface (reify-ir geometry.rs::GeometryKernel h9) and the hard-coded openvdb arm (realization_content h11); this finding is the selection axis that spans them.
findings.proposal: Make kernel selection one function in dispatcher.rs taking (request kind: Op | Query | Export | Conversion, handle provenance, demanded repr) and returning a KernelId. Key geometry_kernels by KernelId, removing the synthetic DEFAULT_KERNEL_NAME. Extend CapabilityDescriptor to declare queries, exports and conversions, so the Gmsh/OpenVdb arms become descriptor rows.

findings.statement:
The same engine writes (open/load file, set parameter, update source, save, export, set FEA case) are scheduled and published by two independent mechanisms, chosen by which front door the request came through.

- **Tauri command path**: commands.rs builds EvalRequest values (8 sites, plus main.rs 1 and mcp_context.rs 1), which the EvalQueue orders, coalesces by EditIdentity and publishes as generation-stamped deltas. eval_queue.rs's module doc calls the queue "the ENGINE lane's single front door: every engine-touching request is submitted here".
- **Debug server path**: debug_server.rs runs 13 engine closures through its own run_on_engine, a spawn_on_large_stack plus with_engine_lock. These are 6 writes (open_source_into_engine_and_refresh_baseline, set_fea_case_on_engine, and write_on_engine_and_refresh_baseline for set_parameter, update_source, save_file, export) and 7 reads. None of them is submitted to the queue. The debug server holds `evals: Arc<EvalQueue>` but reads it only for health and wait_for_idle. It advances its own diff baseline via compute_delta and pushes state with query_frontend.

Interleaving with queued command-path edits is therefore excluded only by the 'serial-debug-ops assumption', which debug_server.rs restates 14 times, and not by the queue's ordering. The CLI MCP surface inside the GUI (mcp_tool_call_evaluation) does go through the queue, so the GUI has three front doors with two scheduling rules. The per-handler symptoms are already filed (handle_set_fea_case h10 for baseline ordering, debug_write_tool_routing_tests h10 for INV-GUI-2). This finding is the axis behind them.
findings.proposal: Route debug-server writes through EvalRequest::edit / evaluation, as mcp_tool_call_evaluation already does, so the queue is the single scheduling and publication mechanism. The debug server then awaits the ticket's published state instead of keeping its own baseline.

findings.statement:
The build-scheduler axis has a single source, BuildScheduler::from_env, read once at Engine construction (engine_admin.rs:279). Its effect is not given one mechanism. demand_scoped_unified_pass encodes LegacyMultiPass as `None` in an Option<UnifiedPassResult>, and that same `None` also means 'no eval_state'. Each build surface then tests the Option inline:

- build_with_geometry_output: 4 sites (4363 realization_read_cells, 4518 BuildStep walk, 4805 post-process gate, 754 cycle detection).
- tessellate_realizations: 2 sites.
- tessellate_snapshot: 2 sites.
- The constraint re-check compares the enum directly (5178).
- build_snapshot: 0 sites. It never consults the schedule.
- distance_between_placed: 0 sites.

The legacy arm was introduced as a 'one-release kill-switch' when the default flipped on 2026-06-23 (2a7c699849, task #4362). It is still live 110 days later with no retirement cite, and its survival is pinned by 26 files outside engine_fixpoint.rs, including the differential harnesses under reify-eval/tests/harness_cache. The canonical build_with_geometry_output h11 counts the per-surface knob axes in general; this finding is the scheduler axis's encoding and lifetime.
findings.proposal: Either retire LegacyMultiPass, as its one-release promise intended, and make the schedule non-optional, or give the scheduler one strategy value that each surface asks for its BuildStep sequence, separate from the 'no eval state' case.

findings.statement:
The debug/release profile axis in verify.sh has no profile record. Every per-profile fact is a pair of global variables suffixed _DEBUG/_RELEASE, and an inline `[ "$x" = "release" ]` selects between them. There are 5 such selections in 3 functions: confirm_failed_run 1468, emit_nextest_pass 3312/3357/3433, and add_test_passes 3642. The pairs are _CONFIRM_MANIFEST, _CONFIRM_SIDECAR, REIFY_VERIFY_RETRY_NEXTEST_FILTER_FILE, _RETRY_NEXTEST_*_APPLIED and _VERIFY_TEST_TIMEOUT, together with their REIFY_VERIFY_*_{DEBUG,RELEASE} env overrides.

emit_nextest_pass does not receive the profile at all. It receives the cargo flag string `rel` (" --release" or "") and recovers the profile twice by pattern match: `case "$rel" in *release*)` at 3301 and 3431.

The profile is also not independent of the role axis. When --profile is not given, DF_VERIFY_ROLE picks the profile (887-893), and per-role walls are applied inside the release branch. The canonical add_test_passes h11 counts one duplicated confirm-path selection; this finding is the whole profile axis.
findings.proposal: Pass the profile name explicitly to emit_nextest_pass, and derive the cargo flag, manifest, sidecar, retry filter and wall from one profile table (an associative array keyed by profile) that every consumer reads.

findings.statement:
There is no single engine-configuration value. Each knob has its own source, and each front end assembles its own posture.

Inside reify-eval, knobs are read from the process environment at different moments:
- REIFY_BUILD_SCHEDULER, once in the with_prelude constructor (engine_admin 279).
- REIFY_WARM_STATE_BUDGET_BYTES, in the constructor (340), or merged with a manifest [warm_state] value by set_warm_pool_budget_from_manifest (2651).
- REIFY_LONG_CHAIN_THRESHOLD_MS, re-read at each of 4 build entry points (engine_build 3583, 4450, 5788, 6748).
- PATH, re-read per fdm_slice dispatch.

The manifest route (kernel pins, warm_state) is never taken in production (canonical tooling reify-config Manifest h1).

The persistent cache, compute trampolines, repr-tol capture and the openvdb kernel are instead opted into by setter calls at each of 17 front-end construction sites, and the mix differs:
- **CLI main** (9 constructions): sets the persistent cache dir 3 times and repr/openvdb capture at 6 call sites.
- **CLI MCP**: sets the persistent cache but registers no compute fns.
- **LSP** (4 constructions): none of these.
- **GUI** (3 constructions): registers compute fns and ensures openvdb, but never calls set_persistent_cache_dir.

The GUI does run a startup sweep of a cache dir it resolves itself, and its resolver inputs differ from the CLI's. gui engine.rs::bootstrap_persistent_cache_sweep passes user_config: None and project_config: None, while reify-cli cache.rs::resolve_cache_root_layered loads ~/.config/reify/config.toml and the project config. The GUI therefore sweeps a different directory than the CLI writes whenever a config file sets the cache dir. The canonical findings mcp_context ensure_engine h10 and cmd_check h3 are two cells of this matrix.
findings.proposal: Introduce an EngineConfig resolved once (env + manifest + front-end overrides), passed to one constructor, and a small set of named postures (batch-CLI, interactive-GUI, LSP-analysis) that front ends select. That way the persistent cache, compute registration and kernel set become fields rather than setter calls.

findings.statement:
The solver execution-mode axis has a declared single policy seam, resolve_execution_modes. Per its doc, it is "the single policy seam for PRD task #16 / #18" and covers determinism, thread count and the PARALLEL_DOF_THRESHOLD tiny-problem rule. It returns a pair of byte-for-byte mirror enums, AssemblyMode and SolverMode.

It has exactly one production caller, compute_targets/elastic_static.rs:3144. Every other assemble/solve path hard-codes AssemblyMode::Deterministic / SolverMode::Deterministic inline: buckling_kernel (6), assembly/global (5), boundary/dirichlet (2), membrane_load (2), tensegrity_load (2), shell_solve (2), reify-mesh-morph elasticity (2) and reify-eval modal_ops (1). So the determinism/parallelism axis is a choice for one compute target and a constant for the others. Two enums carry one fact and are kept in lockstep only by returning them as a pair.
findings.proposal: Fold the two enums into one ExecutionMode and make every assemble/solve entry take it, so callers obtain it from resolve_execution_modes, or from a Deterministic constant named as such at the trampoline layer.

findings.statement:
The pre-done gate's fail-open/fail-closed posture is split across two layers, with two knobs of opposite polarity and different defaults:
- REIFY_AUDIT_FRESHNESS_STRICT in scripts/reify-audit-freshness.sh defaults to fail-open. It runs a stale binary unless set to 1.
- REIFY_AUDIT_PREDONE_WARN_ONLY, read with std::env::var inside the detector by p5_phantom_done::pre_done_refusal_severity, defaults to refuse (High). It downgrades to Low when set to 1.

The detector reads its knob from the ambient environment rather than through AuditContext, so the CLI's --pattern/--pre-done surface cannot see or report it. The deploy script (deploy-reify-audit-predone-hook.sh) documents only the STRICT knob in its probe messages. The repo already has a single posture primitive for the same enforce/bypass question in hooks: hooks/main-gate-lib.sh::gate_switch_on, which reads env, then git config, then a flag file, and serves 4 knobs. Neither pre-done knob uses it.
findings.proposal: Carry a single pre-done posture (strict | fail-open | warn-only) into AuditContext from the bin, and have the freshness wrapper pass it through. Alternatively, source both from one gate_switch_on-style resolver, so the effective posture is printed once per run.
findings.change_note: weakened: pre_done_refusal_severity still reads REIFY_AUDIT_PREDONE_WARN_ONLY via std::env::var (p5_phantom_done.rs:1111-1117). The review-all weakened verdict stands. Owned by ι #8815, pending.

findings.statement:
Engine::check's verdicts for three constraint families depend on which other public Engine calls ran before it, not on its arguments.

Three check-time passes read Engine side tables that only other public surfaces populate:
- dispatch_constraints reads achieved_repr_tol. That table is written only by tessellate_realizations or tessellate_snapshot, and only after set_capture_repr_tol(true). An empty table turns every RepresentationWithin into Indeterminate.
- measure_dfm_rules and measure_gdt_conformance inject kernel handles from realization_handles. That table is written only by the Build/BuildSnapshot surfaces and cleared only at the next Build entry.

check's rustdoc states the required sequence: callers 'must call set_capture_repr_tol(true) followed by tessellate_realizations(&compiled) before calling check()', and DFM needs a subject 'realized by a prior build() call'. The sequence is spelled at exactly 1 of the 6 non-test check() call sites: reify-cli cmd_check's no-purpose arm (main.rs 907-918). The other five silently get Indeterminate or no DFM/GD&T measurement: the CLI --purpose arm, reify-lsp analysis.rs and diagnostics.rs, GUI EngineSession::check_with_solve_slot, and GUI preview.

In the GUI, check runs before that reload's tessellate_snapshot. It also runs right after reset_geometry_for_reload, which resets the kernels and the realization cache but not realization_handles. So check-time DFM/GD&T can only see handles left by an earlier export build, which now dangle (InvalidReference → Indeterminate, thanks to OCCT's monotonic ids). reset_geometry_for_reload's own contract ('exactly once per whole-file reload … never on a slider edit') is kept only by its single GUI call placement (engine.rs 1556).
findings.proposal: Make the measurement an input. Either have check take (or build itself, behind a flag) a MeasurementContext holding achieved_repr_tol and the realization→handle map produced by an explicit realize/tessellate step, or expose a single check_with_geometry(module, CheckGeometry) entry that runs realize → tessellate → check in one call. Then the CLI, LSP and GUI choose a posture instead of a call order. Clear realization_handles in reset_geometry_for_reload, or make it part of the same per-build reset.

findings.statement: Engine::trace_undef_causes joins two inputs that different calls keep current: self.undef_causes(), the origin map, and the current snapshot. The origin map is written only inside a cold eval() (engine_eval.rs:6894, gated on the capture_undef_causes toggle set by the caller beforehand), and engine_edit.rs contains 0 references to last_undef_causes or capture_undef_causes. The snapshot is advanced by eval and by every edit path. After any edit_param, edit_source or edit_check, the walk therefore runs the new snapshot's undef cells against origins classified for the previous cold eval. The GUI hits exactly this path. EngineSession sets set_capture_undef_causes(true) at construction (engine.rs:1192). Each slider tick then runs preview_parameter → edit_check → build_gui_state → build_values, which calls trace_undef_causes for every Undef cell (engine.rs:5247) and renders 'undef because …'. A cell that became Undef because of the edit gets the cause recorded for the pre-edit state, or none.
findings.proposal: Return the undef-origin map on EvalResult (and from edit_param/edit_source, re-classified over the edited cone), or store it inside EvaluationState next to the snapshot it was classified from, so it is replaced atomically with that snapshot. trace_undef_causes then reads one coherent state. The capture toggle becomes a parameter of the eval call instead of a prior setter.

findings.statement:
Several per-call outputs of Engine operations are not returned. They are left in long-lived Engine fields, read afterwards through last_* getters, or reconstructed by the consumer.

EvalResult, BuildResult and TessellateResult carry none of the dispatch attribution, the eval set, the demand-prune measurement or the set of realizations dispatched this pass.

The GUI reads them after the call at 6 sites:
- last_dispatch_count_by_realization at commands.rs 400 and 579. The 400 site is named `_post_refresh` with a comment that the suffix is 'load-bearing', because build_gui_state has already re-run tessellate and overwritten the tally.
- last_eval_set at commands.rs 587.
- last_demand_prune_measurement at engine.rs 1382 and 4276.
- last_substantive_value at engine.rs 5225.

last_demand_prune_measurement is written only by edit_param (engine_edit.rs:2989) and cleared nowhere. eval() resets last_eval_set (engine_eval.rs:6929) but not this field. So after a slider edit followed by a whole-file reload, which goes through check → eval on the same long-lived engine, build_gui_state surfaces the previous edit's prune record as current.

Where no getter exists, the GUI rebuilds the fact. surface_geometry_derived_cells derives 'which realizations ran this pass' by string-parsing mesh entity_path keys (parse_realization_key) as a proxy. Its own comment records the case where the proxy replays a stale value as Final, and says closing it 'needs reify-eval to report the dispatched-realization set on TessellateResult directly'.
findings.proposal: Return these as fields on the operation's result: dispatch_by_realization and dispatched_realizations on TessellateResult/BuildResult, and eval_set and demand_prune on the edit and eval results. Retire the last_* getters, or keep them only behind test-instrumentation. The GUI then builds its DTOs from the value its own call returned, and the mesh-key proxy is deleted.

findings.statement:
The per-lane mutex protocol has no single owner. The protocol is: the lock file is <lane_dir>.lock, exclusive for a reseed or reclaim, shared for a liveness probe, and a fixed FD.

How each script restates it:
- seed-warm-lane.sh: derives the path at line 930, uses FD 9, and has three wait modes.
- thin-warm-lane.sh: line 384, FD 9, -n.
- warm-lane-gc.sh: lines 594 and 766, FD 8, -n.
- warm-lane-lock-guard.sh: line 197, shared probe by path.
- warm-lane-audit.sh: line 1336, _probe_live by path.
- dark-factory's _seed_warm_lane also opens it.

scripts/lib_lane_x_flock.sh shows the repo already uses a library shape for a different lock, but the lane lock has none.

The production path is a cross-repo temporal handshake. DF takes its own outer flock and then runs seed-warm-lane.sh --assume-lane-lock-held on both pool acquires, according to seed's comment at 919-925. In that mode seed skips its acquire entirely and performs 0 checks that the lock is held. Seed's exclusivity invariant (§9.5 inv.2/inv.11) therefore rests on the caller having performed a prior step that seed cannot observe.

The restatements have already disagreed on the base directory: lock-guard and audit derive <REIFY_WARM_LANE_MOUNT>/<lane>.lock, while seed and thin use the lane path under <mount>/worktrees (existing finding scripts/warm-lane-lock-guard.sh|h1).
findings.proposal: Give the lane lock a sourced library, lib_lane_lock.sh, mirroring lib_lane_x_flock.sh. It should own lane_lock_path(lane_dir), lane_lock_acquire(mode, wait) on one FD, lane_lock_probe and lane_lock_assert_held. lane_lock_assert_held does a non-blocking probe on a fresh FD that must report contended. --assume-lane-lock-held then calls that assertion, so the cross-repo handshake is verified at use.
findings.change_note: weakened: The skeptic's weakened verdict stands. The only seed change since review-all is the 3fc64b646e seed-stamp tail and prose. The lock derivation, the FD-9 acquire, and the zero-check --assume-lane-lock-held arm (parser at 400) are unchanged. lib_lane_lock.sh still defines only lane_lock_probe. Owned by #8624.

findings.statement:
The INV-GEO-1 mesh-contract posture (Enforce/Warn) has two homes with different sources, and only one of them is reachable through the Engine.

Engine home: Engine reads MeshContractMode::from_env() at construction (engine_admin.rs:285), exposes pub set_mesh_contract_mode, and threads the value explicitly through RealizationOpsInput to the eval-side conversion handoff (engine_build.rs 3588/4455/5793/6299/12490 → 8461).

Manifold home: the Manifold kernel's ingest ignores all of that. It reads its own process-global `static MODE: OnceLock<MeshContractMode>` from the same env var on first use. The GeometryKernel trait carries no mode parameter.

The two agree only while the env var is the sole input. An Engine configured with set_mesh_contract_mode(Warn), which today only mesh_contract_handoff_diagnostic.rs does, warns at the eval handoff while Manifold ingest still enforces whatever the process env said when the first mesh was ingested.
findings.proposal: Pass the posture to the kernel. Either add it to the ingest call (or to a per-operation options struct the Engine already threads), or have Engine push it at registration through a kernel configuration method. Delete the kernel-local OnceLock so MeshContractMode::from_env has one caller.

findings.statement:
The snapshot-reading entry points check_snapshot, build_snapshot and tessellate_snapshot take a &CompiledModule. They combine its templates with whatever EvaluationState the previous eval, edit_param or edit_source left. Snapshot records no identity for the module it was built from: its fields are id, version, graph, values, topology_fingerprint, provenance and forall_emitted, with no content hash. topology_fingerprint is computed, but none of the three entry points compares it, so the pairing of module and snapshot is purely temporal.

The consumers compensate on their side. reify-lsp keeps its own mirror, EvalState.last_content_hash, beside the engine. Its diagnostics.rs carries a debug-only warning for the case where 'last_content_hash was set without a preceding eval()', and then forces a cold start. The GUI keeps compiled and engine paired inside EngineSession::core to call tessellate_snapshot.
findings.proposal: Record the source module's content_hash in Snapshot or EvaluationState at eval. Have each *_snapshot entry point return an error (or None with a diagnostic) on a mismatch, then delete the LSP mirror.

findings.statement:
compose_morph returns its outcome (Result<VolumeMesh, MorphFailure>) and also records the outcome kind into process-global AtomicU64 COUNTERS: 4 record_* calls (lib.rs 264, 298, 318, 331). Every consumer of morph outcomes reads the globals rather than any per-build value:
- reify-cli prints diagnostics::format_summary(&snapshot()) after builds (main.rs 1622, 1746).
- The GUI debug RPC handle_mesh_morph_stats resets and snapshots them. Its doc concedes that a concurrent recorder can make a post-reset snapshot non-zero.
- reify-eval/tests/morph_arm_e2e.rs asserts on them.

Because the counters are shared across every engine and thread in the process, the tests serialize through 3 independent locks: the mesh-morph crate's TEST_LOCK, morph_arm_e2e's MORPH_DIAG_LOCK, and debug_server's TEST_LOCK. reset_for_test is exported cross-crate behind a 'testing' feature with G-allow justifications.
findings.proposal: Have the Engine's morph producer aggregate the outcome compose_morph already returns into a per-build tally on the build or tessellate result. Keep the process counters only as a telemetry sink, not as the consumer interface. Cross-crate tests then assert on returned values and need no lock.

findings.statement: EvalContext is an optional-capability builder where every missing capability degrades silently: missing determinacy -> silent Undef, missing diagnostics sink -> warnings dropped; the 'MUST keep .with_determinacy and .with_runtime_diagnostics' invariant was enforced by a doc comment. INV-EVAL-2 proposed a required-args constructor (CellEvalCtx).

59 impl GeometryKernel existed (5 real, ~45 bespoke test mocks) while real-output cross-kernel tests numbered exactly two files; real-vs-mock divergence was architecturally induced. reify-kernel-conformance now exists (916 lines) — verify it instantiates one shared contract suite for real AND stub kernels and how many bespoke mocks remain.

Two structurally disjoint invalidation walks existed: the freshness-unaware dirty cone and propagate_freshness_only, built for async compute completions and never called in production, so an async completion never invalidated dependents; Freshness::default() = Final made an absent cache entry read as authoritative. The briefing lists gating.rs Phase-A hooks as retained dead code awaiting #5023 — verify whether the dead walk was wired, deleted, or is still a retained parity obligation.

Cache-write and diagnostic emission were decoupled by API shape (record_evaluation took no diagnostics; NodeCache held none), so the 2259/2267 fix was convention+tests and a new per-cell-branch diagnostic would silently regress on a cache hit. INV-EVAL-3 proposed diagnostics stored in the cache entry and a shared post-pass detector registry.

Every subsystem showed the same shape: a correct helper is extracted and adopted at 3 of N sites, leaving N-3 inline copies that drift (cell_eval_ctx 4/72, journal helper 5/56, emit quintet 5/6, signatures_common half-finished dedup). The systemic cost is that an extraction without an adoption sweep plus a guard against new inline copies does not remove the next-change cost; it adds a second convention.

findings.statement: Key scenario 'The Claude chat panel drives the sidecar … under landlock' breaks on heuristic 7 (temporal coupling): which directory the sidecar may write is decided by whichever design was open when the FIRST chat message was sent. Path: claude_send_message recomputes the landlock workspace on every message with claude_bridge::resolve_workspace_dir. Its inputs are context.current_file, then AppState.initial_file, then cwd. The result is captured only in the spawn closure passed to ensure_sidecar_ready. ensure_sidecar_ready's Phase-1 fast path returns Ok(()) as soon as the slot holds a Ready handle, without comparing workspaces, so the closure never runs again. REIFY_WORKSPACE (sidecar index.ts: 'parent dir of the active editor file at sidecar-spawn time') therefore stays fixed for the sidecar's lifetime. After the user opens a design in another directory, through open_file_engine (which never updates AppState.initial_file; only the argv load sets it), the claude CLI keeps --writable on the OLD directory, and its edits to the newly open design are refused by landlock. The per-message resolve_workspace_dir result is a transient value whose effect is pinned to the first call (heuristic 5). No test covers a workspace change after spawn: claude_bridge_tests' workspace_resolution tests the pure resolver only.
findings.proposal: Key the sidecar on its workspace: respawn the sidecar, or send it a workspace-change message, when the resolved workspace differs from the one it was spawned with. Or state in the briefing and the sidecar contract that the workspace is pinned per session, and give the UI a signal for it.

findings.statement: The host-side half of the deleted in-process tool interception (gui-state-sync L8) is still in the code, and its names lie (heuristic 1). InboundMessage::ToolResult ('Tool result sent back to the sidecar after in-process MCP tool execution') has no production producer: `git grep InboundMessage::ToolResult` finds it constructed only in tests/claude_bridge_tests.rs:1767. Yet the sidecar keeps a whole consumer path for it: ipc.ts validates 'tool_result' inbound; session.ts handleToolResult, the pendingToolUseIds FIFO fallback, and the stdin kept open 'so tool_result blocks can follow'. The Rust side also keeps OutboundMessage::ToolCall.tool_use_id 'enabling id-based correlation' and warn_if_stale_tool_call, which warns about a correlation fallback that no host reply exercises. Names still describe the removed feature: `McpConfig` holds only an event emitter; `SidecarHandle::from_parts_with_mcp` means 'with emitter'; the SharedStdin alias doc says 'so the reader task can write back tool results', which the reader never does. Two languages carry a protocol arm with no producer, and a reader of either side will take it for a live path (heuristic 6, no single purpose).

If ai-native-editing ever reintroduces host tool results, it re-adds them with a producer.

findings.statement: The #7816 confinement of AI write targets is checked separately from the write, and the window between them is unbounded. confined_write_target resolves the target with no lock held. The write happens later inside the seam's run_on_engine closure, which first waits for the engine lock, and that wait can last a whole queued evaluation. For reify_save_file the write is crate::commands::save_file_impl (std::fs::write), which follows a symlink at the resolved path. For reify_export it is the kernel exporter, opening the path. So a symlink created at a not-yet-existing confined path, or a directory swapped for one, during that wait redirects the write outside the design directory. The sidecar's claude CLI can write inside the design directory (it is the landlock workspace), so the requester itself can create that symlink. docs/debug-mcp-contract.md states this residual ('a directory swapped for a symlink between them can redirect the write'), but no task owns it: search_tasks finds only #8471 (screenshot save_path), and briefing known_gaps does not list it. The invariant is therefore enforced at check time only, not at use (heuristic 10, redundantly), and the residual is documented but has no owner, against the umbrella principle 'nothing-vacuous-and-unowned'.
findings.proposal: Re-check at use: open the resolved target with O_NOFOLLOW (or write to a temp file in the confined directory and renameat into it), then fstat-compare against the design directory. Or file a task that owns the documented residual.

The seam then runs build_gui_state under the engine lock before the write, which task #8074 measured at about 8 s on a large design, so the window is long. save_file_impl is a bare std::fs::writ | seat verification: Read write_confinement.rs fully, the #7816 diff to debug_server.rs, save_file_impl, and the contract section. The race was not reproduced.

findings.statement: Follow-up work in this slice is recorded as curator-ticket ids (`tkt_…`) in production prose instead of `#NNNN` task cites. findings.statement: Under heuristic 11 (SPOT), reify-config's persistent-cache resolver is pure: the precedence lives in resolve_cache. Turning the process environment and config files into CacheResolverInputs, though, is written by each caller, and the two production callers disagree. reify-cli cache.rs::resolve_cache_root_layered and resolve_cache_root_with_cli read REIFY_CACHE_DIR, REIFY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES, XDG_CACHE_HOME and HOME, and load `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME|~/.config/reify/config.toml` plus `<cwd>/.reify/config.toml`. gui/src-tauri engine.rs::bootstrap_persistent_cache_sweep reads the same four env vars but passes user_config: None and project_config: None. Its doc nonetheless claims it 'mirrors reify-cli's resolve_cache_root pipeline'. With `[cache] dir` set in the user config, the CLI caches in that directory while the GUI sweeps `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/reify/fea`. The next change, pending #6799 (DC-rho: the GUI installs the FEA persistent cache it sweeps), is premised on 'it already calls the shared config-crate resolver, which is the same pipeline'. Implemented as written, it would point GUI engines at a different cache from the CLI's. The CLI side carries two more heuristic-1/10 costs. First, resolve_cache_root's doc says 'Config-file layers are deliberately not plumbed in', yet it delegates to resolve_cache_root_with_cli(None), which loads both files. Second, a malformed config file is something parse_cache_config treats as a loud hard error (CacheError::EmptyDir: 'a TOML file entry is always intentional'). In configured_eval_engine and mcp_context ensure_engine, that error silently disables the persistent cache with only a tracing::debug line.
findings.proposal: Give reify-config one `CacheResolverInputs::from_process` (or `resolve_cache_from_env(cli_dir)`) that owns the env reads and config-file discovery. Have the CLI and GUI call it, and correct #6799's premise before it lands.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 (invariants enforced) and heuristic 1 (informative names). The refresh guard is the only reify-side enforcement of §9.5 inv.9: only the _merge-verify lane's clean landed-commit target/ may advance the shared base. It never checks that the commit has landed, and it never checks which lane is advancing. The guard checks four things: the advancing dir is inside a worktree (259), `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is empty (265), --landed-commit is non-empty (287), and `git rev-parse HEAD` == --landed-commit (294). No `merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> refs/heads/main` and no lane-identity test exists anywhere in the script. Every caller derives the flag from the advancing worktree's own HEAD: dark-factory GitOps.refresh_warm_base ('derived from git rev-parse HEAD in the _merge-verify worktree'), ensure-warm-base.sh:209 (_r2_head), and seed-warm-base-initial.sh:253-255. The refusal hint at 289 tells an operator to pass `--landed-commit $(git -C <lane_worktree> rev-parse HEAD)`. The 'landed' assertion therefore reduces to HEAD==HEAD. A clean task lane holding committed but unlanded work passes, and the guard promotes it. Dark-factory's docstring calls this guard 'defense-in-depth', and the PRD names it as inv.9's enforcement. The commit-cleanliness half is real; the 'landed' half that the flag's name promises is not checked.
findings.proposal: Make the guard check what the flag's name says: refuse unless `git merge-base --is-ancestor $LANDED_COMMIT refs/heads/main`, and fix the hint to name a main commit. At runtime, engine_edit.rs's CompiledForallBody::Connect arm emits every element's compatibility constraint as `CompiledExpr::literal(Value::Bool(true), Type::Bool)`, so the constraint reports Satisfied. findings.statement: Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings. Since c225a44d88 a connect endpoint parses to a typed PortPath {root: Element | Literal{sub, index} | Named, members}. compile_connection then calls resolve_port_name, which flattens it straight back to a String (`PortPath::parse(expr, None)?.port_name()`). Every downstream decision re-parses that string with ad-hoc parsers. own_port_name uses strip_prefix("self.") and contains('.')/contains('['). sub_member_endpoint uses rsplit_once('.') then split_once('['). These two decide own-port vs sub-member, direction lookup, undefined-port and auto-match. The file itself concedes the string is ambiguous: chain_element_sub says it dispatches on elem.kind because the serialized name 'cannot tell a keyed element from a dotted port reference (vents["a.b"])'. Known costs: the phantom un-indexed `vents.outlet` connection (#7659, pending) comes from sub_member_endpoint stripping the indexer and accepting a collection name, a fact the typed root already distinguishes. `self` is parsed as PortRoot::Named("self") and is only folded into the own-port case by the string prefix strip. The planned next change in this area, nested port paths `a.b.port` (assembly-modal-connection-graph α), would render as "a.b.port". sub_member_endpoint would then look up sub "a.b", miss both side maps, and fall into the documented silent-pass absence contract. The directions would go unchecked and no undefined-port error would fire.
findings.proposal: Keep the PortPath through compile_connection. Classify own vs sub-member endpoints from PortRoot (Named("self") folded at parse), look up directions and member names by (root sub, members), and render the String only where CompiledConnection/labels need it. Then #7659's collection-name endpoint becomes a typed check (Named root naming a collection sub with members non-empty).

findings.statement: Key scenario 'gcode_import(file, dialect) ... a Klipper INPUT_SHAPER directive is a warning, not a parse error' breaks at the eval boundary (INV-SF-1 undef-has-provenance; heuristic 10, informatively enforced). lower_gcode collects typed outcomes: a ParseError carrying its line, plus GcodeImportWarning::{ShaperConflict, ArcFlattened, DialectUnsupported}. eval_gcode_import, the only production caller, discards all of them. A parse error becomes a bare Value::Undef with no diagnostic or UndefCause (gcode_import.rs:404-406). An unrecognised dialect becomes an empty List, which looks the same as an empty program. Every warning is dropped (the doc at :377 says 'undeliverable here'). The trajectory family has no diagnose hook; snapshot, orientation, flexure, fea, geometry, stackup, dfm and tolerancing each register one (reify-stdlib lib.rs). So none of the PRD's three codes, E_GcodeParseError, W_GcodeDialectUnsupported and W_GcodeDialectShaperConflict, exists in reify-core or reaches a user: git grep finds no reference outside gcode_import.rs and reify-gcode. The module-wide #![allow(dead_code)] at :39 suppresses the never-read-warning lint that would otherwise flag this. S8's typed-outcome PRD keeps the trajectory family `legacy` (builtin-registry-migration-and-interception-classifier.md D4), and S6 χ covers only TOTS outcomes, so no stream owns this.
findings.proposal: Make lower_gcode's ParseError and warnings coded DiagnosticCodes and emit them from the gcode_import arm, either through a trajectory diagnose hook today or through S8's Evaluated{value, advisories} once the trajectory family converts. A parse error should become a coded rejection. An unsupported dialect should become a coded error, not an empty list.

It calls nominal_fk_chain once and replicates that single pose across every time sample (:550-553). findings.statement: The runtime EndEffectorTrack does not match its .ri declaration field for field (INV-PD-2 result-fields-populated-or-owned; heuristic 12). trajectory.ri:359-366 declares modal_result: ModalResult, nominal_pose and combined_pose: List<List<Pose3>>, and vibration_offset: List<List<Vec3<Length>>>. track_data_to_value writes modal_result and mechanism as the sentinel Value::Real(0.0) (trampoline.rs:583-584). findings.statement: A PiecewisePolynomialProfile whose first waypoint is not at t = 0 is silently mis-evaluated by simulate_trajectory and by input_shape's impulse arm. The precondition 'profiles start at t = 0' is unenforced (heuristic 10): it is stated only in a doc 'Assumptions' paragraph (sampling.rs:115-118, 'for non-zero-origin profiles the caller must adjust'), and no caller adjusts. The splines keep absolute knots: CubicSpline::eval subtracts knots[i], and segment() clamps t <= knots[0] onto segment 0 (spline.rs:174-196). But duration() is the span t_last − t_first (:364-367). to_trajectory_samples samples [0, duration] (sampling.rs:121-167), and input_shape_value resamples [0, duration + Δ] with convolve_at clamping τ into [0, t_domain] (trampoline.rs:796; impulse_shaper.rs:355). With waypoints at t = 2 s and 3 s, both paths evaluate the segment-0 cubic extrapolated backwards over [0, 1] s. They never sample the real motion. The shaped profile is also re-timed to start at 0. trajectory.ri imposes no first-waypoint-at-zero constraint, and nothing reports the problem.
findings.proposal: Either shift by the first knot inside MultiJointSpline (an eval over a [start, end] domain), or reject a non-zero-origin profile with a coded diagnostic at value_to_multijoint_spline. Pin the case with a test that uses t0 = 2 s.

CubicSpline::segment clamps t <= knots[0] to segment 0 and eval uses s = t - knots[i], so a negative s extrapolates backwards. duration() is knots[n-1] - knots[0]. to_trajectory_ | seat verification: Read spline segment/eval/duration, to_trajectory_samples, convolve_at and input_shape_value's impulse arm, and traced the time origin through each. findings.statement: The Euler-convention axis of variation has no typed home in Rust (heuristic 12, structured data; heuristic 11, SPOT; heuristic 3). The .ri declares enum EulerConvention with 12 variants (geometry_traits.ri:162). eval_orientation reads the variant back as a string in two independent 12-arm tables. orient_euler maps the string to an axis triple (orientation.rs:82-95). orient_to_euler re-implements all 12 conventions as hand-written matrix-element formulas, each with its own gimbal-lock branch (:327-460). Both end in `_ => Undef`. A third copy is the test list ALL_CONVENTIONS (:848). Nothing derives the decomposer from the constructor's axis triple, so the two can disagree silently. The history shows that drift: 11fb37b8eb fixed four proper-Euler decomposer arms at their singularities, and #6082 found the enum under-declaring eval by six variants. eval_orientation is one 627-line match over 13 builtins (heuristic 4), with the 180-line decomposer inline.
findings.proposal: Parse the variant once into a Rust EulerConvention enum with an exhaustive axes() method. Have both the constructor and the decomposer dispatch on it, and derive the decomposition generically from the axis triple (Tait-Bryan vs proper). Lift each builtin arm into its own function.

ALL_CONVENTIONS is at :848 and the .ri enum has 12 variants. findings.statement: PRB flexure constructor rejections are silent for every class except one degenerate-geometry check, and that check is enforced by redundant reconstruction (heuristic 10: 'a census that re-derives state ... is the smell'; INV-SF-1). Each family's parser returns Option: parse_beam_inputs, parse_notch_inputs, parse_bending_hinge_inputs, parse_let_inputs, parse_prismatic_inputs, parse_compound_inputs and parse_cartwheel_inputs. Every rejection collapses to Value::Undef with no reason. flexure_diagnose then re-derives the geometry from the raw args through classify_geometry_invalid. That function holds a second copy of every constructor's positional argument layout, keyed by 13 name strings (common.rs:449-479), and a second copy of the t ≥ L / t ≥ 2r rules the parsers already apply (e.g. beam.rs:75). A missing youngs_modulus, a non-positive width or E, a non-unit axis, or a wrong arity stays silent by design (diagnostics.rs:124-137; common.rs:441-443). S8 α2 #8889 moves the flexure advisories with 'byte-identical' signals, so it does not by itself give the silent classes a code.
findings.proposal: Have each parser return Result<Inputs, FlexureInputError>, with one error enum naming the failed field and its value. Have the constructor arm return it as a coded rejection (S8's Rejection) and delete classify_geometry_invalid's layout table.

findings.statement: lower_commands treats M82/M83 (absolute/relative extrusion) as segment splitters only, and always reads E as an absolute coordinate. After an M83, which is common in slicer output, each waypoint's `e` is the per-move delta mislabelled as the absolute extruder position. waypoint_to_value then publishes it as a Length 'absolute coordinate' (gcode_import.rs:114-118, 466-480). The AST already distinguishes the mode: IgnoredMCode keeps code 82/83. The lowering discards that fact, the waypoint record has no field saying which regime `e` is in, and nothing warns.

findings.statement: parse_value accepts any string Rust's f64::from_str accepts, which includes 'inf', 'infinity' and 'NaN' (case-insensitive). So `G1 XNaN Yinf` parses successfully, although the grammar the crate documents is `<letter><number>`. The non-finite value then flows through lower_gcode into waypoint_to_value as a NaN or ±inf Length nested inside a List of Maps. reify-stdlib's sanitize_value checks only the top-level Value (helpers.rs:83-95), so it never cleans it. The crate's round-trip contract (lib.rs:18-22) also fails for NaN, because NaN != NaN under the derived PartialEq. display.rs's rule 3 already scopes itself to 'every finite x'. No test covers non-finite input.
findings.proposal: Reject non-finite values in parse_value as InvalidParameter (`parsed.is_finite()`), and add a parse_errors test.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10, clear invariants uniformly enforced: the invariant 'a merge into main runs the merge gate (--profile both, role=merge)' has two enforcement points that disagree, and the weaker one marks the move as sanctioned. When a hand `git merge <branch>` on main hits conflicts, the user resolves them and runs `git commit`. Git then runs pre-commit, not pre-merge-commit, which per githooks only fires for an automatically created merge commit. pre-commit calls hooks/project-checks, which runs `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra` with DF_VERIFY_ROLE unset, so the role is `task`. verify.sh's MERGE_HEAD defence (the top-level block before `cd "$REPO_ROOT"`) forces only SCOPE=all. PROFILE stays `debug`: --profile was explicit (PROFILE_EXPLICIT=1), and the role-based `both` default fires only for merge/background. As a result the release-only tests that hooks/pre-merge-commit's header says run 'exactly once, at merge' (reify-solver-elastic's #[cfg_attr(debug_assertions, ignore)] buckling/eigensolve tests) never execute. pre-commit then calls main_gate_mark, and hooks/reference-transaction logs 'sanctioned main move'. scripts/land.sh aborts on conflict, and DF's merge worker verifies with role=merge, so neither sanctioned path produces this. But a conflicted hand merge is exactly the class of move the tripwire exists to classify, and it records it as sanctioned after a debug-only gate.
findings.proposal: In verify.sh's MERGE_HEAD block, also force PROFILE=both and the merge role (or refuse a debug profile while MERGE_HEAD is present). Alternatively, have hooks/pre-commit detect MERGE_HEAD and run the pre-merge-commit gate instead of project-checks. In S18 this is one row of the role/scope record (D3/D5).

findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT: _verify_cleanup feeds two run ledgers from one exit, and they derive the run's exit code by different rules. #7424 added _vl_finalize. It deliberately prefers _VL_EXIT_RC, the last plan step's rc, over the trap's $?, 'which the Node-lane EXIT trap resets before calling _verify_cleanup', and it maps INT/TERM/HUP to 130/143/129 from a new trap argument. The adjacent _record_background_verdict still reads the raw $? captured as _exit_rc and ignores the signal argument. So the S18 §2.4 defect 3 (the background sweep ledger records pass/exit_code 0 for failed runs) was worked around for the new ledger only. The two ledgers can now disagree about the same run.
findings.proposal: Compute the run's exit code once in _verify_cleanup (last-step rc, then signal mapping) and pass it to both recorders; or leave it to S18 epsilon's port.

findings.statement: Heuristic 12, structured data instead of meaningful strings. The verify instrumentation ledger, new since review-all (#7424, 1,065 lines), recovers each plan step's kind by substring and regex rules over verify.sh's emitted shell text. findings.statement: Heuristic 11, SPOT: the locale the shared Rust lexer (scripts/lib_rust_production_view.sh, RUST_LEXER_AWK) must run under is part of its correctness, but the lib states no locale contract, and its two Python consumers decide it oppositely. audit-orphan-producers.sh's _run_lexer is 'Deliberately not pinned to LC_ALL=C', because byte mode splits a non-ASCII char literal and its quotes read as lifetimes. assert-module-scc.py's lex_crate pins LC_ALL=C. Measured with gawk on a probe file: under C.UTF-8, `['é','{']` lexes to `['','']`; under LC_ALL=C it lexes to `['é''{']`. The `{` survives into the production view, and so does a `}` after '—'. assert-module-scc.py runs matching_close and INLINE_MOD_RE over exactly that view. There is no live instance today (no non-ASCII char literal sits beside a brace literal in crates/). There are 40 non-ASCII char literals in crates/*/src, so the hazard is latent. Each Python consumer also writes its own awk driver and record protocol around the lexer: \x01/|/\x02 marks versus _FRAME_END frames.
findings.proposal: State the locale in lib_rust_production_view.sh's consumer contract (a UTF-8 locale) and drop assert-module-scc.py's LC_ALL=C pin. Better, give the lib one Python driver (path list in, (code_view, open_state) per file out) that both Python consumers and the incoming S9/S27/S1 ratchets import.

findings.statement: Heuristic 1 / heuristic 11: GeometryQuery::AdjacentFaces and ::SharedEdges carry a face index that means two different things across the trait seam. The trait contract (reify-ir geometry.rs:1856-1860) says `face_index` is the 0-based index into the shape's face enumeration. The only production consumers, selector_vocabulary_v2::adjacent_to_face (:796-845) and geometry_ops' shared-edges helper (:9750-9787), compute it as the position of a handle in extract_faces(parent), then map reply indices back through that same list. Since #4262, ManifoldKernel::extract_faces returns coalesced planar faces (6 for a cube), while Manifold's AdjacentFaces/SharedEdges arms interpret the index as a raw mesh triangle (0..12) and return triangle indices (kernel.rs ~588-640; queries.rs module doc :29-35 states the two spaces are 'disjoint'). On a Manifold-owned parent, adjacent_to_face therefore asks about the wrong triangle and maps triangle ids back as planar-face positions. findings.statement:
Two implementations map a fused-memory task record to TaskMetadata (heuristic 11, SPOT), and the production callers use the one the bin labels test-only (heuristic 1).
- The Rust live loader: load_tasks_from_fused_memory → FusedMemoryClient::get_task/get_tasks → task_metadata_from_wire.
- The jq sidecar scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq, fed through `--tasks-file`.
- Both production callers use the jq path: the /audit skill and the dark-factory pre-done hook wrapper. The bin's usage calls `--tasks-file` 'for tests' and the live loader 'production'.

The two adapters disagree:
- **Subtasks:** the Rust loader requests `with_subtasks: true` and flattens subtasks (collect_tasks_recursive). The wrapper and skill call get_tasks without it, and jq maps only top-level `.tasks`, so subtasks are never audited and a pre-done flip of a subtask finds no row (check_pre_done returns [] and the flip is allowed).
- **Per-row tolerance:** Rust defaults a missing title to "" and drops a malformed done_provenance per row. In the jq path TaskMetadata.title is a non-defaulted String and serde decodes the whole file, so one null title or malformed row fails the snapshot. The wrapper then exits 125 and every done-flip in the project is blocked.
- **done_at:** jq prefers .metadata.done_at; the Rust loader reads only updatedAt.
- **Pre-done cost:** the Rust pre-done path is a deliberate O(1) get_task. The wrapper pulls the whole corpus with get_tasks inside fused-memory's write lock.

The wrapper's header premise, 'reify-audit is a pure-logic library (no MCP client...)', is false: the bin has had a live client since #3736.
findings.proposal: Pick one adapter. Either the wrapper and skill call the bin's live loader (drop --tasks-file from production, keeping it for fixtures), or the Rust loader is deleted and the jq contract is made total per row. Whichever survives owns subtask flattening, per-row tolerance and the done_at tiers.

- Only pdoccover-baseline-gen and plinecite-baseline-gen use the driver.
- ptodo-baseline-gen and pdiag-baseline-gen hand-roll argv. They accept a bare positional project root, which the driver deliberately refuses ('a stray positional is refused ... never silently taken as a different tree'). They emit only to stdout, with a documented `> baseline.txt` redirect recipe, and each has its own exit-code contract. ptodo-baseline-gen's `--help` exits 0 under that redirect, the hazard pdiag-baseline-gen and the driver both document guarding against.

- Pending task #8925 ('Move pdoccover-baseline-gen onto the shared driver') is already satisfied on main by #6935's amend 651128f46b, so it is stale.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 (SPOT): one chat turn gets its id from two independent minters that are never reconciled, so the chat panel cannot correlate any lifecycle event with its assistant message. claudeStore.sendMessage mints `msg-${Date.now()}-${n}` (generateId, claudeStore.ts:80) and sets it as currentMessageId and as the assistant message id. App's onSend handler then discards it (`onSend: (_id, text, context) => claudeSendMessage(text, context)`, App.tsx:465). bridge.claudeSendMessage returns Promise<void> and drops the id that the Rust command returns (bridge.ts:323). Rust claude_bridge.rs send_message mints its own `msg-{n}` from MSG_COUNTER, writes it to the sidecar and returns it (claude_bridge.rs:581-596). The sidecar echoes that id on every outbound event, and outbound_to_event re-emits it unchanged. In claudeStore.handleOutboundMessage, text_delta and thinking_delta append to state.currentMessageId, so reply text renders. tool_call, tool_result, done and error all look up findAssistantIdx(msg.id) (claudeStore.ts:173, 195, 218, 254), which can never match, so each breaks out early. As a result: no tool-call card is ever added (MessageGroup renders props.message.toolCalls); `complete` and `thinkingComplete` are never set, so MessageGroup's streaming={!props.message.complete} stays true for every finished reply; and an error is never attached to its turn. This breaks the briefing key scenario 'The Claude chat panel drives the sidecar'. It is separate from the permission-envelope defect the S26 PRD found (alpha #9062). Neither the S25 nor the S26 PRD mentions it. The tests mask it: ChatPanel.test.tsx:114-116 and claudeIntegration.test.ts:81-86 feed store.state.currentMessageId back in as the event id, an id the real producer never sends.
findings.proposal: Make one side the id minter. Either the store passes its id through claude_send_message (the Rust command accepts the id and forwards it), or the store takes the id that claudeSendMessage returns, under the S26 bridge port. Then add one test that drives the real bridge mapping with a producer-shaped id, not the store's own id.

findings.statement: Heuristic 11 (SPOT) and heuristic 10 (uniform enforcement): the editor has no single rule for document identity across the two spellings of one file. Editor's own versionKey comment (Editor.tsx:95-105) records that store paths are decoded while every URI the backend mints is percent-encoded by the url crate, and only the version counters canonicalize (versionKey = pathToUri(canonicalizeKey(...))). pathToUri does not encode, so currentUri for '/p/hello world.ri' is 'file:///p/hello world.ri'. Two other identity checks compare raw strings. (1) The LSP diagnostics listener drops every event where `event.uri !== currentUri` (Editor.tsx:685). TauriNotificationSink.publish_diagnostics emits `uri.as_str()` of the server's parsed Url (main.rs:99-109), so a file whose path has a space or non-ASCII character never shows LSP diagnostics. (2) applyWorkspaceEditAcrossFiles routes an edit to the live view only if `uri === activeUri` (rename.ts:204), where activeUri is the decoded currentUri. A fresh F2 rename in such a file therefore fails that test. isOpen(canonicalizeKey(uri)) returns true, so the edit goes to applyOpenInactive on the ACTIVE file (Editor.tsx:395-419). That sink applies the edits to the store's file.content, which the Mod-s branch's own comment says is stale once the user types, writes it to disk with saveFile, and calls updateFileContent. The store-sync effect then replaces the whole view buffer with a sync.external transaction. Any unsaved typing is discarded, and the rename lands on the pre-typing text. Editor.test.tsx covers the spaced spelling only for the stale-refusal path (2433-2489) and the inactive-buffer path (2491-2542). It has no fresh-rename-on-active or encoded-diagnostics case.

findings.statement: Heuristic 6 (well-defined purpose) and heuristic 9 (deep modules): the client half of the LSP document lifecycle has no module of its own. It lives as closure locals of the Editor component: docVersions, versionKey, currentUri, fileOpsPromise, lspDebounceTimer, destroyed, sendDidChange, flushPendingLspChange and onceServerIsCurrent. Those locals are mutated from onMount (lines 218-705, a 488-line closure), three createEffects, the keymap, the rename sinks and onCleanup. The same component also builds the rename overlay DOM, the three WorkspaceEdit disk/store/LSP sinks, the two-channel diagnostics merge, the save keymap, nav history, and the store→view content sync. 322 of 943 lines are comments, many explaining ordering between those effects (comments stance). The cost is measured: in the last 3 days #7510/#7512 landed 12 commits here, and they left three pending point-fix follow-ups in this same lifecycle: #8596 (rename re-issues at stale coordinates), #8603 (a didChange can precede initialize/didOpen because sendDidChange is not chained on fileOpsPromise), and #8604 (didClose sent for documents never opened). The URI-spelling defect recorded separately here is a fourth. Each follow-up has to reason about the whole closure because the ordering invariant (open→changes→close per URI, one version sequence) has no owner that enforces it.
findings.proposal: Extract an LSP document session (for example editor/lspDocumentSession.ts) that owns open/change/close ordering, per-document versions under one key function, and flush-before-request. Editor then calls open(uri,text), change(uri,text), close(uri), syncForRequest() and keeps only the view wiring. Move the rename overlay and the WorkspaceEdit sinks into their own modules beside rename.ts. #8603 and #8604 then become invariants of that module rather than separate patches.

Nothing in the repo can force them to run. run_orphan_audit collapses EnvUnavailable into `None`. EnvUnavailable covers python3 or git missing, the script missing (`scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh not found at …`), and a repo_root outside a work tree. Callers return early on `None`. Four pin files say the authoritative lane 'MUST set REIFY_REQUIRE_ORPHAN_AUDIT=1' to turn that skip into a failure, but no script, hook or orchestrator config sets it (git grep: reads only, in reify-audit tests; none in scripts/, hooks/ or dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml, and none in dark-factory). findings.statement: The Selector branch of the modal location resolver cannot fire in production, and the drop is silent (INV-SF-3, declared-intent-consumed-or-diagnosed). The branch serves displacement_at and StepForce.at. It reads ModalResult.topology through carried_topology_from_result. Every production writer of that field gets it from build_modal_topology_value (modal_ops.rs:1289), which returns Value::Undef unconditionally, or writes a literal Undef (degenerate_modal_result). So in production a `Value::Selector` location always takes the 'honest fallback' and resolves to the global fundamental antinode. That path deliberately emits no diagnostic and no warning ('stays quiet'), so an author who asks for the response at a face gets the response at a different node with nothing reported. Heuristic 1 (informative names): the function's doc says it reads 'the CarriedTopology the BUILD path baked into the echoed modal_result', but no build path bakes one. The 'capability flip' test, r3b_modal_selector_displacement.rs, never runs the producer. It hand-builds a ModalResult with a populated topology through from_realized_mesh and calls displacement_at_trampoline directly, so it masks the gap (Tests stance). from_realized_mesh has no production caller. build_modal_topology_value's own deferral cites done #4654 ('Real population deferred to R3b follow-up per task 4654 design decision'). #7097 owns populating .topology on the body overload only. Its ratified scope says the dims overload's honest form 'stays the C2′ degraded/Undef one', so a Selector on the dims modal path will keep falling back silently even after #7097 lands. S13's PRD lists resolve_location_value as a 'consumer on main today' of the carried-topology resolver, but only tests reach that consumer.
findings.proposal: When the location is a Selector and the result carries no topology, emit a coded Warning naming the selector and saying it resolved to the fundamental antinode, instead of falling back silently. findings.statement: solve_load_cases (solver::multi_case) discards every per-case structured detail that its elastic_static sub-solves emit. findings.statement: The FDM compute targets turn malformed or missing declared inputs into silent results, against INV-SF-3 (declared intent consumed or diagnosed), INV-SF-1 (undef has provenance) and the briefing's 'errors must be noisy' convention. (1) as_printed_material_r_fast_trampoline and as_printed_material_r0_trampoline map any failure in their `?`-chained readers to `degraded_field()` with `diagnostics: Vec::new()`. Those failures are: a missing FDMProcess field (walls, top_bottom_layers, layer_height, build_direction, infill_density), a missing AsPrintedOptions.line_width, a missing body realization, or a G-code parse error. degraded_field() is a Field whose lambda is Undef. Pre-hydration absence and an author's malformed process are indistinguishable, and nothing records why. (2) fdm_slice::read_slice_settings fills any missing or ill-typed FDMProcess field with a hard-coded default via `unwrap_or` (0.2 mm layer height, walls 3, top_bottom_layers 4, infill 0.2, Gyroid), so a mistyped process slices at a profile the author never wrote. Those defaults restate the FDMProcess .ri defaults by hand (h11). (3) A degenerate build_direction silently becomes +Z (`unit3(..).unwrap_or([0,0,1])`) in both rungs. The S15 α decoder (#8674) covers only the ElasticMaterial read (read_base_elastic). It does not cover the FDMProcess/AsPrintedOptions/G-code degrade policy or read_slice_settings.
findings.proposal: Route the FDM readers through S15's InputDecodeError → coded Failed (or coded Warning plus Undef with a recorded cause), keeping 'body not yet realized' as the only silent transient. Have read_slice_settings decode FDMProcess once, through the same decoder, rather than restating its defaults.

findings.statement: run_compute_dispatch takes the prior warm state out of the pool before the persistent-cache lookup. On a persistent HIT it then drops that state and the prior cost. It sources prior_warm_state as `self.cache.get_warm_state(..).or_else(|| self.warm_pool.checkout(..))`, and checkout REMOVES the pool entry (as the in-file tests document). It then runs the persistent lookup. The HIT arm completes with `new_warm_state: None` and cost 0.0 and returns, never restoring the prior. The Cancelled, Failed and unregistered arms do restore it, under PRD §5's 'the prior must survive' rule. So after an edit parks a warm state in the pool, a persistent HIT throws that warm-start seed away and the next real solve runs cold. The HIT arm diverges from the other arms by convention only, the same class as fk-34bddf1fcbce's mirror-by-convention cost (heuristic 7: temporal coupling on the order of checkout vs. lookup).
findings.proposal: Do the persistent lookup before taking the prior out of the pool, or donate the prior back on the HIT arm. S5 ε's single completion hook can carry this.

findings.statement: Heuristic 10 (one invariant, enforced uniformly) is broken at runtime in the transcendental builtins. Forward trig checks its argument's dimension: trig_input (helpers.rs:102-118) rejects any non-ANGLE Scalar, so sin(5mm) is Undef as the briefing scenario says. The inverse trig, exponential/log and hyperbolic arms take a different path. asin, acos, atan, atan2, log, log10, exp, sinh, cosh and tanh go through unary_f64/binary_f64 (helpers.rs:31-49), which call Value::as_f64. as_f64 (reify-ir value.rs:1638-1645) returns si_value for ANY Scalar and discards its dimension. So asin(0.5mm) silently returns an Angle of asin(0.0005), exp(5mm) returns exp(0.005), and atan2(3mm, 2s) returns a value from mixed dimensions, all with no diagnostic. The compiler documents these arguments as 'accept dimensionless Real' (math_signatures.rs:120, :406) but never checks them; that compile-time half is already #6249. Under INV-AD-1 this is an unchecked path that turns a Length into an Angle.
findings.proposal: Add one dimensionless_input(v) helper beside trig_input (Real/Int, or a DIMENSIONLESS Scalar) and route the inverse-trig, log/exp and hyperbolic arms through it, so asin(5mm) is Undef just as sin(5mm) is. Fold this into #6249's scope as its runtime half.

findings.statement: classify_swept_body maps GeometryOp::ExtrudeSymmetric onto the same SweptKind::Extrude { axis: +Z, length: distance } as a plain Extrude and drops the op's -distance/2 translation. reify-ir documents ExtrudeSymmetric as make_prism(profile, 0, 0, d) followed by translate_shape(0, 0, -d/2), so the realized body spans z in [-d/2, d/2]. The only consumer that reads SweptKind position is the structured hex/wedge mesher. It goes through swept_kind_to_sweep_params and reify-solver-elastic sweep::build_vertices, which lays layer k at z = k/layers * length, i.e. z in [0, d]. A swept mesh of a symmetric extrude would therefore be offset by d/2 from its body, so face-location boundary conditions would miss it. Today this is latent: the one production call of dispatch_volume_mesh (engine_build.rs:9470) passes swept_kind None and force_tet true, and the datum projection reads only Extrude's axis (feature_datum.rs:607). Pending #4746 is the leaf that activates the hex/wedge production edge, so that change will produce a misplaced mesh unless SweptKind carries the offset (heuristic 1: the variant's name and doc claim the two ops are 'identical for classification purposes', which is untrue once position is consumed).
findings.proposal: Give SweptKind::Extrude an explicit start offset along the axis (0 for Extrude, -d/2 for ExtrudeSymmetric) or a separate ExtrudeSymmetric variant, and make SweepParams::Extrude carry it into build_vertices before #4746 lands. Pin it with a test that compares the swept mesh's z-range with the realized body's bounding box.
